# DWG/DXF Feature-Completeness Roadmap

Last reviewed: 2026-09-01, rev 1299.

This is the only active implementation plan for DWG and DXF support in
LibreCAD/libdxfrw. It lists only incomplete or unproven work. The final
`Current Active Plan` section is authoritative; earlier review deltas are
immutable evidence and historical corrections. Completed checkpoints are
available in Git history and are intentionally absent from the active queue so
old next steps cannot direct new implementation.

The authoritative queue is the newest `Current Active Plan` section in this
file. Review and progress sections before or after it are retained as
implementation evidence, including a duplicated historical rev 1142 block;
they are not current instructions.

## Scope And Completion Rules

The low-level DWG writer has entry points for AC1015/R2000, AC1018/R2004,
AC1021/R2007, AC1024/R2010, AC1027/R2013, and AC1032/R2018. LibreCAD
currently exposes AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 through
RS2::FormatType and the console/UI save paths. AC1032 has a dedicated writer
type, but its container path
is inherited from the AC1027 writer and is not independently proven yet. DXF
output targets are the versions exposed by the public writer from AC1009/R12
through AC1032/R2018. DXF has typed paths and raw ENTITY/OBJECT fallback, but
the coverage inventory still contains unproven and fixture-needed rows. Reader
work includes legacy formats supported by libdxfrw.

A feature is complete only when its target-version layout, reference graph,
and failure behavior are proved. Successful import in LibreCAD alone is not
enough evidence. Each family and version must meet one contract:

1. A typed representation is read, edited, and emitted with
   specification-backed fields and valid references.
2. Unsupported content is preserved only for the same encoding family and only
   when every opaque reference is byte-stable.
3. When neither applies, export fails before it finalizes a partial or
   structurally misleading file. Cross-version loss must not report success.

Malformed input must fail before publication. A failed object, entity, table
record, page, or DXF record must not publish a map entry, mutate persistent
metadata, or call a public callback.

## Review Delta (rev 1087)

This pass rechecked the current execution order, writer receipts, AC1032
inheritance, and DXF inventory against the source and the local DWG
specification. `dwgRW::write()` calls the filter's `writeDwgClasses()` callback
first; the low-level writer then prepares its manifest, emits HEADER and
CLASSES, freezes class registration, and only afterward runs table, entity,
and OBJECTS callbacks. The derived writers now emit from that frozen manifest
through one lazy placeholder iterator, while the class maximum is computed
from the same snapshot. Bound DataStorage descriptors now copy identity,
ordinal, version, and phase from the executable low-level capability table.
The manifest is a real pre-publication seal, but it is still built after the
filter has mixed collection, conversion, and registration in one callback.

The frame/admission boundary is now implemented for modern DataStorage object
writes. `DwgObjectFrameReceipt` records the actual serialized object type, the
writer operation, and a one-shot filter admission token in addition to its
physical generation, output handle, bit ranges, and handle occurrences. The
writer consumes pending provenance exactly once at `beginObject()` or raw
replay, and compound checkpoints restore both pending and in-flight state. The
filter allocates one token per frozen source row, binds it before OBJECTS
emission, and rejects token, operation, or post-remap class mismatches before
the transaction commits. The filter now also carries an immutable normalized
section/version/source-order key through the plan, admission summary, frame
receipt, and physical section receipt. Section receipts cover every source row,
including duplicate revisions and wide-identity opaque rows; final validation
checks the key against the live section, record, and canonical handle identity.
This closes the modern DataStorage source-row/frame partition, but not the
predictive class manifest for ordinary typed/raw objects or the physical
DataStorage section identity.

This pass closes one sub-boundary of the ordinary class/frame gap. The
low-level writer now exposes its existing handle-to-class admission ledger to
the filter; raw class-number remapping is therefore observable before the
frame is written, and ordinary class-backed frames receive the same one-shot
class provenance check as DataStorage frames. The DataStorage binder also
records the remapped class ordinal for raw carriers. This is intentionally not
the full ordinary source-row bijection: source-row planning, one shared
admission record for typed/raw/entity dispatch, and final ordinary-ledger
validation remain queued.

Verification for rev 1084: `ninja -C build/dwg-fast
librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests -j8` completed; the focused class-remap lane
passed 3 assertions in 1 case, the DataStorage lane passed 111 assertions in
19 cases, the provenance lane passed 12 assertions in 2 cases, and the warm
`[dwg-write]` selector passed 13,161 assertions in 331 cases.

This pass also promotes the executable DataStorage capability table through a
read-only inventory API. The inventory regression proves that every advertised
binding has a non-empty identity and operation, a unique binding, and an exact
reverse lookup; shared operations remain allowed because they are intentional
many-identity-to-one-encoder mappings. This removes the hidden-table boundary,
but the filter still contains explicit metadata-family descriptor lists and
has not yet derived dispatch coverage from the inventory.

The exact supported descriptor rows now consume `descriptorForBinding()` from
that inventory rather than repeating family, class, record, version, and class
ordinal literals. Policy-only rows that intentionally have no supported
DataStorage writer remain explicit and continue to advertise no capability.
The warm writer selector passed 13,547 assertions in 332 cases after this
migration; the capability selector passed 413 assertions in 5 cases.

The follow-up version audit exercises every inventory binding at AC1014,
AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. It verifies that the
public `canWriteDwgDataStorageBinding()` result is exactly the capability
table's min/max range, including the TABLESTYLE upper bound and all shared
encoder operations. That regression passed 679 assertions in 5 cases after
the supported filter descriptors were migrated to `descriptorForBinding()`.

## Review Delta (rev 1088)

The ordinary class/frame slice was implemented and rechecked against the
current callback graph. The filter now stores a source-keyed and output-keyed
admission pair for every handle-associated typed OBJECT class and raw custom
OBJECT class admitted during `writeDwgClasses()`. Re-admission is idempotent
only for the exact source kind, source handle, output handle, and class
ordinal; divergent source/output convergence is rejected. Checkpoints restore
both indexes, so a failed object transaction cannot leave a stale class row.

`writeDwgObjectWithCompletion()` now requires the low-level writer's class
owner lookup to agree with the filter admission before encoding. For a
non-DataStorage class it binds the admitted ordinal as frame provenance; for a
DataStorage class it verifies the existing token-bearing binding instead. The
completed frame must carry the same class ordinal before the class row and
object identity can commit. Finalization additionally requires every admitted
row to be committed, identity-committed, and backed by exactly one recorded
object frame. Raw fixed structural records and handle-less class-definition
counts remain outside this ledger by design because they do not have a
source-backed ordinary frame in this callback path.

The new admission regression covers exact retry, source remap rejection,
output-handle collision rejection, and reuse of one class ordinal for multiple
instances. The focused class-remap lane passed 6 assertions in 1 case, the
new admission lane passed 8 assertions in 1 case, the DataStorage lane passed
760 assertions in 20 cases, and the provenance lane passed 12 assertions in 2
cases. The complete warm `[dwg-write]` selector passed 13,821 assertions in
333 cases. These results prove the implemented handle-associated OBJECTS
slice only; they do not close ordinary entity rows, generated class-backed
records, physical DataStorage destinations, or the independent AC1032 gate.

## Review Delta (rev 1089)

The adjacent entity audit found that ordinary source-backed entity commits and
metadata-only entity commits already converge on recorded object-frame
receipts, while typed custom entity classes are represented by the writer's
sealed class table rather than by the OBJECTS class-owner map. The filter now
adopts those actual frame class ordinals into the same source/output admission
indexes before the entity identity commits. This covers custom entity classes
that are already present in the writer class table, including metadata entity
paths, and leaves fixed entity types and generated entities with no source key
outside the source-row bijection.

The new check deliberately does not turn late class registration into a valid
operation. A typed class must still exist before the CLASSES seal; a writer
call that tries to add a new class after the seal fails at its own boundary.
The remaining P1-L.11f work is therefore predictive admission for those
typed-entity rows, explicit treatment of generated class-backed rows, and a
single pre-seal class/instance manifest rather than post-frame discovery.

The entity extension rebuilt successfully. The class-admission lane passed 8
assertions in 1 case, class-remap passed 6 assertions in 1 case, DataStorage
passed 760 assertions in 20 cases, frame provenance passed 12 assertions in 2
cases, and the full warm `[dwg-write]` selector passed 13,821 assertions in
333 cases.

AC1032 requires a separate evidence gate: `dwgWriter32` selects AC1032 and its
codec but inherits the AC1027 page/object implementation. That may be correct
where the specification says the organization is shared, but inheritance alone
does not prove header fields, section descriptors, page limits, object-map
offsets, or version-specific payload rules. The DXF inventory is also promoted
to an active workstream because raw fallback and write-error latching do not
establish typed parity or lossless raw replay for all 158 entity, 197 object,
and 524 class-table names.

### Current Code Anchors

- `dwgRW::write()` in `libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdwgr.cpp` calls
  `writeDwgClasses()` before low-level HEADER/CLASSES publication, then runs
  table, entity, and OBJECTS callbacks. Any filter admission state must
  therefore be frozen before that callback returns and cannot depend on later
  OBJECTS discovery.
- `collectDwgDataStorageCarriers()`,
  `prepareDwgDataStorageReplayPlan()`, and
  `recordDwgDataStorageObjectCommit()` in
  `librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp` select by source owner and
  carrier index, allocate a stable admission token at freeze time, bind it to
  the next object frame, and validate it against the physical receipt. The
  modern DataStorage path also uses `DwgDataStorageSourceRowKey` to bind the
  physical section and source-order record. Ordinary typed/raw class writes
  now have a transactional handle-associated admission ledger, but still do
  not have a pure predictive class-row manifest or one shared admission record
  across ordinary entities and generated class-backed records.
- `kDwgDataStorageWriterCapabilities` and
  `dwgWriter15::canWriteDwgDataStorageOperation()` are both executable
  surfaces. `getDwgDataStorageWriterCapabilities()` now exposes a stable
  read-only copy of the first table for tests and admission code. The second
  is still an exhaustive switch, and there is not yet a testable one-to-one
  inventory-to-filter-dispatch map.
- `RS_Debug::print()` remains a variadic `vfprintf` implementation, but its
  public format-bearing overloads now carry GCC/Clang format attributes. The
  raw DataStorage ordinal diagnostic uses the typed `LogStream` path; the
  related entity-id diagnostics and dynamic command message were corrected
  after the annotated build exposed their width/nonliteral format defects.
- `prepareDwgDataStorageReplayPlan()` keeps the full `UInt64` record identity.
  Records wider than the current `uint32_t` object-handle domain are entered
  in `opaqueRecordIndexes` and may only be copied through the exact
  same-version raw section. Linked decisions still require a representable
  object owner and are checked independently.
- `recordDwgDataStorageSectionCommit()` and final replay validation now require
  the receipt to cover every source-order DataStorage record. The receipt now
  carries a normalized section/version/index key for each row and records the
  subset with no object-frame link, which makes duplicate revisions and opaque
  wide replay explicit successful states rather than accidental absences of a
  decision.
- `DwgObjectFrameReceipt` in `libraries/libdxfrw/src/drw_base.h` now proves a
  physical frame, its handle occurrences, the actual serialized object type,
  the writer operation, and the optional filter admission token. `finishObject`
  and `replayRawObject()` in `dwgwriter15.cpp` decode the emitted type before
  publishing the receipt. The writer also exposes the admitted class ordinal
  for a handle, allowing the filter to bind ordinary class-backed frames and
  remapped raw DataStorage frames without duplicating the class-owner map; the
  receipt still does not carry a source metadata key.
- `registerRawObjectClass()`, `registerTypedObjectClass()`, and
  `markDwgClassInstanceEmitted()` maintain writer-local class/remap and
  handle-owner state. The filter now binds a frozen DataStorage row token to
  the corresponding OBJECTS frame and uses the same class-owner state for
  ordinary class-backed frames, but its `writeDwgClasses()` and `writeObjects()`
  paths still re-derive the broader class relationship from source handle and
  carrier kind. The remaining one-to-one source-row ledger is a filter/low-level
  API boundary, not another aggregate-count check.
- `dwgWriter32` in `libraries/libdxfrw/src/intern/dwgwriter32.h` and `.cpp`
  sets AC1032 header/codec state while inheriting the AC1027 container and
  object framing. The roadmap must require independent AC1032 conformance
  evidence before declaring the public R2018 target complete.
- `dwgRW::writeRawDwgSection()` queues a raw section through
  `addRawDwgSection()`; the current filter section receipt is matched by
  normalized name/version and source indexes, not by final section id, order,
  payload digest, encoding, or physical size.
- `dxfRW::write()` now checks writer errors and emits registered CLASSES plus
  raw sections, and `writeRawDxfGroups()` validates typed group values and
  handle remapping. The generated
  `libraries/libdxfrw/DWG_DXF_COVERAGE_INVENTORY.md` still reports broad
  `fixture-needed`/`needs-review` coverage, so these safeguards do not close
  the DXF typed/raw parity contract.

### Verified In This Slice

- `MLEADERSTYLE` now has a shared pure `validateDwgPayload(version)` used by
  its encoder and the modern DataStorage filter preflight. The filter also
  checks unsupported EED and records a bounded scratch-frame estimate in the
  frozen admission summary. This closes scalar/finite-value validation for
  one modern binding; it does not yet prove required references or every
  advertised operation.
- `TABLESTYLE` validation is now a separate legacy-only boundary. The shared
  validator preserves its AC1015..AC1021 interval and is called by both the
  encoder and filter registration path; it is not advertised as AC1027/AC1032
  DataStorage support.
- The writer now prepares a version-filtered class manifest after the filter
  admission callback and before any file section is serialized. It checks
  enabled class ordinals, non-negative counts, and pending class references;
  all R2000/R2004/R2007+ class writers reject drift before emitting CLASSES.
  The manifest is part of compound-write checkpoints. Class placeholders are
  streamed for the bounded 16-bit class-number range instead of being
  materialized in a large vector.
- The DataStorage carrier factory now canonicalizes every descriptor that
  resolves to a low-level binding. Intentionally unsupported families remain
  explicit unbound policy entries; TABLESTYLE uses the same canonical path.
- DataStorage raw carriers now validate custom class ordinals before narrowing
  `RawObjectRecord::objectType` to the DWG 16-bit class field. The focused
  regression covers negative, sub-500, over-`UINT16_MAX`, and `UINT16_MAX`
  values with 4 assertions in 1 case.
- Added format checking to `RS_Debug::print()` and fixed all mismatches found
  by the annotated CMake build in the touched DWG/DXF diagnostics. The full
  `librecad_lib` incremental target links successfully; unrelated existing
  `LC_VERSION` redefinition and missing-`override` warnings remain.
- Removed `isHandleSafe` from replay validity checks. It remains an explicit
  JavaScript-number safety annotation in the low-level record, not a DWG
  validity predicate. Added an AC1027 regression for a `UInt64` identity at
  `UINT32_MAX + 1` and verified that its section receipt marks the record as
  opaque.
- Section replay now accounts for all typed-index records, including duplicate
  or unbound source-order records. This prevents a successful save from
  silently dropping a retained record merely because no LibreCAD object frame
  was linked to it.
- A durable output-handle owner ledger now rejects reuse of an emitted custom
  object handle, including reuse under the same class identity. Compound and
  raw-replay rollbacks restore the emitted-handle ledger together with class
  counts and pending tuples.
- Final low-level class validation now also checks the physical object map:
  every handle-associated custom instance must have one committed frame, and
  every emitted class-owned handle must have one owner entry. Handle-less
  typed classes continue to use their explicit emission-count hook.
- Warm CMake evidence: the current `[dwg-write]` selector passes 13,161
  assertions in 331 cases; the DataStorage selector passes 111 assertions in
  19 cases; the focused provenance selector passes 12 assertions in 2 cases;
  and the affected CMake/Ninja test target links successfully. `git diff
  --check` passes. The exact selectors were
  `./build/dwg-fast/librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests '[dwg-write]' --reporter
  compact --abort`,
  `./build/dwg-fast/librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests '[dwg-write][datastorage]'
  --reporter compact --abort`, and
  `./build/dwg-fast/librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests
  '[dwg-write][frames][provenance]' --reporter compact --abort`. The known
  `LC_VERSION` macro redefinition and
  missing-`override` warnings remain unrelated.
- The current implementation pass closes the receipt-boundary contract: the
  writer consumes pending provenance once, restores it through compound
  rollback, validates the actual serialized type, and publishes operation plus
  token in the receipt. The filter freezes one token and one immutable source
  row key per modern DataStorage decision, binds it before OBJECTS emission,
  and validates both the committed frame and the physical section against that
  row. These are local CMake/Ninja results; they do not prove independent
  AC1032 validation or complete DXF feature parity.
- The source-row regression now covers duplicate revision selection and stale
  receipt-row rejection. Warm CMake evidence after the change is 13,161
  assertions in 331 `[dwg-write]` cases, 111 assertions in 19
  `[dwg-write][datastorage]` cases, and 12 assertions in 2
  `[dwg-write][frames][provenance]` cases. The focused target was rebuilt
  incrementally and `git diff --check` passes.

### Findings Still Open After This Slice

1. **P1: capability metadata is only partially de-duplicated.** Bound
   descriptors now overwrite their identity, ordinal, version, and phase from
   the authoritative table in `libdwgr.cpp`, so a supported carrier cannot
   publish stale values. The filter still uses repeated strings to discover
   those bindings, and intentionally unsupported policy entries still carry
   local version/class metadata. Replace bound call sites with binding IDs and
   add one executable inventory before claiming one-to-one coverage.
2. **P1: payload proof is only partial.** `MLEADERSTYLE` now shares scalar and
   finite-value validation with its encoder, but the operation switch does not
   validate required references, owner edges, complete EED conversion, or
   frame limits for the remaining typed families. The MLeader adapter also
   needs explicit required/optional reference rules rather than relying on
   later OBJECTS remapping.
3. **P1: the filter still has no predictive class admission manifest.** Its
   large `writeDwgClasses()` callback mixes metadata scans, typed conversion,
   handle reservation, class registration, and native-set publication. The
   low-level seal catches drift after this mutation, but it cannot prove that
   each source record has exactly one planned class row and one later OBJECTS
   frame.
4. **P1: ordinary class-instance validation still lacks a predictive
   admission bijection.** Modern DataStorage rows now carry a source identity
   key and are checked against one frame or one physical section receipt. The
   filter-side ledger now also covers raw custom entities and source-backed
   typed custom entity frames when their class is already in the sealed writer
   table. It still cannot prove before CLASSES that every ordinary custom
   frame, generated class-backed frame, or class-count registration has exactly
   one planned source row, that no late class can acquire a frame, or that
   every committed frame has one predictive admission row.
5. **P2: sparse custom class ordinals are bounded but can still be expensive.**
   The DWG class number is a 16-bit field, so an arbitrary smaller semantic
   maximum would change the supported wire domain. Emission now avoids the
   previous large in-memory placeholder vector, but a sparse class near
   `0xFFFF` still creates a long contiguous wire range. Add a shared output
   budget/high-ordinal regression policy rather than an invented format limit.
6. **P1: the current DataStorage contract remains OBJECTS-only.** The
   collection path emits only OBJECTS-phase DataStorage carriers; section,
   image/reactor, viewport-header, and block-representation paths are handled
   by other callbacks or opaque paths. They need an explicit section/auxiliary
   receipt contract or an early rejection rule, not an implicit reuse of the
   OBJECTS ledger.
7. **P1: fixed OBJECTS coverage is not yet audited one-to-one.** The
   capability switch and the filter dispatch contain many fixed-type families,
   but there is no generated or test-enforced relation proving that each
   advertised fixed type has one writer entry point, one matching dispatch
   gate, and one version-bound test.
8. **P2: raw entity and raw object replay have different owner obligations.**
   Raw custom entities can be routed through the OBJECTS callback and patched
   only for the writer-supported modern owner layout; legacy or owner-only
   opaque layouts are rejected when a block remap is needed. This is the right
   conservative behavior, but the rule is spread across class admission,
   replay filtering, and the low-level raw writer and needs a single matrix
   with explicit tests for model space, paper space, user blocks, and remapped
   owners.
9. **P2: parser tolerance remains broader than specification evidence.**
   Supported-opaque DataStorage segment/header variants retain bytes and may
   remain replayable without a version/revision fixture or a specification
   citation for the exact producer variant.
10. **P2: AC1027 evidence is still synthetic.** No external AC1027
   TABLESTYLE/DataStorage sample, independent-reader result, or complete
   3DSOLID/REGION/SURFACE ownership matrix has been added. Same-version raw
   replay is tested with synthetic carriers only.
11. **P2: AC1021/R2007 remains absent from the public format surface.** The
   low-level writer and parser support AC1021, but `RS2::FormatType`, dialogs,
   console defaults, and public save selection do not expose a deliberate
   R2007 target.
12. **P1: AC1032 container conformance is unproven independently.**
   `dwgWriter32` inherits the AC1027 page, section, object-map, and framing
   implementation and changes version/codec state. Add a specification-backed
   AC1032 audit and external-reader fixtures before treating R2018 as complete;
   split overrides only where the evidence shows a real layout difference.
13. **P1: physical frame provenance is partial outside DataStorage.**
   `DwgObjectFrameReceipt` now carries the actual serialized type, operation,
   and optional admission token, so a bound DataStorage row cannot silently
   produce the wrong class frame. Raw custom entities and source-backed typed
   custom entity frames now receive a post-frame class admission. Source-backed
   PLOTSETTINGS rows also stage their remapped output handle before CLASSES and
   consume that class owner only after the returned frame receipt. Ordinary
   typed/raw rows still have no immutable pre-seal source-row token, generated
   class-backed rows other than PLOTSETTINGS still need explicit ordinals, and
   the low-level class ledger cannot by itself detect two predictive rows
   converging on one ordinary frame.
14. **P2: DataStorage section receipts are logical, not physical.** The
   current receipt confirms source-order record indexes and the opaque subset,
   but not final section identity/order, encoding/encryption mode, payload
   size, or a digest of the bytes actually queued and emitted.
15. **P1: the active plan has no DXF parity execution track.** Raw fallback,
   CLASSES emission, binary chunks, and write-error propagation are present,
   but the inventory still contains fixture-needed and needs-review rows across
   typed entities, OBJECTS, custom classes, version gates, and malformed-input
   behavior. Completeness needs a classification and fixture queue, not only
   more DWG work.
16. **P2: one static-analysis format defect remains outside the touched
   diagnostics.** The annotated build still reports a nonliteral format call
   near `librecad/src/ui/lc_actionhandlerfactory.cpp:1001`; close or explicitly
   waive it before claiming a repository-wide format audit.

### Implementation-Ready Remaining Plan

Completed `TABLESTYLE` validation, frozen-manifest consumption, lazy class
placeholder emission, durable class-handle ownership, and the low-level
physical-frame audit are removed from the active queue. The remaining work is
split by invariant so
each slice can be implemented and verified without reopening completed
legacy behavior:

P0-L.0a and P0-L.0b are complete for the current AC1027 preservation surface.
The format audit, wide-identity policy, receipt-boundary provenance, and modern
DataStorage source-row/frame partition are executable and covered by the
focused CMake lane. No new typed DataStorage family should be advertised until
the physical-section gate and ordinary class admission gate below are closed.

## Review Delta (rev 1090)

The adjacent-feature audit compared the executable DataStorage capability
inventory, its version gate, the filter carrier factory, and every
`writeDwgDataStorage...` dispatch site. The low-level table has 38 unique
bindings and 38 operation tags; `dwgWriter15::canWriteDwgDataStorageOperation`
has one switch case for each operation, and the version-bound capability
regression covers AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. Promoted
filter descriptors now consume the inventory for family, class, record,
ordinal, version, phase, and presence-bit policy. This proves the declaration
and low-level availability boundary only. It does not prove that each binding
is dispatched exactly once to its intended typed writer: shared operations
(underlay and point-cloud), metadata-family loops, and explicit policy-only
rows still bypass a machine-checkable binding-to-call map.

The ordinary class/frame review also followed all entity commit paths rather
than only `writeDwgObjectWithCompletion()`. Normal source-backed entities and
metadata-only entities now adopt the actual frame class before identity commit;
raw custom entity replay and source-backed typed custom entity frames are
therefore included when their class definition was sealed before CLASSES.
At rev 1090, generated class-backed entities with no source handle, fixed
entity types, and handle-less class-count registrations remained outside the
source-keyed ledger. The generated PLOTSETTINGS case is now covered by a
separate source ordinal; fixed entity types and definition-only class counts
remain outside it. The next class slice still needs predictive rows and a
shared dispatch contract, not another post-frame lookup.

Verification for rev 1090: the warm DWG write target passed 13,821 assertions
in 333 cases; the class-admission lane passed 8 assertions in 1 case; the
class-remap lane passed 6 assertions in 1 case; the provenance lane passed 12
assertions in 2 cases; the DataStorage lane passed 760 assertions in 20 cases;
the capability/version lane passed 679 assertions in 5 cases; and
`git diff --check` passed. These are local CMake results and do not prove
independent AC1032 conformance, physical section layout, or complete DXF
parity.

## Review Delta (rev 1091)

The first predictive source-less row was implemented for the default
PLOTSETTINGS object. `DwgWriteSourceKey` now separates a real source handle
from a nonzero source ordinal, so the registry no longer needs to fabricate a
DWG handle for generated content. The class admission is created during the
pre-CLASSES callback with the writer-local PLOTSETTINGS class ordinal; the
common object transaction binds the actual output handle from the returned
frame receipt, records the frame, and rolls back both indexes on failure.

This is deliberately a narrow proof point. It covers the synthesized default
PLOTSETTINGS row and generated PLOTSETTINGS metadata entries, but it does not
yet create a general predictive descriptor for generated entity/object
families, fixed entity types, or definition-only class counts. Existing
source-backed rows continue to use the zero source-ordinal path, so their
identity and handle semantics are unchanged.

Verification for rev 1091: the incremental
`librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` target built successfully; the focused filter
PLOTSETTINGS lane passed 60 assertions in 4 cases; the class-admission lane
passed 8 assertions in 1 case; the warm `[dwg-write]` selector passed 13,821
assertions in 333 cases; and `git diff --check` passed. The recurring
`LC_VERSION` macro redefinition warning remains unrelated. No independent
AC1032, qmake6, sanitizer, external-reader, or slow-corpus gate is claimed.

## Review Delta (rev 1092)

This pass re-audited the roadmap against the current callback order and all
ordinary DWG write paths. The low-level writer's class manifest is genuinely
prepared before HEADER/CLASSES publication and rejected on later drift, but
that manifest is a snapshot of registrations, not a filter-owned plan of
source rows. `RS_FilterDXFRW::writeDwgClasses()` still performs conversion,
handle remapping, native-set population, class registration, and DataStorage
admission in one callback. `writeObjects()` then reconstructs the same
selection from repeated metadata predicates and native handle sets. The
roadmap must therefore require a filter descriptor/admission layer, rather
than describe the existing low-level manifest as a complete solution.

The ordinary audit now separates the four lifecycles that had been
conflated:

1. Source-backed class instances have a source handle, a remapped output
   handle, a class ordinal, and one physical frame. The current admission
   ledger covers many OBJECTS families and sealed custom entity classes, but
   their rows are still discovered in the class callback and rediscovered in
   later callbacks.
2. Source-less generated instances have no valid source handle. Generated
   PLOTSETTINGS now uses a nonzero source ordinal and binds its actual frame
   handle after encoding. Generated metadata entities and any future generated
   class-backed OBJECTS need the same contract; a fabricated source handle is
   forbidden.
3. Fixed DWG object types have a physical frame but no CLASSES row. They need
   a type/dispatch/frame receipt and must be excluded from class-admission
   cardinality checks, while still participating in owner and output-handle
   uniqueness checks.
4. Definition-only class counts have a class registration but no object-frame
   lifecycle. They must retain an explicit count-only contract and must not be
   forced into the frame bijection.

The capability audit also tightened the meaning of “covered.” The executable
low-level inventory has 38 bindings and 38 operation tags, and the operation
availability switch is exhaustive. The filter still has no machine-readable
mapping from each binding to its exact gate, conversion path, typed writer
call, and receipt kind. The repeated Underlay/PointCloud families and the
metadata loops make an operation-count comparison insufficient; shared
operations must be represented as deliberate aliases, not counted as missing
or duplicated writers.

The physical-container audit confirms that `dwgWriter18::finalize()` queues
standard and raw sections, sorts map and stream orders separately, creates

encoding, payload size, or a digest after layout. The AC1032 writer continues
to inherit this path from the AC1027 writer, so local readback remains
insufficient evidence for R2018 conformance.

The DXF review remains an active adjacent workstream. The public interface
has raw CLASSES and section callbacks and the writer propagates failures, but
the generated inventory still contains fixture-needed and needs-review rows.
No DWG class-ledger result should be reported as DXF parity evidence.

## Review Delta (rev 1095)

This audit followed the class admission calls from the filter's pre-CLASSES
callback through every DWG frame completion path. The implementation boundary
is narrower than the previous queue wording suggested:

- `writeDwgClasses()` now sends all source-backed typed OBJECT registrations,
  raw custom OBJECT registrations, and both PLOTSETTINGS lifecycles through
  the explicit descriptor API. Those rows have a source/output key and a
  target version before CLASSES is sealed.
- `writeDwgObjectWithCompletion()` consumes those OBJECTS descriptors and
  checks the actual frame class before committing the object transaction.
  Its generated-row path binds the output handle from the returned frame.
- The only remaining production uses of the legacy admission wrapper are the
  generic `writeEntity()` completion path and the metadata-entity completion
  path. They discover the class ordinal from the physical frame, so they are
  compatibility assertions, not predictive rows. They now pass the target
  version through the descriptor contract; they still must not create the
  impression that entity rows were admitted before CLASSES.
- Direct fixed-type entity writes do not have CLASSES rows and therefore
  cannot be folded into the class ledger. They need a separate type,
  dispatch, owner, and frame-receipt ledger. Native MLEADER is especially
  important: it can fall back to LEADER/MTEXT, so its predictive descriptor
  must be selected only after the native-versus-fallback decision is stable.
- The low-level `registerTypedEntityClass()` path registers a class definition
  but does not stage a handle-associated class instance. Entity class counts
  must therefore not be inferred from `m_dwgClassInstanceHandleOwners` or
  from the OBJECTS count validator. A future entity ledger must define its
  own count and fallback rules instead of reusing the OBJECTS API by analogy.

The next implementation slice is a prediction adapter for the smallest
deterministic custom entity family, followed by a fixed-type receipt ledger.
The adapter must identify the final writer route before class planning,
including version gates and fallback branches, and must be rollback-owned by
the existing identity checkpoint. Do not pre-admit MLEADER, surfaces, or
decomposed sidecar entities until their route selection and one-to-many output
semantics have an explicit contract.

### Rev 1095 implementation-readiness refinement

The code review now has a route inventory for `writeEntities()` rather than a
single generic "entity" bucket:

| Route | Current behavior | Ledger needed before migration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ordinary POINT/LINE/CIRCLE/ARC/TEXT and similar writers | One low-level frame; the outer `writeEntity()` completion code records the physical receipt and then learns the class number, if any. | A predicted fixed-type or custom-class route plus one-frame receipt. |
| DIMARC | `writeDimension()` selects `DRW_DimArc`, whose wire type is the fixed writer-local class 500; it is a deterministic one-frame custom-class candidate. | Source/generated descriptor, owner result, class identity, and class-instance count policy. |
| Typed sidecar reconstruction | RAY/XLINE/TRACE/3DFACE and related conversions emit a different fixed type from the original entity and mark the source entity consumed. | Conversion route identity and exactly one source-to-output receipt. |
| POLYLINE/MLINE reconstruction | A source entity can produce an anchor plus child frames, with child handles and ownership recorded during one transaction. | Compound cardinality and child receipt ledger; it cannot use the one-frame class descriptor. |
| UNDERLAY reconstruction | One source polyline is consumed and one native frame is emitted after inverse-transform validation. | Sidecar route, owner, and source-consumption receipt. |
| MLEADER | AC1024+ native text-content output may produce one custom-class frame and returns through the generic one-frame completion path; otherwise visible LEADER/MTEXT fallback can produce multiple fixed frames and sets `m_dwgEntityWriteHandled` after committing its own transaction. | Route decision before CLASSES, compound fallback cardinality, and no class admission for fallback geometry. |
| Metadata entity objects | A dedicated transaction writes one source-backed frame and validates owner/DataStorage/reference receipts, but class admission is still post-frame. | Versioned predictive descriptor after its class identity is collected before CLASSES. |

The first implementation target should be the deterministic DIMARC route, but
only as a source-backed proof point. It has one physical frame and no native
fallback. Generated DIMARC and every compound route remain separate test cases
until their source ordinal and cardinality contracts are available. The
implementation must not infer class counts from the low-level
`m_dwgClassInstanceHandleOwners` map: `registerTypedEntityClass()` installs a
class definition, whereas entity frame emission does not stage a handle-owned
OBJECTS class instance there.

The descriptor migration itself is now split into these executable sub-plans:

1. Add a filter-side route descriptor containing source key, target version,
   an optional owner expectation, writer route, class identity, expected frame
   count, and the allowed generated/source lifecycle. Keep it in the existing
   identity checkpoint so failed entity transactions restore it with handles
   and frame receipts. Do not require a final output owner in the pre-CLASSES
   class descriptor until block-record handles have a reservation pass.
2. Add a low-level class-identity query returning class name, record name,
   application name, entity/object flag, and effective class ordinal. The
   filter descriptor must retain the identity used for planning and compare it
   with the emitted frame; an ordinal-only comparison is insufficient after
   class remapping.
3. Add a DIMARC prediction adapter in `writeDwgClasses()` and a matching
   `writeEntity()` completion path. For source-backed DIMARC, reject duplicate
   source/output keys, bind class provenance before encoding, and commit
   exactly one receipt. Validate the actual owner at the entity frame receipt;
   do not claim that the owner was resolved before CLASSES. Add a generated
   ordinal only after the source-backed path is proven.
4. Add a separate fixed-frame receipt type. It must record the predicted
   fixed wire type, route, source/output identity, owner, frame generation, and
   cardinality, but must never enter CLASSES admission or class-instance
   count validation. Use this receipt first for ordinary LINE and the typed
   RAY/XLINE/TRACE/3DFACE conversions, then extend it to compound routes.
5. Make MLEADER and sidecar reconstruction choose a route before encoding and
   expose the choice to the transaction helper. A failed native attempt must
   roll back its tentative route; a fallback must commit only its child
   receipts and one source-consumption receipt. Do not admit a native class
   merely because a later fallback frame happened to use a custom ordinal.
6. Replace the two post-frame compatibility admissions only after the
   descriptor lookup is required for the deterministic routes. Retain the
   post-frame class comparison as an assertion until all one-to-many and
   generated routes have explicit contracts.

The corresponding test slices are deliberately ordered: direct registry
descriptor identity and rollback; source-backed DIMARC class prediction;
fixed LINE receipt; typed-conversion cardinality; MLEADER native/fallback
rollback; then the warm `[dwg-write]` selector. A test that only reimports the
resulting file does not prove the filter ledger, and a class-count test does
not prove fixed-frame ownership.

## Review Delta (rev 1096)

This pass checked the proposed entity migration against the actual callback
order in `dwgRW::write()`. The order is `writeHeader()`, `writeDwgClasses()`,
low-level header/CLASSES sealing, tables, `writeDwgObjects()`, `writeBlocks()`,
`writeEntities()`, and `writeObjects()`. Consequently, block-record output
handles and the active block owner do not exist when the filter plans classes.
The previous wording that required DIMARC or every ordinary route to resolve a
`BLOCK_RECORD` owner before CLASSES was not implementable with the current API.

The plan now has two independent bindings:

- The pre-CLASSES descriptor freezes source/output identity, target version,
  route, class identity, and cardinality. It may carry only a source/container
  owner expectation or `NoHandle` at this stage.
- The block phase binds the actual owner handle while
  `prepareBlockOwnedEntity()` is active. The entity frame receipt then checks
  that owner against the source/container expectation. A future reservation
  pass may make the owner predictive, but it is a separate API and is not
  silently inferred from the later frame.

The first implementation slice is therefore source-backed DIMARC class
prediction and provenance binding without pretending to solve owner
reservation. The next fixed-frame receipt slice must use the same separation:
wire type and route can be predicted before CLASSES, while owner and physical
frame generation are validated at the block/entity write boundary. Compound
and fallback routes remain excluded until their cardinality and owner receipts
are explicit.

## Review Delta (rev 1101)

The previous review found that source-backed DIMARC and 3DLINE had filter-side
class/frame receipts but did not update the low-level class instance ledger.
That left a physically emitted custom entity paired with a `CLASSES` entry
whose instance count could remain zero. `dwgWriter` now exposes a narrowly
scoped pre-freeze entity-instance admission operation. It validates the
existing class identity and version gate, reserves the output handle, stages
the `(class ordinal, handle)` owner pair, and updates the same class
definition count used by raw and typed OBJECTS. The public `dwgRW` bridge also
rejects an unrepresentable handle before mutating the ledger.

The filter invokes this operation beside the existing source-backed DIMARC
and class-562 3DLINE predictions. The operation is intentionally pre-`CLASSES`
only; it cannot make a late custom class legal, and it does not pretend to
solve routes whose physical carrier can change after the seal. In particular,
native MLEADER versus fallback geometry, UNDERLAY sidecars, and metadata
entity routes still require route-specific prediction or an atomic
pre-encoding decision. A failed entity frame remains an export failure rather
than a stale class-count publication.

The re-audit also checked adjacent custom-entity entry points. `dwgRW::writeMLeader`
is reached after the class seal, while the LibreCAD filter can speculatively
try native MLEADER and then fall back to LEADER/MTEXT children. A pre-counted
class row would therefore be stale when native encoding fails. `writeUnderlay`
registers its PDF/DGN/DWF entity class at the call site, and the
Navisworks/CAMERA/LIGHT/SECTIONOBJECT metadata helpers similarly lack a
source-row class-instance receipt. These are not folded into the DIMARC/
3DLINE fix because their carrier choice or late registration requires a
different contract.

Implementation-ready next steps from this audit are therefore: (a) inventory
each custom entity route with its class ordinal, version gate, fallback policy,
and exact output handle before CLASSES; (b) make native-versus-fallback
selection a preflight decision, or fail the export when no deterministic
choice can be made; (c) stage one class instance per predicted output handle
and consume it only after the physical frame commits; and (d) add two-instance
tests so class counts are checked for both multiplicity and rollback. The
underlay and metadata routes must also prove their BLOCK_RECORD owner before
they leave this phase.

Affected files: `libraries/libdxfrw/src/intern/dwgwriter.h`,
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdwgr.h`, `libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdwgr.cpp`, and
`librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp`.

## Review Delta (rev 1103)

This audit rechecked the rev1102 class-instance changes against the actual
`writeDwgClasses()`, `writeObjects()`, `writeEntities()`, and finalization
callbacks. The new pre-seal API correctly merges instance counts for the
source-backed DIMARC, 3DLINE, LIGHT, NAVISWORKSMODEL, CAMERA, and
SECTIONOBJECT routes. It does not yet establish a general class/frame
bijection. The following findings are now implementation gates rather than
implicit assumptions:

- `writeDwgClasses()` still combines DataStorage freezing, handle remapping,
  class registration, native handle-set creation, metadata conversion, and
  class admission. `writeObjects()` repeats several version and replay
  predicates. A record can therefore be admitted from one predicate set and
  suppressed by another before its frame is committed. The route decision must
  become one immutable descriptor shared by preflight and emission.
- The metadata adapter records source/output identity and class count, but
  passes an empty owner and zero frame estimate. Owner resolution, payload
  validation, required references, and physical frame receipt still happen
  later. A successful class count therefore does not yet prove that the
  advertised object can be emitted by the selected route.
- MLEADER class 501 remains uncounted before `CLASSES`. Native AC1024+ output
  is attempted only for text content and can fall back to LEADER/MTEXT. The
  filter also does not assign `d.hasBlockContents` to
  `e.context.hasContentsBlock`; when both content flags are set, the native
  encoder takes the text branch and silently loses block content. Native,
  fallback, and unsupported-content selection must be decided before class
  serialization, with exactly one source receipt and an explicit child
  cardinality for fallback output.
- UNDERLAY classes 523/524/525 are still registered from the physical writer
  call. Reconstructed sidecars omit inverse-clip data, replace near-zero
  scales with `1.0`, and have no pre-admission class count, generated-row
  ordinal, owner receipt, or definition-reference receipt. Source-backed and
  generated underlays need separate contracts; invalid scale, definition
  handle, clip, and finite-coordinate data must not be normalized into a
  different drawing.
- Fixed receipts cover LINE and typed-fidelity sidecars, but ordinary fixed
  entities, POLYLINE/ATTRIB/VERTEX/SEQEND compounds, MLINE, and sidecar
  one-to-many output still depend on generic post-frame discovery. The
  `m_dwgEntityWriteHandled` flag is a hidden route result and can allow a
  compound writer to bypass the ordinary completion path without a common
  source-consumption and child-ownership receipt.
- DataStorage receipts prove logical record accounting only. They do not
  identify the final physical section id/order, page list, encoded or
  encrypted representation, size, or a digest of the bytes actually handed
  to `dwgWriter21`. AC1027/AC1032 preservation cannot be called byte-stable
  until the writer reports this physical identity.
- Real ACadSharp samples for AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
  AC1032 are available under `../ACadSharp/samples`, and existing smoke tests
  exercise the version family. They are source-controlled smoke fixtures, not
  feature-specific conformance fixtures or independent-reader evidence.
  `dwgWriter32` inherits most of `dwgWriter27`, while shared code contains
  explicit AC1032 branches for HSize and related payloads; every such branch
  needs a version-difference assertion rather than an inheritance-based

## Historical Review Delta (rev 1072, superseded by rev 1075)

This follow-up rechecked the new admission summary against mutable metadata
and the writer receipt fields. The summary now validates class number, source
kind, block owner, and class-required status by re-deriving them from the
currently selected carrier at each callback boundary; it no longer relies on
stale receipt values alone. The warm CMake target was rebuilt incrementally
for the filter edit and both focused selectors were repeated afterward.

### Implemented In This Slice

- Strengthened `validateDwgDataStorageAdmissionSummary()` so current carrier
  metadata must still agree with the frozen source/output identity and receipt.
  A mutation between `writeDwgClasses()` and `writeObjects()` now fails before
  the OBJECTS callback emits.
- Removed an exception-capable map lookup from the validator; validation is a
  non-mutating, non-throwing comparison path.
- The DataStorage selector passes 96 assertions in 16 cases. The broader
  `[dwg-write]` selector passes 12,576 assertions in 319 cases. `git diff
  --check` and the fast-check shell syntax check pass. The known `LC_VERSION`
  macro redefinition warning remains unrelated.

### Findings Still Open After This Slice

1. **P1: operation identity still lacks payload validation.** The concrete
   operation switch proves that an encoder exists, but it does not validate an
   individual payload, EED conversion, required reference, or frame-size
   limit before class admission.
2. **P1: the complete class/handle manifest is still not immutable.** The
   DataStorage summary is immutable, but the wider callback still mutates
   handle maps, reservations, class counts, and native carrier sets while
   discovering content. Filter-owned remaps and known-handle sets do not yet
   have a transaction checkpoint equivalent to the writer's class checkpoint.
3. **P1: fixed-type coverage needs a complete source audit.** The six
   DataStorage fixed types are centralized, but the broader fixed OBJECTS
   inventory still needs a one-to-one registration/write audit and explicit
   compile-time or test-time coverage.
4. **P1: non-OBJECTS DataStorage remains explicitly unsupported.** Section,
   image/reactor, viewport-header, and block-representation paths need their
   own carrier/receipt contract or an early rejection rule.
5. **P2: parser tolerance remains broader than the specification proof.**
   Accepted producer variants still need a version/revision matrix and
   fixture-backed replay authorization.

### Next Slice

Implement P1-L.8c for one complete typed family first, using a pure validator
that checks payload bounds, EED representability, required references, and
the operation's version interval before class admission. Use TABLESTYLE as the
initial bounded family because its encoder already exposes explicit structural
limits and an AC1015..AC1021 interval. Then generalize the validator contract
to the remaining bindings. Keep the full filter-level planning checkpoint,
fixed-type audit, non-OBJECTS policy, parser oracle work, external AC1027
fixtures, and AC1021 public format exposure in their existing queues.

   mutates handle maps, reservations, class counts, and native carrier sets
   while discovering content. The late TABLESTYLE path is closed and failures
   now abort before section serialization, but a rejected plan can still
   mutate temporary writer/filter state until the writer is discarded.
4. **P1: non-OBJECTS DataStorage remains explicitly unsupported.** Section,
   image/reactor, viewport-header, and block-representation paths need their
   own carrier/receipt contract or an early rejection rule.

### Next Slice

Implement the first half of P1-L.11b without widening feature scope: create a
read-only class/handle admission summary from the already-frozen DataStorage
plan, validate that every selected custom carrier has one pre-`CLASSES`
registration and one planned OBJECTS frame, and make the final callback assert
that summary before emitting. Add direct rollback tests for class counts,
raw-class instance handles, remaps, and known-handle sets. Then continue the
fixed-type audit and per-family payload validators. Keep parser tolerance,
non-OBJECTS phase policy, external AC1027 fixtures, and AC1021 public-format
exposure in their existing queues.

## Fast Implementation Contract

Keep build/dwg-fast warm. Before each build run:

    git diff --check && bash -n scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh

After a behavior edit run one exact source-scoped regression:

    scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test-file path/to/test.cpp \
      --test exact-test-name --abort --quiet

Use --changed --compile-only for a production-only edit and
--test-only --no-discover only for an unchanged repeat. Slow fixtures, corpora,
external readers, sanitizers, full qmake6, and GUI checks are milestone
evidence rather than per-edit work. Do not run CMake and qmake6 builds
concurrently.

The format-local CMake targets are selective: librecad_dwg_fast_tests and
librecad_dxf_fast_tests compile only their registered source slices plus the
small shared release-label definition. A header or shared-library boundary
change outside those slices needs one normal target build before the fast lane
is trusted. `--allow-slow` changes selector policy; it does not turn a micro
lane into the complete test target.

## Historical Review Delta (rev 1068, superseded by rev 1069)

This pass re-audited the rev1067 changes against the actual call order in
`libdwgr::write`, the current `RS_FilterDXFRW` class and entity dispatch, every
DataStorage carrier/receipt, the `dwgWriter15` writer gates, and the current
DataStorage parser tests. It also repeated the two narrow CMake checks without
building. The capability binding and DataStorage preflight slices are now
implemented, but their scope is narrower than the old queue wording implied.
The active plan below describes the remaining work only.

### Closed Since rev1067

- `DwgDataStorageWriterBinding` is now carried from the descriptor through the
  typed/raw carrier, decision, and commit receipt. The filter resolves it from
  one low-level capability inventory instead of inferring it from a family
  string at commit time.
- `dwgRW::canWriteDwgDataStorageBinding()` now rejects unknown bindings,
  unsupported phases, presence-bit-incompatible writers, and version ranges
  that do not include the active target.
- The DataStorage preflight is a const validation pass over the planned
  modern records. It checks section and record identity, same-version raw
  bytes, replay diagnostics, owner handles, remap/duplicate maps, selected
  carrier fields, and the active writer capability before the filter freezes
  the plan.
- The preflight is invoked before the low-level writer serializes its HEADER
  and CLASSES sections. `libdwgr::write` still calls the filter's
  `writeDwgClasses()` callback first, then calls `writeFileHeaderStub()`,
  `writeDwgHeader()`, and the writer's `writeDwgClasses()` method.
- The focused no-build CMake lane
  `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test-only --test
  '[dwg-write][datastorage]' --build-target
  librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests --trust-selector --quiet --abort` passes 88
  assertions in 15 cases. The broader no-build
  `[dwg-write]` lane passes 12,555 assertions in 317 cases. `git diff --check`
  and the fast-check shell syntax check also pass.

### Findings That Supersede rev1067

1. **P1: the capability inventory is executable only at the boundary.** The
   binding table has identity, phase, version, class/fixed-type, and
   presence-bit fields, but `canWriteDwgDataStorageBinding()` does not invoke
   the concrete encoder or its payload/reference validator. Several fixed
   object types are repeated as numeric literals in `libdwgr.cpp` and
   `dwgWriter15.cpp`; `AcDbPlaceholder` has no shared fixed-type constant.
   This permits descriptor/writer drift and violates the no-duplicated-wire-
   constant invariant.
2. **P1: the preflight is DataStorage-complete, not DWG-write-complete.**
   `validateDwgDataStoragePreflight()` is read-only, but
   `writeDwgClasses()` calls the mutating `prepareDwgEntityHandleMap()` and
   then performs many class registrations. It does not validate every typed
   payload, EED conversion, required reference, body limit, block-owner
   edge, or final frame before class admission. A TableStyle registration is
   still reachable in the later entity-writing path, so class discovery is
   not yet closed before CLASSES publication.
3. **P1: phase handling is still OBJECTS-only in practice.** The enum and
   receipt fields can name a section phase, but all current DataStorage
   carriers are OBJECTS-phase and the carrier-availability gate rejects every
   other phase. Image-definition/reactor, viewport-header, block-representation,
   and section-side paths therefore need explicit rejection or an independent
   section carrier/receipt; they must not inherit the OBJECTS contract.
4. **P2: DataStorage ledger closure is local, not global.** The DataStorage
   receipt state machine now rejects stale, failed, repeated, wrong-carrier,
   and wrong-frame commits. The legacy committed-kind map remains only as a
   compatibility index. The broader owner/reference receipt system still
   needs one authoritative manifest and first-divergent-field diagnostics so
   non-DataStorage objects cannot publish inconsistent edges.
5. **P2: parser tolerance remains broader than the specification proof.**
   Segment signature, segment-index, embedded-size, and alignment anomalies
   are retained as `SupportedOpaque` and leave `replayAllowed` true. This may
   be correct for known producer variants, but the repository has no
   version/revision matrix proving each case for AC1027. Raw retention is
   useful, but replay must remain disabled until a fixture or specification
   rule justifies the variant.
6. **P2: AC1027 evidence is synthetic and incomplete.** Current tests prove
   generated modeler/surface DataStorage linkage, blob retention, version
   rejection, and same-version raw replay. They do not prove a real external
   TABLESTYLE class/instance, an external AC1027 DataStorage section, or
   independent-reader acceptance of the emitted files. ACIS ownership and
   remap coverage is also not a complete three-family matrix.
7. **P2: the public AC1021/R2007 format gap remains.** `DRW::AC1021` and the
   low-level writer exist, but there is no `RS2::FormatDWG2007`; the file
   dialog, console conversion defaults, and public save selection cannot name
   or target R2007 explicitly.
8. **P2: parity reports are still inventory, not closure.** The generated
   status remains 51 DWG custom/unlisted rows, 82 DWG fixed-type rows at
   equal-or-needs-fixture, and 47/49 DXF parity-gap rows at
   equal-or-needs-fixture/needs-review. `accepted-exception` and
   `preserve-shell` rows still require fixture-owned dispositions.

### Implementation-Ready Remaining Subplans

#### P1-L.8b: make the capability source authoritative

1. Replace duplicated fixed-type literals with named constants owned by the

2. Extend each capability record with a concrete operation identity and a

   `canWriteDwgDataStorageBinding()` must answer whether the active writer can

3. Add an audit test that every DataStorage-capable registration/write pair
   has exactly one binding and that every binding has a registration path,

4. Exercise all lower and upper boundaries, especially AC1014/AC1015,
   AC1017/AC1018, AC1020/AC1021, AC1024/AC1027, AC1027/AC1032, the

#### P1-L.11b: close the class manifest before CLASSES

1. Split handle discovery from handle-map mutation. Build a temporary,

2. Move the remaining class selection and typed conversion decisions into

3. Add pure validators for common-object state, EED representability,

4. Add direct tests that malformed typed state fails before class mutation,

#### P1-L.9b: make non-OBJECTS DataStorage explicit

1. Inventory image definitions/reactors, viewport entity headers, section

2. Until a section carrier and receipt are implemented, reject an unaccounted

3. If section replay is implemented, define its section identity, record set,

2. Unify owner/reference receipts with the immutable manifest. Every required

## Historical Review Delta (rev 1066, superseded by rev 1068)

This implementation pass closed the DataStorage policy and parser issues found
in rev1065, then rechecked the affected code paths with warm incremental
builds. The low-level sidecar writers now reject modern presence-bit claims
that have no filter-side ledger carrier. Modern commit APIs require a frozen,
valid, current-generation plan, and terminal failed receipts cannot be retried
within that generation. The parser retains tolerant producer-variant
diagnostics for bounded section inspection, but exposes `replayAllowed=false`
for structural diagnostics and the filter refuses orphan DataStorage records
whose owners will not be emitted.

### Confirmed Implemented

- `writeImageDef`, `writeImageDefinitionReactor`, viewport entity-header
  emission, and the compound IMAGE path reject unaccounted modern
  `has_ds_data` requests before handle or body mutation.
- DataStorage class, object, and section receipts enforce the frozen plan,
  selected carrier, generation, source kind, frame identity, exact section
  record set, and one-way terminal failure semantics.
- DataStorage schema-only sections correctly accept optional `-1` data-index
  references. Valid bounded schema fixtures remain replayable; unsupported
  producer signature, index, header-size, and alignment variants remain
  inspectable without being conflated with top-level structural corruption.
- The descriptor phase is copied into typed carriers and receipts instead of
  being discarded by carrier construction. Current supported carriers remain
  OBJECTS-phase and are still checked against that phase at commit time.
- The focused CMake lane
  `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test '[datastorage]'` passes 272 assertions in
  36 test cases. This includes the new sidecar, receipt-state, schema, and
  orphan-replay regressions. No qmake6, sanitizer, complete-suite, or external
  reader evidence is claimed by this delta.

### Findings Still Open

1. **P1: capability descriptors are only partly executable.** Phase plumbing
   is now live, but generic family registration still needs exact class,
   version, payload, reference, and writer bindings before it can authorize
   typed DataStorage emission.
2. **P1: pre-CLASSES validation is incomplete.** EED, reference targets, body
   limits, and some version-specific failures can still be discovered by a
   writer callback after class admission.
3. **P1: section-phase support is intentionally absent.** Sidecar APIs reject
   modern DataStorage until a phase-specific carrier and frame receipt can be
   implemented without partial output.
4. **P2: strictness policy needs specification closure.** The parser now has an
   explicit replay boundary, but top-level version/revision semantics and all
   accepted producer variants still need oracle-backed classification.
5. **P2: valid AC1027 evidence remains incomplete.** Parsed DataStorage is now
   covered, but a real R24 TABLESTYLE object, generated ACIS ownership/remap
   cases, and external-reader validation remain pending.
6. **P2: parity inventory is not yet owned work.** The 51 DWG custom/unlisted
   rows and 47/49 DXF parity-gap rows still need fixture-level dispositions.

### Next Implementation Order

1. Finish L.8 by making descriptor intervals and capability records executable
   against actual `dwgWriter15` gates, including negative version-boundary
   tests.
2. Finish L.11 by moving typed conversion, EED, reference, and body validation
   into a pure pre-CLASSES preflight that freezes one decision per source
   handle.
3. Close L.12 with specification-backed top-level DataStorage version and
   revision rules, while preserving the explicit tolerant-inspection versus
   replayable-output distinction.
4. Add M.6 AC1027 fixtures and O.1 parity dispositions, then run N.7 milestone
   evidence through qmake6, sanitizers, complete suites, and available
   `dwgread`/ODA validators.

## Historical Review Delta (rev 1067, superseded by rev 1068)

This pass reviewed the rev1066 implementation against the current filter
dispatch, every DataStorage-related `dwgWriter15` entry point, the metadata
carrier inventory, and the incremental test lanes. It also rechecked the
boundary between a parsed DataStorage record and a writer that can actually
emit the corresponding object. The transaction work remains sound, but the
capability table is still a declarative inventory rather than an executable
writer contract. The next implementation slice must close that gap before
more typed families are enabled.

### Evidence Confirmed In This Pass

- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test '[datastorage]' --build-target
  librecad_datastorage_tests --abort --quiet --jobs 8` passed 272 assertions in
  36 test cases after an incremental link-only build.
- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test '[dwg-write]' --build-target
  librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests --abort --quiet --jobs 8` passed 12,535
  assertions in 316 test cases with no rebuild required.
- `git diff --check` and `bash -n scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh` passed.
- The current writer gates were rechecked: DBCOLOR starts at AC1018;
  DIMASSOC, EVALUATIONGRAPH, and SECTION start at AC1021; TABLESTYLE is
  limited to AC1015 through AC1021; and several classes deliberately reject
  modern DataStorage presence bits. Those gates are not yet generated from,
  or mechanically checked against, the filter descriptor records.
- The typed carrier list covers many metadata arrays, but it does not cover
  every metadata record that can report `hasDsData`. In particular,
  IMAGEDEF and IMAGEDEF_REACTOR are retained as metadata but their direct
  low-level writers reject modern DataStorage; model entities such as CAMERA,
  LIGHT, and NAVISWORKSMODEL use separate paths and do not currently expose a
  typed DataStorage carrier. This is an intentional boundary only when the
  planner rejects or selects a same-version raw carrier; it is not evidence of
  complete phase coverage.
- `writeDwgMetadataEntityWithCompletion` now records a typed receipt when a
  matching decision exists, while `writeDwgObjectWithCompletion` records the
  general OBJECTS path. The metadata-entity hook currently has no effective
  decisions for CAMERA, LIGHT, or NAVISWORKSMODEL because their records do not
  carry DataStorage markers. It is therefore a boundary check for future
  carriers, not a claim that those separate paths are fully replayable.
- DataStorage parsing is bounded and replay-invalidating for structural
  diagnostics, while selected producer variations remain inspectable. The
  top-level signature, header size, file size, segment-index offset, and
  referenced index numbers are checked. The specification status of the
  top-level version/revision pair, segment alignment variants, and all
  tolerated segment-header variants is still not closed by an oracle-backed
  test matrix.

### Findings Still Open

1. **P1: typed capabilities lack an executable writer binding.** A descriptor
   currently carries family/class/record strings, class number, version range,
   phase, and a boolean. It does not identify the concrete registration
   method, object writer, fixed-type encoder, source conversion function, or
   payload/reference validator that makes the claim true. A typo or stale
   descriptor can therefore pass collection and fail later in CLASSES or
   OBJECTS.
2. **P1: pre-CLASSES validation is not pure.** The interface callback
   `RS_FilterDXFRW::writeDwgClasses()` is invoked before `dwgRW` serializes the
   HEADER and CLASSES sections, but it currently mixes conversions, reference
   checks, raw/native arbitration, and class admission. Later OBJECTS,
   block/entity, and finalization callbacks can still discover payload, EED,
   reference, and frame failures after those sections have been emitted. A
   frozen decision must be validated before the first serialized section and
   then consumed without discovering new policy in later callbacks.
3. **P1: typed and raw alternatives are not uniformly phase-aware.** Current
   carriers are OBJECTS-phase. IMAGEDEF/IMAGEDEF_REACTOR, viewport headers,
   modeler payloads, and other side paths either use a different writer phase
   or reject the modern bit. The plan must represent these as explicit
   unsupported bindings or add a phase-specific receipt; silently treating
   them as ordinary OBJECTS carriers would make the presence bit and section
   ownership diverge.
4. **P2: modern low-level writers do not share one capability source.** The
   same version rules are distributed across individual `dwgWriter15` methods,
   class registration helpers, and filter conditionals. This permits drift,
   especially at AC1015/AC1018/AC1021/AC1024/AC1027 boundaries. The writer
   gate and filter plan need one testable matrix, even if the actual encoding
   remains in the existing methods.
5. **P2: DataStorage parser policy is only partially oracle-backed.** The
   parser distinguishes inspection from replay, but does not yet prove which
   version/revision values, alignment rules, empty segments, duplicate
   records, and producer signatures are valid for AC1027. A tolerant parse must
   never accidentally authorize replay merely because all byte ranges fit.
6. **P2: AC1027 end-to-end evidence remains missing.** No valid external
   TABLESTYLE fixture with its exact target-version behavior, real DataStorage
   blob fixture, ACIS ownership/remap fixture, qmake6 test execution,
   sanitizer run, complete filter suite, or strict external-reader result is
   recorded by this revision.
7. **P2: parity inventory rows remain unowned.** The current generated status
   still contains 51 DWG custom/unlisted rows and 47/49 DXF parity-gap rows at
   equal-or-needs-fixture or needs-review status. They need explicit fixture,
   typed support, opaque-preservation, or deliberate-out-of-scope dispositions.

### Implementation-Ready Sub-Plans

#### L.8a: bind descriptors to concrete writer capabilities

1. Define a small closed binding identifier for each supported typed family.
   The identifier must distinguish custom-class registration plus OBJECTS
   emission from fixed-type emission and must have an explicit unsupported
   value.
2. Store the binding in the descriptor, carrier, decision, and commit receipt.
   Do not infer it later from a family string. Unknown or default bindings
   cannot produce `WriterCapability::Typed`.
3. Implement one low-level capability table that records the binding,
   registration requirement, class identity or fixed type, phase, minimum and
   maximum version, and whether the encoder accepts a modern DataStorage bit.
   Keep the table adjacent to the writer registration/dispatch declarations so
   adding a writer without adding a capability record is visible at compile or
   test time.
4. Make the filter descriptor factory resolve only through that table. Reject
   class-name, record-name, class-number, phase, and version mismatches before
   the carrier reaches the replay planner. Preserve raw fallback only when its
   own identity, version, and payload checks pass.
5. Add boundary tests for every nontrivial gate: AC1014/AC1015,
   AC1017/AC1018, AC1020/AC1021, AC1024/AC1027, and AC1027/AC1032. Include a
   negative test proving a descriptor with a known family but an unbound writer
   cannot authorize typed replay.

#### L.11a: pure pre-CLASSES replay preflight

1. Split planning into a side-effect-free `validate...` phase and a later
   freeze phase. The validation must inspect all records, selected carriers,
   raw section identity, raw payload availability, version family, class
   registration need, owner/reference targets, EED conversion, and body-size
   limits before header/CLASSES publication.
2. Make the preflight output immutable decisions keyed by source handle and
   storage identity. The interface `writeDwgClasses()` callback may register
   exactly those decisions before low-level CLASSES serialization; it must not
   choose a new carrier, convert a new object, or widen a version range.
3. Give each typed writer a preflight validator that runs without mutating
   handles or buffers. The existing writer call remains the final encoder and
   must assert that its binding and version agree with the preflight token.
4. Add a failure-injection test for every post-CLASSES failure currently
   reachable. The expected result is no successful save, no advertised
   presence bit without a committed receipt, and no retry that changes the
   selected carrier within the same generation.

#### L.12a: close DataStorage strictness policy

1. Use the local DWG specification material and known reader implementations
   to classify each header/version/revision/alignment rule as required,
   tolerated-and-replayable, inspectable-only, or fatal.
2. Keep `structurallyValid` and `replayAllowed` independent. A bounded
   producer variation may remain readable and replayable only with a fixture
   proving that its raw section can be copied without changing references.
3. Add malformed and near-valid fixtures for short headers, signature and
   revision variants, segment-index truncation, duplicate handles, invalid
   blob page metadata, zero-length payloads, and section-size mismatches.
   Check both diagnostics and whether a writer is allowed to replay the raw
   section.

#### M.6/O.1/N.7: evidence and parity closure

1. Add valid AC1027 fixtures for TABLESTYLE, DataStorage blobs, and ACIS
   ownership/remapping. Verify output with at least one independent reader or
   validator when available.
2. Turn each parity inventory row into a disposition with a source fixture,
   target version, expected behavior, and test owner. Do not count metadata
   exposure alone as feature completion.
3. Run CMake focused lanes for edits, then serial qmake6, ASan/UBSan, complete
   DWG/DXF suites, and external-reader checks. Record compiler, generator,
   target, selector, and result in the roadmap. Keep slow lanes out of the
   per-edit loop as specified by the fast implementation contract.

### Revised Next Order
