qmake6, full-suite, external-reader, or complete AC1032 evidence.

### Remaining boundary after rev1115

The next entity-ledger refinement is not to enable more block routes blindly.
Replace the implicit, mutable `m_dwgEntityWriteHandled` escape hatch with an
explicit result from entity production: `SingleFrame` (common post-commit),
`SelfCommittedCompound` (the producer commits all planned/generated frames),
or `Failed`. First migrate the MLEADER fallback to that result and prove it
cannot accidentally bypass the common receipt path. Then design separate
compound descriptors for mesh/polyface and MLINE: each must specify its source
anchor, required sibling set, exact frame count/types, generated-handle policy,
owner-list effects, and transaction rollback. Only after those descriptors and
their model-space tests exist may the block prepass be widened. Generated
sidecars remain deferred because they lack a pre-`CLASSES` source identity and
class-instance ordinal.

## Review Delta (rev 1116)

The MLEADER fallback no longer signals its special ownership through the
mutable filter-wide `m_dwgEntityWriteHandled` flag. `writeEntity()` now owns a
local `DwgEntityProductionResult`: normal producers, including native MLEADER,
return `SingleFrame` and therefore use the shared frame receipt/identity
commit; a fallback that has committed its complete nested transaction returns
`SelfCommittedCompound`; an invalid or rolled-back producer returns `Failed`.
The caller rejects a failed result through the same entity rollback path and
checks that a self-committed result neither inherited a prior failure nor
claimed success without producing a frame. No producer can leave a stale flag
that changes the handling of the next entity.

The distinction matters because the native and fallback MLEADER paths have
different ownership contracts. Native MLEADER produces one planned custom
frame; its nested transaction protects reference receipts but the common
post-processing remains responsible for the planned frame receipt and source
identity. Fallback MLEADER emits a source-anchor first child plus generated
children and commits all their receipts and identities inside one nested
transaction, so repeating generic single-frame post-processing would be
incorrect. The result type encodes that fact at the call boundary.

Incremental CMake rebuilt `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests`. Existing focused
regressions passed without behavior changes: fallback MLEADER, 35 assertions
in three cases (including mid-compound failure and retry); native MLEADER in a
block, 38 assertions in two cases; and the block one-frame typed/UNDERLAY
route, 48 assertions. `git diff --check` passed. The unrelated duplicate
`LC_VERSION` macro warning remains. No new compound descriptor, sanitizer,
qmake6, full-suite, external-reader, or AC1032 release claim is made.

### Compound descriptor entry criteria

Before migrating mesh/polyface or MLINE, add a compact descriptor whose
validation happens before the first child write. It must name the exact source
anchor, valid sibling membership and ordering, expected fixed/custom frame
types and child count, source versus generated handle allocation, owner-list
effects, and rollback checkpoint. The producer may return
`SelfCommittedCompound` only after that descriptor has verified every emitted
receipt and committed its entire transaction. A malformed or incomplete group
must return `Failed` with no consumed set entry, no source identity commit, and
no open block content. Start in model space with one valid round trip and one
late-child failure per family; widen into blocks only after its descriptor
proves the active-block owner list.

## Review Delta (rev 1117)

The first descriptor-backed sidecar route is now MLINE, but the code audit
changes the terminology used for the next item: MLINE is a **source compound**
(several editable fallback polylines) that produces one native MLINE frame. It
is not a DWG output compound like POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND. The descriptor runs
before any write and requires exactly `N` sidecars with contiguous element
indices, one and only one anchor at index zero, matching style, scale,
justification, and open/closed state, finite and bounded baseline/miter data,
and fallback geometry that exactly matches every stored offset. Edited,
malformed, or incomplete groups therefore retain their visible LWPOLYLINE
fallbacks without reserving a frame or committing a source identity.

The valid route writes its one MLINE inside a nested DWG transaction. It records
the actual frame, commits only the anchor source identity, rolls the consumed
sibling identities back, and consumes the sidecars only after that transaction
commits. A nonzero MLINESTYLE source handle is resolved through the already
planned/remapped OBJECT namespace before frame emission; the committed MLINE
also records a required hard-pointer receipt to the final MLINESTYLE handle.
This closes the previous source-handle leak when a preserved style is remapped
for a fixed-structural collision. The MLINESTYLE object is still emitted in the
later OBJECTS callback, so this resolver/receipt boundary rather than callback
order is the required correctness proof.

The focused AC1027 filter fixture now creates an MLINE with a fixed-handle
MLINESTYLE, imports its two sidecars, and proves the native export has one
MLINE, no fallback polyline, one MLINESTYLE, and an exact entity-to-style handle
link. It separately moves a sidecar and removes a sidecar, proving both cases
write the original visible polylines rather than an invented native MLINE. The
selector passes 36 assertions after incremental CMake rebuild; `git diff
--check` passes. The earlier MLEADER fallback, native-block MLEADER, and
block one-frame routes remain focused regression lanes. The known duplicate
`LC_VERSION` macro warning is unrelated. This is not sanitizer, qmake6,
full-suite, external-reader, user-BLOCK MLINE, or release evidence.

### Remaining output-compound boundary

The low-level audit shows why mesh/polyface cannot reuse the MLINE contract.
`dwgRW::writePolyline()` reserves a parent POLYLINE handle, every VERTEX handle,
and a generated SEQEND, then writes every frame within its own checkpoint. Its
public success result publishes only the parent handle and parent frame;
`getLastSuccessfulEntityHandle()` and `getLastDwgObjectFrame()` deliberately do
not expose the child frame receipts. The current mesh/polyface reconstruction
therefore records only a parent occurrence and source-anchor identity, while
its generated child frames have no filter receipt outside a later user-BLOCK
result. That is insufficient for a model-space compound ledger and must be
fixed before this route is widened or described as complete.

1. Add a low-level `DwgCompoundEntityWriteReceipt` returned only after a
   successful `writePolyline()` transaction. It must contain ordered parent,
   VERTEX, and SEQEND entries with output handle, frame receipt, fixed wire
   type/subtype, and generated/source role. Capture every frame immediately
   after it encodes; reject zero or duplicate handles and a malformed frame
   order. Do not require numeric handle contiguity: preserved callers may
   supply valid sparse handles.
   Rollback must clear the last compound receipt together with its byte and
   mutation checkpoint. Keep the existing parent-only compatibility getters
   unchanged for ordinary callers.
2. Build immutable `MeshSidecarDescriptor` and `PolyfaceSidecarDescriptor`
   objects before the first write. They must validate the exact fallback sibling
   set, source anchor, row/column or face ordering, source geometry, face index
   ranges, parent flags, expected vertex count, and the fixed generated SEQEND
   cardinality. They also state the source identity attached to the parent and
   the generated-child policy; no loop may write while validation is still
   discovering the group.
3. Rework each reconstruction path to use one outer filter identity checkpoint
   plus the low-level compound receipt. Record every parent/child frame,
   commit the anchor identity only after all receipts validate, register every
   generated child with its parent/owner contract, and roll back the entire
   receipt, source group, and consumed state on a receipt or reference failure.
   Do not use `DwgEntityProductionResult` for these prepasses: it protects
   dispatch from `writeEntity()`, whereas a source-sidecar prepass owns a group
   before ordinary dispatch. Keep the two concepts explicit.
4. Add model-space tests for mesh and polyface valid round trips, malformed
   sidecar groups, an injected failure after a child frame, and same-filter
   retry. Assert the emitted object map contains parent, every VERTEX, and
   SEQEND exactly once, all child owners target the parent, no unconsumed
   fallback survives a valid reconstruction, and no generated-child identity
   survives a failed reconstruction. Then add a user-BLOCK case using the
   published BLOCK_RECORD owned-entity list as the owner-list oracle; only then
   allow these descriptor routes in `writeBlocks()`.
5. After POLYLINE is green, audit INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND against the same public
   compound receipt API. MLEADER fallback already self-commits a deliberately
   different sequence and should be migrated only if it can provide the same
   complete receipt contract without weakening its existing rollback test.

# Current Implementation Queue

3. **P1-L.11h.c/f: finish mesh/polyface evidence, then admit user BLOCKs.**

## Review Delta (rev 1126): current-tree audit after the checked-access slice

This review was performed against the files currently in the working tree,
not against the older status text above. The relevant implementation surfaces
are `librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp`,
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdxfrw.cpp`,
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp`,
`CMakeLists.txt`, and the focused filter tests. The worktree contains other
unrelated changes; this revision records only the DWG/DXF plan consequences.
It supersedes the historical review deltas below and is the implementation
authority until the next active-plan revision.

### What is implemented now

1. The filter has a local `XDataReadResult` boundary with checked string,
   integer, real, coordinate, binary, marker, and hexadecimal access. The
   generic EED parser, DIMSTYLE EED parser, INSERT/ATTRIB sidecar decoder,
   underlay sidecar parser, typed-conversion sidecar parser, OCS helpers, and
   elliptic-polyline marker reader no longer intentionally read an inactive
   `DRW_Variant` union member. `addHeader()` also rejects null pointers and
   non-finite coordinate/real values before publishing variables.
2. `extractEntityExtData()` now stages one group at a time. A bad recognized
   value or an unbalanced `1002` structure drops that group and keeps valid
   groups before and after it. The direct parser selector currently passes 57
   assertions in four cases. This is atomic group handling, not complete
   lossless support for every possible XDATA code.
3. `dxfRW::writeExtData()` rejects null variants, wrong storage types, null
   payload pointers, non-finite coordinates/reals, invalid textual `1004`
   hex, and out-of-range integer values. Binary `1004` output is bounded and
   split into 127-byte hexadecimal chunks. A malformed-binary writer selector
   passes three assertions in two cases.
4. Most ordinary DXF entity/table writers now propagate an EED failure. The
   DWG writer already validates entity EED before allocating its object frame,
   and staged DWG export removes the destination when filter-side validation
   fails.
5. Immutable mesh/polyface descriptors and the model-space compound receipt
   transaction are implemented. The existing filter transaction coverage
   proves retry and rollback for model-space compounds. Low-level user-block
   ownership is proven for ordinary POLYLINE and INSERT/ATTRIB sequences, and
   filter-level one-frame sidecars are proven in user blocks for the currently
   covered versions. Neither result proves filter-generated mesh/polyface
   admission to user blocks.
6. The incremental CMake graph is now explicit: filter safety tests belong to
   `librecad_dxf_fast_tests` or their per-source `librecad_*_tests` target,
   while `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` contains the large
   `dwg_write_smoke_tests.cpp` source. The previous verification instructions
   that used the writer-smoke target for every checked-access edit were
   inaccurate and are replaced below.

### Findings that change the remaining plan

#### P1-L.11e.d: EED write propagation is only partially complete

The strict EED encoder is stronger than the caller contract. There are still
31 direct statements of the form `writeExtData(ent->extData);` in
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdxfrw.cpp`. They are concentrated in Wipeout,
PointCloud/Navisworks/Surface/Modeler entity writers and the long-tail object
writers such as Layout, Sun, Scale, GeoData, SpatialFilter, SortEntsTable,
MLeaderStyle, Material, Background, SunStudy, MotionPath, CurvePath,
PointPath, ObjectPtr, PartialViewingIndex, RenderSettings, Section, and
DbColor. Several of those functions return `true` without checking either the
EED result or the writer error latch. Top-level `dxfRW::write()` may later
observe the latch, but a direct writer caller can receive a false success and
the record may already contain a partial EED.

The same boundary has two adjacent gaps:

1. `writeAppData()` validates marker nesting and storage kinds but still needs
   an explicit `std::isfinite()` check before writing DOUBLE values.
2. `writeDimstyle()` writes `ent->vars` through a raw type switch. A null
   string payload, a non-finite double, or an unsupported variant can be
   skipped or emitted after earlier DIMSTYLE bytes have been written. Its
   dynamic variables need the same exact type/code contract as the filter's
   checked DIMSTYLE reader.

The implementation slice is therefore:

1. Add a no-output EED preflight for shared-pointer entity data and raw-pointer
   table data. It must validate the complete vector before the containing
   writer emits its record prefix. The preflight must share the exact rules
   with the encoder, including binary size, textual hex, integer width, and
   finite numeric checks, so validation cannot drift from emission.
2. Convert all 31 remaining call sites to an explicit result path. A writer
   returning `bool` returns false on EED failure and on `writer->hasWriteError()`;
   pointer-returning writers return their null failure value. Preserve existing
   result accumulators where they already model write failures.
3. Validate DIMSTYLE variable codes against a static descriptor table before
   the first `DIMSTYLE` group is written. Preserve absent optional variables,
   reject a present variable with the wrong storage or null string, and reject
   non-finite real values. Do not reinterpret a union member as a fallback.
4. Keep top-level staged-file cleanup as the publication boundary. Add direct
   writer tests because a top-level failure latch alone does not prove the
   low-level function's return contract or prevent a caller from continuing.

The proof condition is not merely “the final file is absent.” For a malformed
EED after a valid ordinary field, the test must show: the writer method returns
failure, the writer failure latch is set, no success receipt/callback is
published, and a retry starts from a clean transaction. For raw DXF direct
writers, byte-level rollback is only claimed where the writer has an explicit
checkpoint; otherwise the contract is failure-before-publication via preflight.

#### P1-L.11e.e: remaining filter-side raw variant consumers

The common helper adoption is sufficient for the main sidecar paths, but the
audit found a separate legacy layer-marker path that remains unsafe:
`RS_FilterDXFRW::addLayer()` dereferences each `data.extData` entry, assumes a
code `1001` value is a non-null string, and reads `content.i` for code `1070`
without checking the variant type. `hasLibreCadConstructionMarker()` has the
same type-only assumption for `1070`. A malformed layer EED can therefore
still crash or interpret unrelated union storage during import.

The next read-side sub-plan is deliberately narrow:

1. Route layer construction-marker detection through the checked marker and
   integer helpers. Null entries, wrong marker storage, and wrong `1070`
   storage must mean “marker not usable” and must not mutate the layer.
2. Audit every remaining `extData` loop in `rs_filterdxfrw.cpp`, including
   `isIgnorableLayerExtData()`, `fillEntityExtData()`, and marker-removal
   helpers. Either use the shared helper or document why the code is operating
   on an already validated typed value. A code check alone is not a sufficient
   proof for a union-backed field.
3. Decide the unknown-XDATA policy explicitly. The generic extractor currently
   ignores unrecognized group codes. For same-version round trips, either
   retain the original raw vector alongside the typed metadata or mark the
   entity as non-losslessly writable and refuse export when the unknown data is
   semantically relevant. A silent drop cannot count as preservation.
4. Keep the distinction between absent and malformed recognized markers in the
   sidecar preflight. A valid sidecar marker followed by bad payload is a hard
   refusal; an unrelated absent marker may continue through ordinary fallback.
   Do not let a malformed group be consumed merely because a later group is
   valid.
5. Add direct tests for layer marker null/wrong-type values, header null and
   non-finite values, malformed MText sidecar payloads, typed/underlay marker
   failures, DIMSTYLE wrong types, and elliptic-polyline wrong-type values.
   Keep parser tests separate from fallback-policy tests so a safe ignore is
   not mistaken for a lossless round trip.

#### P1-L.11h.c/f: mesh and polyface ownership remains a gated feature

The current descriptor and model-space transaction code is complete enough to
remove the old “procedural descriptor” item from the active queue. The remaining
work is ownership and evidence:

1. Add a writer-only user-BLOCK test that emits a mesh and a polyface while
   `beginBlockContent()` is active. The `DwgBlockWriteResult` must contain the
   parent, every physical VERTEX, and one SEQEND in order; the published
   BLOCK_RECORD list must contain each handle once; model/paper lists must not
   contain any of those handles; and every child must resolve to the active
   BLOCK_RECORD owner.
2. Inject a failure at the child or SEQEND boundary. Verify rollback of the
   pending block entity list, object map, compound receipt, frame occurrences,
   source/generated identity ledgers, consumed set, and INSERT reverse
   reference. Retry after the one-shot hook is consumed and require one clean
   owner list.
3. Only after the low-level proof, call
   `reconstructPolylineSidecars(blk, consumed)` in `writeBlocks()` immediately
   after `beginBlockContent()` and before
   `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()`. Ownership must come from the active
   writer context; no missing-handle or block-name guess may select the owner.
4. Add a filter fixture containing one mesh and one polyface inside a named
   user block referenced by INSERT. Assert that successful reconstruction
   consumes source sidecars only after commit, leaves unrelated children, and
   reads back as native compounds. Assert that refusal leaves ordinary
   fallback polylines and their sidecars available.
5. Execute in-tree readback for AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
   AC1032. External-reader results from libreDWG, ODA, and ezdxf remain named
   interoperability gates and must not be inferred from the in-tree reader.

#### P1-L.11g: INSERT/ATTRIB remains intentionally deferred

The existing low-level INSERT/ATTRIB compound test is useful evidence for the
writer's current path, but the public `Attribute` receipt role is still not a
contract. Before any filter migration, specify and test the parent INSERT's
target BLOCK_RECORD, attribute order/count, child owner handle, terminating
SEQEND, `insertHandles` reverse reference, source/generated identity, and
rollback when any attribute fails. Do not broaden the receipt API to an
arbitrary sequence just to make this family fit.

#### P1-L.8d, P1-L.9e/P1-L.10d, and P0-L.12e: structural work after the EED gate

These phases remain active, but their dependencies are now explicit:

1. Complete the executable DataStorage capability-to-filter dispatch map.
   Every advertised operation needs one observable dispatch path, a version
   range test, and an explicit refusal reason where the policy row is not
   supported. Inventory presence alone is not dispatch coverage.
2. Add post-assembly DataStorage section/page receipts. Capture canonical
   section id/order, page ids and boundaries, version, encoding/encryption,
   final byte sizes, alignment, and immutable byte identity. Reconcile the
   receipt with the section-page map after pagination, not only before it.
   Keep wide opaque record identities on the exact same-version raw path.
3. Centralize raw entity owner resolution and verify non-owner ACIS links.
   The owner graph must be checked after all generated and preserved entities

4. Gate AC1032 independently from AC1027. Generate both versions, inspect
   header/class/section/page/object-map/HANDSEED/CRC receipts, and test
   version-gated payload bits. Shared implementation is acceptable only after

### Revised implementation order

2. Finish P1-L.11e.e: layer-marker safety, remaining filter XDATA audit,

## Review Delta (rev 1118)

The low-level prerequisite is now implemented without widening the concrete
writer ABI. `dwgRW::writePolyline()` captures the committed object-frame receipt
immediately after the parent, each VERTEX, and SEQEND encodes, and publishes a
single ordered `DwgCompoundEntityWriteReceipt` only after all frames succeed.
It retains the established parent-only last-frame API for existing callers.
Every ordinary write, explicit rollback, failed child write, and filter-level
rollback clears the compound receipt, so a caller cannot attach stale child
bytes to a later entity. The receipt test proves one parent, two vertices, and
one SEQEND with unique handles and generations; it also proves explicit
rollback, injected SEQEND failure, and retry leave no receipt behind.

`reconstructPolylineSidecars()` now has one DWG compound commit route for both
mesh and polyface. It verifies that the receipt currently held by `dwgRW`
matches the exact parent/child generation and role sequence, records every
physical frame under one filter identity checkpoint, commits the source anchor
only after all frames are present, and registers VERTEX/SEQEND outputs as
`GeneratedChild` identities. A failed write or receipt/ledger operation rolls
the entire low-level compound transaction and every source sidecar identity
back, then returns before the sidecars can enter the consumed set. This closes
the model-space parent-only frame gap; it does not add user-BLOCK mesh/polyface
reconstruction.

Incremental CMake rebuilt `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests`. The new compound
receipt selector passes 66 assertions. The existing mesh/polyface sidecar and
R2010 polyline selector passes 47 assertions in three cases, including native
polyface and mesh readback. The MLINE descriptor selector remains green with
36 assertions. `git diff --check` passes. The known duplicate `LC_VERSION`
macro warning is unrelated. No sanitizer, qmake6, full-suite, external-reader,
user-BLOCK compound, or release claim is made.

### Remaining P1-L.11h work

1. Replace the current in-loop mesh and polyface validation with immutable
   `MeshSidecarDescriptor` and `PolyfaceSidecarDescriptor` values containing
   the anchor and ordered sibling pointers, reconstructed source geometry,
   expected parent flags, exact child-role count, and generated-child policy.
   Their construction must be pure and complete before the shared write route
   receives a `DRW_Polyline`; this makes the pre-write contract inspectable and

2. Add filter-level malformed, late-child failure, and same-filter retry

   Reuse the low-level SEQEND failure hook through a narrow test-only writer

3. Extend the public compound receipt deliberately to INSERT/ATTRIB only after

This review rechecked the active compound path against the actual sidecar
schema emitted by `addPolyline()`, the identity ledger, and the low-level
BLOCK_RECORD implementation. The completed low-level path is soundly narrow:
`dwgRW::writePolyline()` reserves and emits the POLYLINE, each VERTEX, and the
SEQEND in one checkpoint; it publishes their ordered receipts only after the
last child succeeds. The active-block writer records every compound child in
the selected `PendingUserBlock::entityHandles` list, so the eventual
BLOCK_RECORD has a mechanism to represent the full owned sequence. The filter
currently uses that receipt for model-space mesh/polyface reconstruction only.

The remaining in-loop mesh/polyface checks are intentionally not yet called
descriptors, and this audit identified several conditions they do not prove:

1. A mesh selects the first entry with source vertices as its anchor. It does
   not require exactly one anchor, `row` role/index zero, or a one-to-one map
   of all `M` row roles and `N` column roles. Unique global `elementIndex`
   alone still admits a duplicate role plus a missing role.
2. A mesh compares dimensions and visible XY endpoints, but does not require
   common flags, smoothing values, curve type, expected closed state, finite
   source coordinates, or the schema relation `row.elementIndex == rowIndex`
   and `column.elementIndex == M + columnIndex`. It also performs signed-int
   `M + N` and `M * N` computations before bounding them against the writer's
   owned-object limit.
3. Both families accept endpoint-equivalent fallback polylines without proving
   that every segment remains a straight LINE. A changed arc/bulge can retain
   the same endpoints and be silently collapsed into a native mesh/polyface.
   They also take attributes solely from the selected anchor, so a presentation
   edit to one sibling could be discarded by reconstruction.
4. A polyface likewise selects the first nonempty source list and ignores the
   recorded `originalFaceCount`, common flags, closed state, finite source
   coordinates, and exact face-index-to-entry ordering. Its currently sorted
   output therefore has less provenance than the source schema contains.
5. `commitDwgPolylineCompound()` checks the caller's copied receipt against
   the current wrapper receipt by handle, generation, version, and role. The
   private caller is currently trusted, but the next cleanup should make the
   commit routine fetch the current receipt itself, or compare full immutable
   frame layout/occurrence data, so a future caller cannot supply a compatible
   but incomplete copy.

### P1-L.11h.a: Immutable sidecar admission

1. Introduce local `MeshSidecarDescriptor` and `PolyfaceSidecarDescriptor`
   values beside `MLineSidecarDescriptor`. Each owns no geometry or entities:
   it holds a non-null anchor pointer, an ordered vector of member pointers,
   the checked source-coordinate span, normalized counts/flags, and the
   expected POLYLINE child count. Construction returns `nullopt` before any
   DWG or DXF write and never mutates the collected group.
2. Add one shared checked-coordinate and linear-fallback helper. It must reject
   non-finite XYZ source coordinates, non-finite visible points, arcs/bulges,
   unexpected atomic entities, closure mismatches, and presentation attributes
   that differ from the anchor. Preserve the existing `RS_TOLERANCE` XY
   comparison, but require every fallback segment to be a LINE so endpoint
   equality cannot erase a shape edit.
3. For a mesh descriptor, require exactly one source-vertex anchor and require
   it to be element zero, role `row`, and row index zero. Check positive `M`
   and `N` with checked addition/multiplication, bound `M * N` by
   `dwgSafety::MaxOwnedObjectCount`, ensure `M + N` is representable for the
   collected sidecar group, and require the source list to contain exactly
   `M * N` finite coordinates. Every member must have identical mesh
   id, flags, `M`, `N`, smoothing values, curve type, and element count. Require
   mesh bit `0x10`, reject nonzero curve type until a typed smooth-surface
   representation exists, and require all row and column role indices exactly
   once. Rows use `elementIndex == rowIndex`, `N` linear vertices, and the
   N-closed flag; columns use `elementIndex == M + columnIndex`, `M` linear
   vertices, and the M-closed flag.
4. For a polyface descriptor, require exactly one anchor at face index zero;
   require a positive, bounded vertex/face count; require `faceCount ==
   originalFaceCount == member count`; and require exactly that many finite
   source vertices. Every face must share id, flags, counts, and presentation
   attributes, have the polyface bit `0x40`, occupy its exact face index once,
   and remain a closed linear three- or four-point fallback. Validate that the
   first three signed indices are nonzero, the fourth is zero only for a
   triangle, absolute indices are within the source span, signs are preserved,
   and each visible point exactly corresponds to its indexed source vertex.
5. Build `DRW_Polyline` only from a descriptor. Do not sort or otherwise mutate
   the original collection in the emitter; descriptor member order is the
   authoritative row/column or face order. A rejected descriptor leaves every
   fallback entity unconsumed for the ordinary writer.

### P1-L.11h.b: Receipt and failure closure

1. Narrow the public receipt documentation to the currently implemented
   POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND producer. Keep `Attribute` reserved but do not imply
   INSERT support. Make the filter's private compound commit fetch the current
   writer receipt itself, then validate its parent owner, full role sequence,
   object handle, generation, version, bit-range sizes, and occurrence list
   before recording any identity. This removes the mutable copied-receipt
   parameter from the trust boundary.
2. Retain one identity checkpoint around the entire sidecar output. On a failed
   low-level child, receipt validation, frame-ledger record, or identity commit,
   roll back the low-level compound transaction and all selected source
   identities; do not add a consumed entity, a generated child, or an
   owner/reference receipt. Preserve the fallback entities for a later ordinary
   path only when descriptor validation declined before a write began; a
   required DWG write failure remains an export failure.
3. Add a narrow test-only filter/writer seam for the existing SEQEND failure
   hook only if the integration test cannot reach it through the current
   friend-based test access. Do not expose a production failure switch merely
   to test the filter. The same test must retry with the same filter/graphic
   after clearing the hook and prove that no stale compound receipt or planned
   identity survives.

### P1-L.11h.c: Focused evidence and block admission

1. Add descriptor refusal fixtures for duplicate mesh row/column role, second
   mesh anchor, changed closure, an arc/bulge retaining endpoints, mismatched
   sibling pen/layer, non-finite source coordinate, duplicate polyface anchor,
   mismatched original face count, and malformed signed face indices. Each
   fixture must export only its ordinary fallback polylines, not a native
   POLYLINE mesh/polyface.
2. Add successful mesh and polyface fixtures at AC1024 first, then rerun at
   AC1027 and AC1032 after the descriptor itself is version-neutral. Assert one
   parent, exactly `sourceVertexCount` VERTEX frames, one SEQEND, unique object
   map handles/generations, child parent handles, source-anchor identity, and
   generated-child identities only for physical child frames.
3. Add a late-SEQEND-failure/retry fixture for each family. The failed attempt
   must leave no object-map entry, no source/generated identity, no consumed
   fallback, and no destination accepted by `fileExport`; the clean retry must
   produce exactly one native compound without duplicated callbacks.
4. Only after model-space evidence passes, add one user-BLOCK fixture per
   family. It must prove that `DwgBlockWriteResult` contains the parent,
   every VERTEX, and SEQEND exactly once in that block's `entityHandles`, that
   no model-space owner receives a child, and that block-phase rollback after a
   late child failure leaves the deferred block result empty. Do not add either
   reconstruction route to `writeBlocks()` before these owner-list assertions
   pass.

The next implementation slice is P1-L.11h.a only: pure descriptor helpers and
their rejection tests. It intentionally does not add INSERT receipts, change
the concrete writer ABI, enable compounds in user BLOCKs, or broaden DWG
version claims.

The descriptor boundary now proves all of the following before a native
POLYLINE can replace fallback geometry:

1. Each marker group has exactly one correctly typed application marker, the

   variant type, repeated marker, or an additional payload code is a refusal,
   not an attempt to read the variant's inactive storage.

   mesh flag set, and a zero curve type. Checked `M + N` and `M * N` arithmetic
   bounds both group and source sizes. Every row and column occurs exactly

   remains a LINE-only polyline, and matches the recorded source grid.
3. Polyface reconstruction has one face-zero anchor only, exact face-count
   agreement with the original count and group size, bounded source/face

   The absolute-index calculation widens before negation, so `INT_MIN` cannot
   overflow while being validated.

   any layer, visibility, pen, alpha, or dash-offset divergence from the

## Review Delta (rev 1122)

This review was checked against the current source rather than the previous
roadmap wording. The focused CMake writer lane is green at 301 assertions in 8
test cases. The command used was the warm `build/dwg-fast` target with the
receipt, R2010, sidecar-safety, sidecar-transaction, and sidecar-version
selectors. No full-suite, sanitizer, qmake6, external-reader, or release
validation is implied by that result.

### What is now proven

1. The immutable mesh/polyface descriptors are version-neutral at the filter
   boundary. Existing AC1024 evidence plus the new AC1027 and AC1032 cases
   prove that a successful model-space compound publishes one parent, four
   VERTEX frames, and one SEQEND for the fixtures, with unique physical
   frame receipts and committed generated-child identities. The model-space
   receipt's `parentOwnerHandle == NoHandle` is intentional; the BLOCK_RECORD
   owner list, not a nonzero entity owner field, supplies reachability.
2. A late SEQEND failure is observable through the real `fileExport()` path.
   The failed mesh/polyface attempt removes the destination, physical frame
   occurrences, source identity, generated-child identity, and current
   compound receipt. A retry with the same filter and graphic emits one clean
   compound. This is filter-level transaction evidence, not merely a low-level
   writer failure test.
3. The current descriptor boundary rejects duplicate mesh anchors, wrong mesh
   role/index, inconsistent polyface original-face counts, changed sibling
   presentation, and extra sidecar payload fields. The ordinary fallback path
   remains available for those refusals.

### Code-to-plan corrections

1. `RS_FilterDXFRW::writeEntities()` invokes
   `reconstructPolylineSidecars(m_graphic, consumed)` before the ordinary
   entity loop. `RS_FilterDXFRW::writeBlocks()` does not invoke that route; it
   currently runs `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()` while a user BLOCK is
   active and then calls `writeEntity()` for the remaining children. The
   roadmap must therefore describe the current route as top-level/model-space
   reconstruction only, not general block support.
2. `writeDwgPolylineSidecar()` currently receives a descriptor member list but
   lets `DRW_Polyline::vertlist.size()` be the only effective child-count
   source. `PolyfaceSidecarDescriptor::compoundVertexCount` is calculated but
   not enforced. Before broadening admission, add an explicit expected-count
   argument and reject before `dwgRW::writePolyline()` unless the descriptor,
   `vertlist`, `vertexcount`, and expected compound child count agree. The
   mesh expected count is its source vertex count; the polyface expected count
   is source vertices plus face records.
3. The current version test reads the generated file with the in-tree DWG
   reader. It proves wire compatibility with that reader and the filter
   ledger, but it is not an ODA/AutoCAD/external-reader claim. Keep those
   validation levels separate in later status updates.
4. The safety cases mutate imported sidecars through the integration path; no
   direct unit test currently proves every extractor variant failure. The
   malformed-type matrix must be explicit because a wrong `DRW_Variant` type
   must cause refusal without calling inactive-storage accessors.

### Revised implementation order

#### P1-L.11h.d: close the descriptor-to-emitter count contract

1. Add one checked `expectedVertexCount` parameter to the DWG sidecar emitter.
   Pass `descriptor->sourceVertexCount` for mesh and
   `descriptor->compoundVertexCount` for polyface. Check the value before
   starting the low-level transaction and require the generated list size and
   serialized `vertexcount` to match the descriptor. Keep all arithmetic in
   `size_t` after checked conversion from the sidecar counts.
2. Preserve the existing early-refusal rule: a count mismatch before writing
   leaves the source entries unconsumed and allows the ordinary fallback path.
   A mismatch discovered after a low-level write has started is an export
   failure and must use the existing rollback path.
3. Add one positive assertion for each family and one test-only mutation that
   makes the generated count disagree. The negative case must prove no
   partial receipt or identity survives.

#### P1-L.11e: complete the refusal matrix for both output families

1. Build a reusable test fixture from an imported sidecar source and apply
   exactly one mutation per run: changed closure, a nonzero bulge or arc with
   unchanged endpoints, non-finite source coordinate, duplicate polyface
   anchor, invalid signed face index, changed sibling layer/pen, and wrong
   `1001`, `1000`, `1070`, or `1010` variant type. Do not mutate the source
   collection order; descriptor order is part of the contract.
2. Export every refusal to DWG and DXF. For DWG, read with the existing
   capture interface and require fallback LWPOLYLINE records only. For DXF,
   read the output through the binary/ascii DXF reader and check both fallback
   geometry and the original `LibreCAD_POLYLINE_*` XDATA. This catches the
   nearby failure mode where a claimed sidecar is rejected but its ordinary
   geometry or metadata is silently dropped.
3. Check finite-coordinate rejection before any point comparison and keep
   signed-index validation widened before absolute-value conversion. Add a
   direct extractor assertion where the mutation is a variant-type error so
   the test distinguishes safe refusal from accidental fallback after an
   unsafe accessor.

#### P1-L.11f: admit mesh/polyface compounds to user BLOCKs

1. First add a deferred writer-only proof using `beginBlockContent()`, the
   existing `DwgBlockWriteResult`, and a real compound write. Verify one
   user BLOCK record owns the parent, every VERTEX, and SEQEND exactly once;
   verify model-space lists do not receive those handles; and verify the
   final BLOCK_RECORD uses the same ordered ownership set after deferred
   emission.
2. Add a failure after a child frame while the user BLOCK is active. The
   block transaction must restore the pending block's entity list, object map,
   published receipt, and identity checkpoint before any BLOCK_RECORD is
   emitted. Re-run the same block with the failure hook cleared and require a
   single owner list with no duplicate handles.
3. Only after those writer assertions pass, move the descriptor pre-pass into
   the block path. Give it the active block owner explicitly; do not infer a
   user-block owner from `NoHandle`. Keep model-space and user-block
   transactions distinct so a failed block cannot roll back an already
   committed top-level entity.
4. Add one mesh and one polyface user-BLOCK filter fixture, including an
   INSERT that references the block, then inspect both the deferred owner list
   and in-tree readback. External-reader validation remains a separate gate.

#### P1-L.11g: only then widen compound families

1. Keep `DwgCompoundEntityFrameRole::Attribute` reserved until an INSERT/
   ATTRIB producer has an explicit receipt, child count, owner handle, and
   rollback contract. The current POLYLINE receipt must not be generalized by
   changing enum names or accepting an arbitrary frame sequence.
2. Audit INSERT attributes for the same distinction between source-backed
   identities and generated children. A failed attribute must leave the
   parent INSERT uncommitted and must not leave a dangling reverse reference
   in the block's `insertHandles` list.
3. Add version coverage only after the owner and refusal matrices are green;
   reuse the existing focused selectors and `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh` so
   the incremental loop does not rebuild unrelated application tests.

### Current status and next slice

- Complete: immutable mesh/polyface admission, model-space POLYLINE receipt

## Review Delta (rev 1124): codebase-grounded execution update

This revision supersedes the execution wording in rev 1123 while preserving
the earlier entries as history. It was checked against the current
`RS_FilterDXFRW` implementation, `dwgWriter15` block transactions, and the
focused CMake writer target. It intentionally narrows the next slice instead
of treating every guarded accessor or every existing readback test as proof
of complete DWG/DXF support.

### Verified state

1. The mesh/polyface DWG emitter now checks the descriptor's physical child
   count and semantic `vertexcount`/`facecount` before calling
   `dwgRW::writePolyline()`. The focused version/readback, receipt, R2010,
   refusal, transaction, safety, and malformed-type selectors pass **485
   assertions in 10 test cases** through the warm `build/dwg-fast` CMake
   target. The malformed selector alone passes 64 assertions.
2. The model-space sidecar path has real filter-level rollback evidence for a
   late SEQEND failure and a clean retry. The evidence covers the current
   mesh/polyface fixtures at AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 and is limited to the
   in-tree reader plus the filter's internal receipt/identity ledger.
3. Valid descriptor refusal remains recoverable: the source polylines are
   left unconsumed and the ordinary fallback writer gets another chance.
   This applies to changed closure, geometry/presentation mismatch, duplicate
   anchors, invalid indices, and other schema inconsistencies.
4. A wrong `DRW_Variant` storage type is a different failure class. The
   malformed matrix now reaches the real `fileExport()` path without a crash,
   and rejects all eight wrong-type DWG/DXF cases. The generic EED writer
   cannot safely preserve an integer-as-string, double-as-coordinate, or
   similar malformed value, so it must report export failure rather than
   silently coerce or drop the value. The roadmap must not describe these
   cases as successful fallback preservation.

### Newly confirmed implementation gaps

#### P1-L.11e.a: centralize checked XDATA access

The recent crash fixes cover the paths reached by the polyline malformed
fixture (`isGeneratedInsertAttrib()`, `extractMLineMeta()`, and
`extractLWPolylineMeta()`), but the audit still finds the same unchecked
assumption in adjacent code:

1. `extractEntityExtData()` dereferences every input variant and calls
   `c_str()`, `coord()`, `i_val()`, or `d_val()` from the group code alone.
   This is a read-side UB/crash boundary for malformed DWG EED and malformed
   DXF XDATA, and it also accepts a null shared pointer as if it were a
   record.
2. `parseDimStyleExtData()` has the same null/type problem and toggles its
   `expectType` state even for unsupported group codes. A malformed sequence
   can therefore poison the next typed value while appearing to parse
   successfully.
3. `extractInsertAttribSidecar()` still assumes the expected type for its
   `1070`, `1071`, `1040`, `1010`-`1012`, and `1000` fields after validating only
   the marker. The MText XDATA/common groups are copied before their payload
   schema is validated.
4. Hatch, image-frame, TEXT OCS, and MTEXT OCS extractors and their removal
   helpers still call `c_str()` for code `1001` without requiring a non-null
   string variant. Their coordinate and real-value accessors need the same
   checked boundary. `reconstructTypedConversions()` has the equivalent
   unchecked marker scan while stripping re-emitted F2 groups.

Implement a small local checked-access layer used by all of these helpers,
with no implicit conversion between `DRW_Variant` storage types:

1. `readXdataString`, `readXdataCoord`, `readXdataInteger`,
   `readXdataDouble`, and `readXdataBinary` take a nullable variant, an
   expected code/range, and an output reference. They return `Absent` for a
   nonmatching code, `Malformed` for a matching code with null or wrong
   storage, and `Ok` only after the accessor is legal. Numeric helpers reject
   non-finite values where the corresponding DWG/DXF field is a coordinate or
   real-valued geometric parameter.
2. Add `readXdataMarker()` on top of the string helper. A malformed marker
   terminates the active application group and records malformed state; it
   must never inherit the previous group.
3. Preserve the distinction between “marker absent” and “marker present but
   malformed” in sidecar results. The former permits ordinary behavior; the
   latter is surfaced to the writer preflight so a bad value cannot reach a
   generic encoder.
4. Make `extractEntityExtData()` and `parseDimStyleExtData()` total over null
   and wrong-type input. They may discard an invalid record according to the
   existing compatibility policy, but they must not allocate partial nested
   tags or change parser state from an invalid field. Add direct tests for
   null variants, wrong marker types, wrong numeric types, invalid binary
   text, and an unmatched `102` brace.

#### P1-L.11e.b: make fallback and export-failure policy executable

1. Add a preflight over XDATA/EED before ordinary fallback emission. A valid
   schema refusal keeps the source entity available; an unrepresentable
   variant sets `m_writeFailed`, removes any destination already created by
   the current export transaction, and prevents callbacks/partial output.
   Do not repair malformed storage by reading a different union member.
2. Keep DXF binary `1004` handling explicit: binary storage is accepted for
   DWG and binary-DXF input, while ASCII DXF hex text is decoded only after
   strict string validation. An invalid hex payload is a hard export/read
   failure, not an empty byte array.
3. Extend the current mesh/polyface matrix to assert the policy separately:
   valid sidecar edits produce fallback LWPOLYLINE records and retain their
   sidecar data; wrong-type or invalid-binary cases return `fileExport ==
   false`, leave no destination, and do not publish a native compound receipt.
4. Add the equivalent read-side assertions through `dxfRW` and `dwgRW`, with
   callback counts and map/identity counts checked after failure. This closes
   the gap between “no crash” and “no partial parse/write state.”

#### P1-L.11f.a: prove active user-BLOCK ownership before routing sidecars

The current `writeBlocks()` path defines all blocks, calls
`beginBlockContent()`, runs only `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()`, writes
remaining children, calls `endBlockContent()`, and commits one block-phase
transaction. The low-level `dwgWriter15` already appends compound children
to the active pending block when they are marked as compound children, and
its checkpoint can restore pending entity/insert-list sizes. That is useful
infrastructure, not yet proof that the filter chooses the correct owner.

Implement the block gate in this order:

1. Add a writer-only test using the existing `DwgBlockWriteResult` seam. Open
   one user block, emit a real mesh and polyface compound independently, and
   assert that each result contains exactly one parent, the descriptor's
   physical VERTEX frames, and one SEQEND in order. Assert that no child is in
   model-space lists and that the pending block's owner handle is the active
   block record.
2. Arm the existing one-shot late-child/SEQEND failure while the block is
   active. Assert rollback of the pending block entity list, object map,
   frame occurrences, receipt, and source/generated identities before the
   BLOCK_RECORD is emitted. Retry after the hook is consumed and require one
   clean owner list with no duplicates.
3. Only after those assertions pass, invoke
   `reconstructPolylineSidecars(blk, consumed)` between
   `beginBlockContent()` and `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()`. The active
   writer context must supply the user-block owner; no code may infer a user
   block from `NoHandle`. On failure, end/rollback the block phase exactly
   once and do not continue the ordinary entity loop.
4. Add one filter fixture for a mesh and one for a polyface inside a user
   block referenced by INSERT. Inspect the deferred block result and perform
   in-tree DWG readback. Keep external-reader validation separate.

#### P1-L.11g.a: defer INSERT/ATTRIB until its ownership contract exists

The public `DwgCompoundEntityFrameRole::Attribute` value is still reserved;
the POLYLINE receipt does not authorize INSERT migration. Before changing it:

1. Define the ATTRIB child count, owner handle, SEQEND behavior, source versus
   generated identity rules, and the block's `insertHandles` reverse-reference
   rule. A failed attribute must leave neither a dangling parent INSERT nor a
   partial block reference.
2. Add low-level and filter retry tests using the same transaction and
   identity checkpoints as POLYLINE, then add version coverage only for the
   versions that pass the ownership matrix.
3. Do not broaden the compound receipt enum or accept arbitrary frame
   sequences as a shortcut. Each producer needs an explicit descriptor and
   rollback proof.

### Verification ladder for the next implementation slices

Use the warm target and selectors below as the default loop. Do not rebuild
the whole application or run the slow corpus lane after every local edit:

1. Parser guard edit: build `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` incrementally and
   run the single direct XDATA safety selector.
2. Sidecar behavior edit: run the 10-case, 485-assertion selector gate plus
   `git diff --check`.
3. Block-owner edit: run the writer-only block selector, then the two filter
   user-block fixtures, then the combined sidecar gate.
4. Integration gate: run the existing LibreCAD filter tests and qmake6 only
   after a complete slice is green. Sanitizers, external readers, and corpus
   tests remain milestone gates rather than per-edit tests.

Record exact assertion counts and the command/target in the next roadmap
revision. A passing in-tree reader is not evidence of AutoCAD, ODA, ezdxf, or
libreDWG interoperability; those claims require a separately named fixture
and external-reader result.

### Updated status and next slice

- Complete: descriptor admission, expected physical/semantic count closure,
  model-space POLYLINE receipt publication, filter transaction rollback,
  AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 in-tree model-space evidence, valid-refusal coverage,
  and the wrong-variant malformed safety matrix.
- In progress: P1-L.11e.a checked XDATA access and P1-L.11e.b explicit
  fallback-versus-hard-failure behavior for all adjacent EED/sidecar paths.
- Next structural gate: P1-L.11f.a low-level user-BLOCK owner-list and
  late-child rollback proof. Do not route mesh/polyface reconstruction into
  `writeBlocks()` until it passes.
- Deferred: INSERT/ATTRIB receipt expansion, typed ACIS/SAB conversion,
  external-reader interoperability, qmake6/full-suite validation, and any
  claim of complete DWG version support.

## Review Delta (rev 1125): second codebase-grounded execution update

This revision re-audited the implementation after the checked-XDATA pass,
using the symbols and call paths currently present in
`librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp`,
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdxfrw.cpp`, and
`libraries/libdxfrw/src/intern/dwgwriter15.cpp`. It narrows the next slice
again. The plan must distinguish a parser that does not crash from a parser
that refuses malformed data atomically, and it must distinguish low-level
BLOCK support from filter-generated sidecar admission.

### What the current tree now proves

1. The local `XDataReadResult` helpers reject null variants, wrong storage
   types, null string/coordinate/binary payload pointers, and non-finite
   geometric values before the accessor is used. They are now used by the
   generic entity EED parser, dimension-style EED parser, INSERT/ATTRIB
   sidecar parser, OCS sidecar readers/removers, and the typed-conversion
   marker stripping path.
2. The direct malformed EED test passes 51 assertions in three test cases,
   and the focused mesh/polyface safety matrix passes 485 assertions in ten
   cases. Those results establish a useful regression floor; they do not yet
   establish complete XDATA coverage or atomic behavior for every caller.
3. `dwgWriter15` already has an active user-BLOCK owner context, pending
   `entityHandles`/`insertHandles`, compound checkpoints, and rollback of
   those lists. The existing low-level test proves ordinary POLYLINE and
   INSERT/ATTRIB compounds can be read back from a user block.
4. The filter's `writeBlocks()` still runs only
   `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()` while a user block is active. The
   mesh/polyface reconstruction pre-pass remains model-space-only. Therefore
   the existing low-level BLOCK test must not be cited as evidence that
   filter-generated mesh/polyface sidecars are admitted to user blocks.

### Findings that change the remaining plan

#### P1-L.11e.c: checked-access adoption is still incomplete

The new helper layer is not yet a complete boundary. The following paths
still read union-backed values directly or can treat a malformed value as
absent:

1. `parseDwgUnderlaySidecar()` and `hasDwgUnderlaySidecar()` check the marker
   type but still call `c_str()` without checking `content.s`. Their active
   groups also skip null variants, so a null payload after a valid marker can
   produce a partially parsed sidecar instead of a hard refusal.
2. `parseTypedConversionSidecar()` and
   `hasDwgTypedConversionSidecar()` have the same marker-pointer gap. Their
   numeric checks are locally safe, but they should use the common helpers so
   pointer, finite-value, and exact-storage rules cannot diverge.
3. `decodeInsertAttribMTextXData()` and
   `decodeInsertAttribMTextCommon()` still call `c_str()`, `d_val()`, and
   `i_val()` after type-only checks. The string pointer, finite-double,
   signed-handle/range, and binary-hex checks need to be explicit. The
   encoded MText group is copied before decoding, so malformed data must be
   rejected before it can be replayed.
4. `addHeader()` still reads `content.v`, `content.s`, and `c_str()` directly
   for header/custom variables. `addPolylineSegment()` has the same risk for
   the LibreCAD elliptic-arcs marker and also assumes every shared pointer is
   non-null. These are read-side entry points and need the same totality
   contract as entity EED.
5. `strVal()` and the large raw-accessor sequence in `createDimStyle()` treat
   presence of a named DIMSTYLE variable as proof of its storage type. A
   malformed variable can therefore corrupt style construction even though
   the generic EED parser is guarded. The style-variable type table must be
   made explicit and invalid optional fields must leave the default intact.
6. `extractEntityExtData()` now avoids unsafe access, but an unmatched
   `102`/`1002` brace can still leave an already-created app/group object or
   partial nested list in the returned metadata. The intended invariant must
   be decided and tested: invalid groups are dropped atomically, while valid
   groups before and after them remain available.

Implement this slice as a bounded adoption pass, not as another broad parser
rewrite:

1. Keep the helper local to the filter until all call sites have migrated.
   Add a marker helper returning `Absent`, `Malformed`, or `Valid`; make the
   hex helper return the same distinction rather than a boolean. A matching
   code with invalid storage must never be treated as an absent optional
   field.
2. Migrate underlay, typed conversion, MText decode, header/custom-variable,
   and elliptic-polyline paths. Use exact storage types for each recognized
   code; reject non-finite coordinates/reals; validate unsigned handles before
   converting; require even, hexadecimal text for textual `1004` values.
3. For every recognized sidecar marker, make null or malformed data while
   the marker is active terminate with a malformed result. Do not publish a
   partially filled sidecar, do not consume the source entity, and do not
   let an invalid group bleed into the next marker.
4. Replace `strVal()` with a checked string read and add a small DIMSTYLE
   field descriptor table covering expected string, integer, and double
   variables. The constructor may ignore an invalid optional variable, but it
   must not reinterpret its union or overwrite a valid default.
5. Define the EED brace policy in the implementation: stage one application
   group until its group/control structure is closed, discard only the
   malformed group on bad storage or unbalanced braces, and retain unrelated
   valid application groups. Add a depth-aware close check rather than using
   a final `listParents.clear()` as implicit recovery.

#### P1-L.11e.d: make the writer failure contract complete

The low-level DXF writer now records failures from `writeExtData()`, but the
callers are mixed: many entity/object writers ignore the boolean return while
others combine it into their result. This leaves a real risk of bytes being
written for an entity whose EED was rejected, followed by a successful
top-level return or a later callback.

The implementation-ready contract is:

1. Validate the complete EED/XDATA vector before allocating a DWG object
   handle or emitting an entity frame. For DXF, validate before the first
   group of that entity is written where the writer API permits; otherwise
   latch `m_writeError` and make the containing entity writer return false.
2. Never silently skip a null variant, unsupported recognized storage type,
   invalid `1004` text, non-finite real, or invalid coordinate. Unknown group
   codes may remain compatibility-skipped only when their storage is not
   accessed by this library.
3. Audit every `writeExtData()` call in `libdxfrw.cpp`. Either combine its
   result with the containing `result` or explicitly document why the caller
   is already failure-latched. Add a test that injects a bad EED after a
   valid ordinary field and verifies `write()` is false and no public
   success/callback state is published.
4. Preserve the existing distinction between a valid sidecar schema refusal
   and an unrepresentable malformed variant. The former leaves the source
   available for ordinary fallback; the latter is an export failure and must
   roll back the current object/compound transaction.
5. For binary DXF, encode `BINARY` 1004 values as bounded hexadecimal chunks;
   for ASCII DXF, accept only validated hexadecimal text. Test both forms,
   including an odd-length string, a non-hex character, and a null binary
   payload.

#### P1-L.11f.b: user-BLOCK admission must test the filter route

The prior BLOCK sub-plan was too strong about the existing low-level test.
Use it as a foundation and add the missing filter-level proof:

1. Extend the writer-only seam with a real mesh and a real polyface
   compound, each emitted while `beginBlockContent()` is active. Verify the
   receipt order is parent, all physical VERTEX frames, then SEQEND; verify
   the pending user BLOCK owns each handle exactly once and model/paper lists
   contain none of those children.
2. Add a late-child/SEQEND failure while the active user block is open. The
   rollback oracle must cover the pending block entity list, object map,
   frame receipt, generated/source identity ledgers, and insert references.
   After the failure hook is consumed, retry and require one clean owner list
   with no duplicate handles.
3. Add the filter route only after that low-level test passes:
   `writeBlocks()` should invoke `reconstructPolylineSidecars(blk, consumed)`
   immediately after `beginBlockContent()` and before the existing
   single-frame pass. The active writer context, not `NoHandle` or a guessed
   block name, is the sole owner source.
4. Add one mesh and one polyface fixture in a user BLOCK referenced by an
   INSERT. Verify source sidecar entities are consumed only after successful
   commit, ordinary unrelated children remain, and a failed reconstruction
   rolls back the entire block phase exactly once.
5. Read back the resulting files with the in-tree reader for AC1015,
   AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032. Keep libreDWG/ODA/ezdxf
   results as separately named external gates; in-tree readback cannot prove
   external interoperability.

#### P1-L.11g.b: keep INSERT/ATTRIB deferred

The low-level INSERT/ATTRIB test is evidence for the existing writer path,
not permission to expand the compound receipt. Before adding a new filter
route, specify and test all of the following:

1. Parent INSERT owner and target BLOCK_RECORD handle.
2. Attribute child order, count, owner handle, and terminating SEQEND.
3. The `insertHandles` reverse-reference entry for the target block.
4. Source/generated identity and receipt rollback when any attribute fails.

Do not use a generic frame list or infer ownership from a missing handle as a
substitute for this contract.

### Revised implementation order

1. Complete P1-L.11e.c checked-access adoption and add the direct malformed
   marker, MText, header, DIMSTYLE, elliptic-polyline, and unmatched-brace
   tests. This is the next code slice.
2. Complete P1-L.11e.d writer preflight/result propagation and its atomic
   no-callback/no-partial-output tests. Do not widen sidecar admission while
   this contract is incomplete.
3. Extend the low-level P1-L.11f.b owner-list/rollback test for generated
   mesh/polyface compounds.
4. Route mesh/polyface sidecars through user BLOCKs and add the two filter
   fixtures plus versioned in-tree readback.
5. Re-audit all `DRW_Variant` accessors in the DWG header/object readers and
   all DXF entity/object writers, then run sanitizer and external-reader
   milestones. Only after those gates may the roadmap claim this slice is
   complete.

### Verification ladder for this revision

Use the warm `build/dwg-fast` target and keep the feedback loop narrow:

1. Checked-access edits: build `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` incrementally
   and run the direct entity-metadata, underlay, MText, and DIMSTYLE
   selectors.
2. Writer propagation edits: run the smallest DXF/DWG malformed-EED
   selectors, then the existing 10-case/485-assertion sidecar gate.
3. Low-level BLOCK edits: run only the writer BLOCK/compound selectors and
   the filter's two new user-BLOCK fixtures.
4. Slice milestone: run `git diff --check`, existing LibreCAD filter tests,
   qmake6, ASan/UBSan, and named external-reader gates. Full corpus tests
   remain milestone-only and must not be part of every edit loop.

Record exact assertion counts and whether a fixture was executed or skipped;
do not turn a missing external tool or missing developer corpus into a
passing interoperability claim.

### Status after rev1125

- Complete: checked access for the generic EED/dimension-style/INSERT main
  paths and the existing model-space sidecar receipt/rollback matrix.
- Partially complete: checked-access adoption, because underlay, typed marker,
  MText decode, header/custom variables, DIMSTYLE construction, and
  elliptic-polyline marker paths still require migration or direct tests.
- Not started: complete EED writer preflight/result propagation and atomic
  malformed-group staging.
- Proven only at low level: ordinary user-BLOCK POLYLINE and INSERT/ATTRIB
  ownership. Filter-generated mesh/polyface user-BLOCK admission remains
  gated by P1-L.11f.b.
- Deferred: INSERT/ATTRIB receipt expansion, typed ACIS/SAB conversion,
  external-reader interoperability, qmake6/full-suite milestone validation,
  and any claim of complete DWG version support.

## Review Delta (rev 1127): post-EED codebase audit

This section supersedes every earlier active/status section in this file. It
was reviewed against the current working tree on 2026-08-30. It records what
the source proves now, corrects stale claims in rev1126 and rev1125, and keeps
the implementation queue limited to work that still has a concrete exit test.

### Evidence reviewed

- `libraries/libdxfrw/src/libdxfrw.cpp`, including `dxfRW::write()`,
  `writeEntity()`, `writeAppData()`, `writeTableEntryAppData()`,
  `writeDimstyle()`, all `writeExtData()` callers, and raw DXF replay.
- `librecad/src/lib/filters/rs_filterdxfrw.cpp`, including the checked
  `DRW_Variant` helpers, typed-conversion and INSERT/ATTRIB sidecars, header
  variables, DIMSTYLE construction, and mesh/polyface/MLINE extraction.
- `librecad/src/lib/filters/tests/dxf_object_tests.cpp`,
  `entity_metadata_tests.cpp`, and `dwg_write_smoke_tests.cpp`.
- The warm CMake tree `build/dwg-fast`; no clean rebuild or broad corpus run
  is used as evidence for this revision.

### What the current tree proves

1. **DXF EED preflight is implemented.** The raw-pointer and shared-pointer
   `writeExtData()` overloads share one complete-vector validation pass. Null
   variants, invalid recognized storage, non-finite reals/coordinates, odd or
   non-hexadecimal textual `1004`, oversized binary data, out-of-range `1071`,
   and unknown EED codes fail before the first EED group is emitted.
2. **DXF APPDATA validation is implemented at its own boundary.** Nesting,
   opener/closer order, null strings, unsupported variant types, and non-finite
   doubles are checked before application groups are emitted. The same helper
   is used through `writeTableEntryAppData()` and the BLOCK path.
3. **DIMSTYLE dynamic write values have a low-level descriptor table.** The
   current table records supported code, variant type, and minimum DXF version;
   the writer rejects unknown or wrong-type values for the target version and
   suppresses fields that do not exist in that target. This is a writer-side
   contract, not yet a shared read/write schema.
4. **The EED call-site audit is materially complete.** There is no remaining
   bare `writeExtData(...);` statement in `libdxfrw.cpp`. Callers either combine
   the result, pass it through the local write accumulator, or return failure.
   This closes result propagation for EED itself, but not the larger
   `writeEntity()` result contract described below.
5. **Layer construction-marker access is null/type guarded.** Invalid layer
   marker storage is no longer read through the inactive union member. The
   malformed-marker policy is still not independently tested for all layer
   metadata variants.
6. **Model-space mesh/polyface descriptor admission is implemented.** The
   descriptor checks marker schema, roles, counts, source geometry, finite
   coordinates, presentation agreement, linear fallback geometry, signed face
   indices, and the physical child-count contract before writing. Its DWG
   receipt/identity rollback and AC1024/AC1027/AC1032 in-tree evidence are
   already recorded in the preceding review deltas.
7. **The focused malformed DXF writer lane is green:**
   `dxf_object_tests.cpp` with `[dxf][xdata][malformed]` passes 13 assertions
   in 4 cases. Existing positive table-XDATA and application-group checks pass
   8 assertions in 1 case and 33 assertions in 3 cases respectively. These are
   focused CMake results only.

### Findings that keep the gates open

#### P1-L.11e.c: checked read-side access is not yet a closed contract

The common `readXDataString`, `readXDataInteger`, `readXDataDouble`,
`readXDataCoord`, and `readXDataBinary` helpers are safe, and several major
sidecar parsers use them. The remaining code still has correctness gaps that
must be addressed before this item is marked complete:

1. `extractLWPolylineMeta()` and `extractMLineMeta()` accept `INTEGER64` for
   code `1071` and then call `i_val()` instead of reading and range-checking the
   64-bit value. This is a type/union mismatch, not just missing validation.
2. The same extractors can silently accept a null or non-finite coordinate after
   a recognized `1010`/`1011`/`1013` marker. Mesh, polyface, and MLINE paths
   also need finite-coordinate checks at the extractor boundary, before any
   descriptor or geometry comparison.
3. `hasDwgTypedConversionSidecar()` and the sidecar scanners intentionally
   skip malformed data outside an active group, but the policy is implicit. A
   malformed recognized marker must be distinguished from an absent marker so
   it cannot accidentally select a later valid group or hide data loss.
4. `addHeader()` and `createDimStyle()` avoid the worst inactive-union reads,
   but invalid optional variables are silently ignored. Their accepted type,
   finite-value, version, and default-retention policy needs direct tests.
   The filter's `checkedDimStyleVariable()` map and the low-level DIMSTYLE
   descriptor table currently duplicate knowledge and can drift.
5. `parseInsertAttribSidecar()` and its MText decoders are substantially
   checked, but their malformed-group boundary still needs explicit tests for
   null values, out-of-range integer64 handles, binary payload limits, and a
   malformed group followed by a valid group.

Implementation requirements:

1. Keep the three-state result (`Absent`, `Malformed`, `Valid`) as the only
   raw-variant access boundary. Migrate every recognized `1071`, coordinate,
   string, real, and binary read in the sidecar extractors to it.
2. For integer64 values, widen first, validate the permitted range, and only
   then narrow. Never call a 32-bit accessor merely because the semantic value
   will eventually fit in 32 bits.
3. Make each recognized sidecar parse into local state and return no sidecar on
   malformed storage. Preserve unrelated valid groups, but never let malformed
   state bleed into a later marker.
4. Either centralize the DIMSTYLE field descriptors in a small shared internal
   header or generate the filter's expected-type lookup from the same source as
   the writer table. Keep target-version filtering explicit.
5. Add direct tests for every fixed boundary above, including the inactive-union
   regression. A no-crash assertion alone is insufficient: verify whether the
   source is retained as ordinary fallback, the optional value stays at its
   default, or the export is rejected.

#### P1-L.11e.d: EED result propagation is complete, but record publication is not

The new validators prevent malformed EED/APPDATA from being appended, but they
run after the ordinary record prefix and fields have begun. `dxfRW::write()`'s
`failWrite` lambda closes the stream but leaves the destination path in place,
so a malformed callback can leave a partial DXF file. In addition, many fixed
entity writers call `writeEntity(ent)` and ignore its boolean result; examples
include POINT, LINE, 3DLINE, INSERT, POLYLINE, ATTRIB, and several simple
entities. A failed `writeEntity()` latches `m_writeError`, but the containing
writer can continue emitting geometry, children, or later callback data.

The implementation-ready contract is:

1. Add a pure preflight for the entity-level data that can fail after the
   record has opened. Call it before the first record group where practical;
   keep `writeExtData()` and `writeAppData()` as defensive checks at their own
   APIs.
2. Make every entity writer check `writeEntity()` and return immediately on
   failure. Add null/writer preconditions consistently to the public low-level
   entity entry points. A failed parent must not write VERTEX, ATTRIB, or
   SEQEND children and must not mint or publish a new child identity.
3. Use a temporary output path for a complete DXF write, then close, flush, and
   atomically replace the requested destination only after `EOF`, HANDSEED
   back-patching, and all error latches pass. On failure, remove only the
   temporary path and leave a pre-existing destination unchanged. Preserve the
   current public filename/API behavior.
4. Exercise ASCII and binary DXF `1004` writing with empty, bounded, chunked,
   null, odd-length, non-hex, and oversized payloads. The malformed cases must
   prove both `false` and no published partial destination.
5. Replace the current tests that merely read and delete a failed output with
   assertions that the path is absent, or that an existing sentinel file is
   byte-identical after failure. Add a callback counter proving no later
   success state is published after a required record fails.

#### P1-L.11f: user-BLOCK mesh/polyface admission remains deferred

`writeBlocks()` currently opens a user BLOCK, runs
`reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()`, and writes remaining children. It does not
call `reconstructPolylineSidecars()`. The low-level writer can record compound
children in a pending user-block `entityHandles` list, and existing tests prove
ordinary POLYLINE and INSERT/ATTRIB block behavior, but that is not proof for
filter-generated mesh/polyface compounds.

Implement this in two gates:

1. Extend the writer-only fixture to emit one real mesh and one real polyface
   while `beginBlockContent()` is active. Inspect the completed
   `DwgBlockWriteResult` and require one ordered owner list containing the
   parent, every physical VERTEX, and SEQEND exactly once. Confirm model-space
   and paper-space lists contain none of those handles.
2. Inject a late VERTEX/SEQEND failure while the user block is active. Verify
   rollback of the pending owner list, object map, compound receipt, source and
   generated identity ledgers, and any INSERT reverse reference. Clear the
   one-shot hook, retry, and require one clean owner list without duplicates.
3. Only after both low-level cases pass, invoke
   `reconstructPolylineSidecars(blk, consumed)` immediately after
   `beginBlockContent()` and before `reconstructSingleFrameSidecars()`. The
   active writer owner is authoritative; do not infer ownership from
   `NoHandle`, block name, or a guessed source handle.
4. Add one filter fixture containing a mesh and one containing a polyface in an
   INSERT-referenced user BLOCK. Prove unrelated children remain ordinary,
   sidecar entries enter `consumed` only after compound commit, and failed
   reconstruction rolls back the entire block phase once.
5. Use in-tree readback for AC1015, AC1018, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032, and the
   low-level writer matrix for AC1021 until the public filter exposes that
   format. Name libreDWG/ODA/ezdxf checks as separate external gates.

#### P1-L.8d/P1-L.9e/P1-L.10d: modern DWG receipts remain open

The DataStorage capability and admission ledgers are stronger than the
historical plan states, but they still do not prove the physical output:

1. Add post-pagination section receipts containing canonical section id/order,
   page ids and bounds, encoded/encrypted size, alignment, and immutable byte
   identity. Reconcile them with the final page map after all pages are split.
2. Keep wide opaque record identities on exact same-version raw replay only;
   reject cross-version replay unless a typed converter exists.
3. Reconcile the owner graph after generated and preserved entities are all
   admitted. Check BLOCK_RECORD lists, model/paper ownership, raw custom entity
   owners, and non-owner ACIS links together rather than by family.
4. Finish the one-to-one source-row/frame ledger for ordinary typed/raw objects,
   generated class-backed records, and duplicate source revisions. Aggregate
   counts are not sufficient evidence.

#### P0-L.12e: AC1032 remains an independent release gate

`dwgWriter32` selects AC1032 and its codec but inherits the AC1027 container
and object framing. Shared code may be correct, but inheritance is not proof.
Generate AC1027 and AC1032 fixtures independently and compare header fields,
class records, section descriptors, page limits/alignment, object-map offsets,
HANDSEED, CRCs, and version-gated payload bits. Do not claim R2018
completeness until the differences are either proven intentional by the DWG
specification or covered by an external reader.

2. Close P1-L.11e.d: propagate `writeEntity()` results, stage DXF output
   transactionally, and replace partial-output tests with publication tests.
3. Re-run the model-space mesh/polyface refusal and transaction matrix for

4. Add and pass the low-level user-BLOCK mesh/polyface owner-list and rollback

5. Route mesh/polyface reconstruction through active user-BLOCK context and

6. Complete physical DataStorage section/page receipts and owner-graph

7. Prove AC1032 independently, then advance INSERT/ATTRIB receipt expansion

8. Run qmake6, sanitizer, full filter, GUI open/save, and named external-reader

   opt-in with `--allow-slow`.
