## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1134

This pass followed the public DXF compound emitters into the actual output
stream and checked the generated record boundaries with focused Catch2 tests.
It found that the earlier A-3 handle-map fix had prevented map pollution but
had not corrected the emitted records themselves: `writePolyline()` wrote the
parent entity header for every VERTEX and for SEQEND, and `writeInsert()` used
the parent entity re-entry for ATTRIB/SEQEND. That violates the DXF ownership
graph even when the file remains parseable.

### Implemented in this pass

1. `writeEntity()` now accepts an owner override used only for the current
   record. VERTEX records receive their own allocated handles and a 330 owner
   equal to the POLYLINE handle. ATTRIB records receive their own handles and
   a 330 owner equal to the INSERT handle. The source entity's `parentHandle`
   is not overwritten to achieve this.
2. Added `writeSequenceEnd()`. It allocates a distinct handle, emits the
   SEQEND record, writes the compound parent as code 330 for R2000+, and emits
   the R2000+ sequence-end subclass fields. Synthetic terminators do not enter
   the source-to-minted identity map.
3. `writePolyline()` now uses each actual `DRW_Vertex` child and terminates
   through `writeSequenceEnd(parentHandle)`. `writeInsert()` routes ATTRIB
   children through the INSERT owner and uses the same terminator helper.
4. INSERT preflight now rejects empty/unsafe block names, invalid grid counts,
   null attributes, and unsafe attribute tags before group 0. ATTRIB/ATTDEF
   preflight validates tags, prompts, field-length ranges, and embedded MTEXT.
   All these extra validation exits latch `m_writeError`, so a callback-level
   false result cannot be mistaken for a successful top-level write.
5. Added focused tests for independent compound handles/owners and malformed
   INSERT attribute children. Existing POLYLINE, INSERT, object, HATCH, and
   unsupported-legacy tests remain green in the incremental CMake lane.

### Verification

- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only`: passed after the
  emitter changes.

### Remaining findings after rev 1134

#### P1-L.11e.d1-d: close all public emitter result paths

The unsupported legacy matrix is covered for the principal entity family, but
the complete public declaration list still contains emitters whose null,
version, or unsupported-type exits return false without consistently latching
the writer error. The next audit must cover CAMERA, GEOPOSITIONMARKER,
SECTIONOBJECT, IMAGE, WIPEOUT, POINTCLOUD/EX, NAVISWORKS, SURFACE, and
MULTILEADER, plus the OBJECTS helpers. Every public path needs a deliberate
`Written` or `Failed` result and must propagate every delegated write result.

#### P1-L.11e.d2-d: record-byte transactions are still open

The top-level destination is protected by `DwgDxfOutputTransaction`, and the
compound ownership bug is fixed, but a failed typed record can still leave
bytes in the staging destination until the top-level write aborts. Direct
emitter callers still have no per-record rollback, and `writeBlockRecord()`
still restores the whole allocator after a failed emission. The next design
slice must first prove a stream-sink checkpoint with an in-memory writer, then
wrap simple records and compound records separately. Compound scopes must
keep parent, child, and SEQEND bytes together; a group-0 boundary alone is
not a transaction boundary.

#### P1-L.11e.d3: child payload and callback receipts

POLYLINE and INSERT now emit the correct low-level ownership, but their
parent/child metadata maps and caller-visible handle fields are still
published before the complete sequence is known to succeed. A failed child or
SEQEND write can therefore consume a partial identity plan. The transaction
must stage source mappings, generated handles, and ownership receipts with
the bytes, while retaining consumed allocator values for the remainder of the
top-level write.

#### P1-L.11f-d: registry manifests and version gates

Class/table closure, fallback layer/style exactly-once emission, and late
registration rejection remain incomplete. The new child owner override does
not solve class manifest closure. Build normalized manifests before HEADER,
CLASSES, and TABLES and derive counts/HANDSEED from committed records.

#### P1-L.8d/P1-L.9e/P1-L.10d: physical DataStorage

DataStorage remains represented by logical carrier/decision metadata only.
There is still no version-specific physical section/page serializer or final
receipt binding source identity to immutable bytes, page location, size,
encoding, and CRC. No same-version preservation claim should be made until
that receipt is produced by the final writer.

#### P0-L.12e: independent AC1032 evidence

AC1032 factory selection exists, but an independently inspected emitted file
has not yet verified header, section/page map, object-map offset, classes,
HANDSEED, DataStorage bits, and CRC. External libreDWG/ODA checks remain
evidence items, not passes, when the tools are unavailable.

### Refined next implementation slice

1. Finish the emitter matrix and latch policy for the remaining public
   unsupported/null paths. Add direct tests that assert callback false,
   writer false, no group-0 prefix, and unchanged existing output.
2. Introduce a checked `std::ostream` sink in `dxfWriter` and a nested record
   scope with checkpoint/commit/abort. Keep `std::ofstream` access only in the
   top-level HANDSEED back-patch path. Prove ASCII and binary staging first.
3. Wrap simple entity records, then POLYLINE/INSERT, BLOCK/ENDBLK,
   BLOCK_RECORD, IMAGE/IMAGEDEF, and raw OBJECT replay. Do not use fixed byte
   offsets; the scope must own the bytes and restore the stream state on abort.
4. Add allocator/map staging without rewinding consumed handles. A failed
   record may discard unpublished maps and receipts but must not make its
   attempted handle available to a later record in the same write.
5. Re-run only the changed libdxfrw targets by default; invoke broader
   LibreCAD targets only from an already-warm build directory. Add a dedicated
   test target for the sink and transaction proof so the 900-step application
   link is not required for each codec iteration.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1135

This pass re-audited the complete public DXF writer surface after rev 1134,
including the newer OBJECTS callbacks. The important invariant is now stated
as a callback contract: a public emitter that cannot produce a valid record
must return failure and latch the enclosing `dxfRW::write()` operation. A
successful low-level stream call must also be reflected in the emitter result.
The audit was performed against the current source, not against the earlier
inventory alone.

### Implemented in this pass

1. Closed the remaining entity-side post-preflight failure paths for 3DLINE,
   SHAPE, OLE2FRAME/OLEFRAME, CAMERA, GEOPOSITIONMARKER, SECTIONOBJECT,
   MULTILEADER, WIPEOUT, POINTCLOUD/POINTCLOUDEX, the point-cloud definition
   family, Navisworks records, and SURFACE. Invalid payloads now set
   `m_writeError` before returning false; version gates use the common
   unsupported-write failure path.
2. Added an explicit invalid-kind failure to POINTCLOUDDEFINITION instead of
   silently serializing an invalid enum as the first known record type.
3. Made IMAGE's legacy-version rejection an explicit latched failure. IMAGE
   remains a pointer-returning compatibility API, so the failure result is
   `nullptr` plus the writer latch rather than a bool conversion.
4. Made ELLIPSE return the actual writer status after its R2000+ record is
   emitted. Made MLEADERSTYLE use the same latched unsupported-version policy.
5. Rebuilt the changed libdxfrw core incrementally and reran the focused DXF
   object, image, wipeout, INSERT safety, POLYLINE ownership, and HATCH tests.

- `[dxf][objects][wipeout]`: 4 assertions in 1 test case passed.

### Findings that remain after rev 1135

#### P1-L.11e.d1-e: OBJECTS helper contract is only partly closed

The entity family and the newer typed OBJECTS validators now latch their
direct validation failures, but four structural cases remain. The helpers
`writeBackground`, `writeRenderSettings`, `writeSection`, and `writeDbColor`
accept a caller-provided record name and return false for a null/empty name
without an explicit latch. `writeSortEntsTable` silently skips unresolved
entity handles when a source-to-minted map exists; that can lose sort order
data and must become a deliberate strict failure or an explicitly documented
lossy policy. The callback-facing `writeBlockRecords()`/`writeEntities()`
interfaces are void, so their admission and failure receipts still rely on
the global latch. These are separate from ordinary payload validation and
should be fixed with a small helper-level test matrix.

#### P1-L.11e.d1-f: allocator exceptions still cross direct emitter boundaries

`writeImage`, `writePlotSettings`, `writeLayout`, APPID emission, and several
typed object callbacks call `HandleAllocator::next()` directly. The top-level
writer catches exceptions, but a direct callback caller can still observe an
exception after bytes or metadata have been started. The eventual record
scope must convert allocator exhaustion to a failed record, consume attempted
handles for the rest of the top-level write, and publish no maps or reactor
edges from that record. Do not restore the entire allocator as the current
IMAGE and BLOCK_RECORD paths still do on some failures.

#### P1-L.11e.d2-e: no per-record byte rollback

The top-level `DwgDxfOutputTransaction` protects the destination path, but a
failed direct emitter leaves its partial record in the staging stream until
the whole file is aborted. This is especially visible in POLYLINE/INSERT,
IMAGE/IMAGEDEF, BLOCK/ENDBLK, and raw replay. A stream checkpoint must stage
bytes, generated handles, source mappings, ownership lists, caller metadata,
and reactor edges as one unit. Group 0 is not a sufficient transaction
boundary because compound children and SEQEND belong to the parent receipt.

#### P1-L.11f-e: registry manifests still depend on callback order

The current CLASSES/TABLES output is improved but is not yet an immutable
pre-write manifest. Late custom-class registration, duplicate case-folded
names, conflicting class numbers, fallback layer/style emission, and final
HANDSEED derivation still need one normalized identity pass before HEADER,
CLASSES, and TABLES. The manifest must include typed and raw carriers and
reject late additions rather than producing a structurally plausible but
incomplete file.

#### P1-L.8d/P1-L.9e/P1-L.10d and P0-L.12e remain unchanged

Physical version-specific DataStorage serialization/receipts and independent
AC1032 evidence are still open. Logical metadata and typed fields are not a
physical section/page receipt. AC1032 completion still requires independent
inspection of header, section/page map, object map, classes, HANDSEED,
DataStorage bits, checksums/CRCs, plus named external-reader results when
those tools are available.

### Refined implementation sub-plans after rev 1135

#### Slice 1: finish direct emitter failure semantics

1. Add a private `failDxfWrite()` helper returning false and latching
   `m_writeError`; use it for invalid record-name arguments and all remaining
   helper-only validation exits.
2. Decide and document `writeSortEntsTable` behavior: strict failure when a
   referenced source handle cannot be resolved, with a test for no partial
   sort entries; do not silently drop the reference.
3. Add focused tests for each public helper's null/name/version/invalid-kind
   path. Assert callback false, top-level false, and no target publication.
4. Add an allocator-exhaustion test through IMAGE and one typed OBJECTS path;
   verify no exception escapes the direct emitter and the attempted handle is
   not reused during the same top-level write.

#### Slice 2: prove the record-scope mechanism

1. Introduce a small ostream checkpoint/sink abstraction with ASCII and binary
   tests. It must support begin, append, commit, abort, and stream error
   recovery without hard-coded offsets.
2. Wrap one simple entity and one typed OBJECTS record first. Stage the
   source-handle map and caller-handle mutation with the bytes.
3. Extend the scope to POLYLINE/INSERT, BLOCK/ENDBLK, BLOCK_RECORD,
   IMAGE/IMAGEDEF/reactor, and raw OBJECT/section replay. A failed child or
   SEQEND aborts the complete compound receipt.
4. Remove allocator snapshot/restore only after the scope proves that failed
   records consume handles but publish no identity/ownership metadata.

#### Slice 3: close registries and physical evidence

1. Build the immutable class/table manifest before writing HEADER/CLASSES.
2. Add duplicate, case-variant, late-registration, and HANDSEED tests.
3. Implement version-specific DataStorage section/page serialization and bind
   every preserved source to a final immutable page receipt.
4. Add AC1027 and AC1032 evidence fixtures, with explicit skipped status for
   unavailable libreDWG/ODA tools; never treat unavailable external checks as
   passes.

### Execution policy

Use `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test-file ... --test ... --no-discover` for
the changed Catch2 source and `--changed --compile-only` for production edits.
Do not invoke a cold broad LibreCAD target during each codec iteration. Run
qmake6, sanitizers, full tests, and external readers only at the end of each
completed slice or when a changed contract crosses that toolchain boundary.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1136

This follow-up rechecked the rev 1135 conclusions against the current
`libdxfrw` writer, the LibreCAD filter, the DataStorage carrier, and the
focused DXF tests. It also checked that the plan did not describe a missing
implementation where the code already has one. The result is a status
correction plus a narrower set of implementation-ready next slices.

### Completed since rev 1135

1. Added `dxfRW::failDxfWrite()` as the single false-and-latch helper for
   helper-level structural failures.
2. `writeBackground()`, `writeRenderSettings()`, `writeSection()`, and
   `writeDbColor()` now latch null and empty record-name failures before
   emitting a group-0 record.
3. `writeSortEntsTable()` now fails when an active source-to-minted entity
   map cannot resolve a nonzero entity source handle. This prevents a
   successful-looking file from silently losing draw-order entries.
4. Replaced the remaining DXF model-space fallback literal in that writer
   with `DRW::DxfModelSpaceBlockRecordHandle`, keeping owner identity in the
   shared named-constant table.
5. Added a helper matrix covering null and empty names for all four public
   OBJECTS helpers. Each case asserts the callback result is false, the
   enclosing write is false, and a pre-existing destination remains intact.
   Added a SORTENTSTABLE regression proving an unresolved remapped entity
   handle fails without publishing the output.

### Verification for rev 1136

- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only`: passed; the changed
  libdxfrw archive and filter compile-check were rebuilt incrementally.
- `[dxf][objects][writer][safety]`: 28 assertions in 2 test cases passed.
- `[dxf][sortents]`: 40 assertions in 4 test cases passed.
- `git diff --check` for the touched codec, test, and roadmap files: passed.
- No broad application rebuild was used; the warm codec target was sufficient
  for this change.

### Corrected implementation status

#### Direct DXF emitter contract: substantially closed, not transactional

The audited public entity and typed OBJECTS validation exits now use a
deliberate false result and latch policy. This closes the direct helper gap
identified in rev 1135, but it does not make a direct emitter atomic. The
remaining direct-boundary problem is allocator exhaustion: `writeImage()`,
`writePlotSettings()`, `writeLayout()`, APPID emission, and several typed
OBJECTS paths still call `HandleAllocator::next()` directly. A later
allocator wrapper must catch exhaustion at the emitter boundary and preserve
monotonic consumption during the active top-level write.

#### SORTENTSTABLE policy: entity resolution is strict, sort resolution remains
explicit work

An entity source that is nonzero but absent from the active remap map now
fails. The paired sort handle still has a compatibility fallback: an absent
sort source is emitted verbatim, while a zero source falls back to the
resolved entity. Before transaction work is declared complete, establish
whether the paired sort values are always entity identities in this model. If
they are, unresolved nonzero sort sources must fail or resolve to the already
resolved entity; if they are an independent opaque ordering identity, retain
the current behavior and document it. The existing GROUP path intentionally
skips unresolved members and needs the same explicit lossy-policy decision.

#### DataStorage: physical container exists; physical receipt proof does not

The earlier wording that there is no physical DataStorage serializer was too
strong. The current implementation has all of the following pieces:

- `drw_datastorage.cpp` validates the section signature, indexes, segments,
  schemas, record ranges, blob pages, and retained payloads.
- `dwgReader18`/`dwgReader21` and `dwgRW` expose raw DataStorage sections and
  object presence bits to the filter.
- `RS_FilterDXFRW` builds a typed/raw replay plan, source-row keys, admission
  records, object/frame commits, and section commit receipts.
- `dwgWriter18::finalize()` and `dwgWriter21::finalize()` physically rebuild
  section descriptors, split payloads into bounded pages, generate section
  maps/page maps, and calculate their container checksums. AC1027 and AC1032
  select the version-specific writer factories.

The real open item is the binding between the filter ledger and the final
physical result. No receipt currently exposes the final section id, page id,
file offset, stored size, decoded size, encoding, and checksum for each
replayed source row. The plan must therefore add post-finalize physical
inspection, not another parser or another logical carrier.

#### Version coverage: factory coverage is broader than evidence coverage

Readers currently select dedicated implementations across the supported DWG
families, including pre-R13, R13/R14/R2000, R2004, R2007, R2010, R2013, and
R2018. Writers accept AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032;
AC1027 and AC1032 reuse the newer page/container family with version-gated
payload encoders. This is source-level coverage, not proof that every
version's emitted bytes are accepted by an independent reader. AC1032 still
needs an independently inspected fixture, especially for inherited R2013
container logic, maintenance-version gates, string streams, class framing,
DataStorage flags, and page-map checksums.

#### Outer publication versus record atomicity

`DwgDxfOutputTransaction` protects the destination path for both DWG and DXF:
failed top-level writes do not replace an existing file. DWG additionally has
compound-write checkpoints used by `dwgRW` for object/entity frames. DXF still
uses a concrete `std::ofstream*` sink and has no byte checkpoint around a
direct record. These are different guarantees and must remain separate in the
plan: the next DXF work is a record-scope mechanism, not another destination
rename helper.

### Remaining findings, ordered for implementation

#### P1-L.11e.d1-f: allocator-safe direct boundaries

Centralize fresh-handle allocation behind a writer method that returns a
checked result and latches failure. Apply it first to the direct paths listed
above, then to image reactors, dictionaries, groups, and table fallback
records. A failed allocation must not restore the allocator to a prior value;
it may discard unpublished metadata, but all attempted values remain consumed
until the top-level write resets generated state. Add a deterministic test
hook rather than relying on a process-wide maximum-handle fixture.

#### P1-L.11e.d2-f: DXF record sink and rollback

Add a small writer sink/checkpoint abstraction under `src/intern` with no
format-specific byte offsets. The first proof should cover ASCII and binary
`writeString()` calls, stream failure, begin/commit/abort, and nested scopes.
Then wrap one simple ENTITY and one OBJECTS record. The scope must own bytes,
caller-handle mutations, newly generated handles, source-to-minted mappings,
and any reactor/ownership edges that become visible only after commit.

#### P1-L.11e.d3-f: compound and raw replay scopes

Extend the same mechanism to POLYLINE/INSERT, BLOCK/ENDBLK, BLOCK_RECORD,
IMAGE/IMAGEDEF/reactor, and raw OBJECT/section replay. A child or SEQEND
failure aborts the complete compound receipt. Raw DXF replay must either stage
the complete raw object or clearly reject a partial direct replay; it must not
leave a valid group-0 prefix after returning false.

#### P1-L.11f-e: immutable class/table registry

Replace callback-order assumptions with one pre-write manifest containing
typed classes, raw class carriers, fixed structural records, fallback
layer/style records, and all source-handle reservations. Normalize names for
duplicate detection, reject conflicting class identities and late additions,
derive class instance counts from committed receipts, and calculate HANDSEED
from the final committed handle set. Add case-variant, class-number collision,
late-registration, fallback-exactly-once, and HANDSEED tests.

#### P1-L.10d/P1-L.12c: physical DataStorage receipts

Expose a writer-side finalize report or a deterministic parser of the emitted
file that maps each accepted DataStorage source row to its physical section
and page receipts. Validate page boundaries, physical versus logical sizes,
encoding normalization, page checksums, section-map references, and object
presence bits together. Keep same-version raw replay as the only preservation
claim until this report is validated; cross-version replay remains rejected
unless a typed converter exists.

#### P0-L.12e: AC1032 external evidence

Generate a minimal AC1027 and AC1032 corpus with a line, a compound entity, a
custom OBJECT, a class collision candidate, and a DataStorage-bearing object.
Inspect header/version, class and object framing, HANDSEED, page maps, CRCs,
presence bits, and ownership with the in-tree reader. Run libreDWG and ODA
when available, recording unavailable tools as skipped rather than passed.
Any inherited AC1027 behavior used by AC1032 must have a version-specific
assertion before the roadmap can claim AC1032 writer completeness.

### Implementation sequence after rev 1136

1. Replace the remaining direct allocator calls with a checked internal helper
   and add deterministic exhaustion tests. Resolve the paired SORTENTSTABLE
   sort-handle policy and document GROUP's unresolved-member policy.
2. Prove the DXF sink with focused in-memory tests, then add a record scope to
   one ENTITY and one OBJECTS helper. Keep the existing outer output
   transaction unchanged.
3. Add staged allocator, caller-mutation, source-map, ownership, and reactor
   state to the scope; extend it to compound entities, blocks, image records,
   and raw replay only after the simple proof passes.
4. Freeze class/table manifests before HEADER/CLASSES/TABLES and derive
   counts and HANDSEED from committed records. Do not combine registry changes
   with physical DataStorage changes in one debugging slice.
5. Add physical DataStorage finalize receipts and emitted-file inspection,
   followed by AC1027/AC1032 evidence fixtures and external-reader checks.

### Fast verification policy

For a production codec change, run
`scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only`. For one test source, build and run only its mapped
target with `--test-file`, then use `--test-only` for repeated selectors. Keep
slow corpus, fixture, external-reader, sanitizer, qmake6, and full LibreCAD
tests out of the inner loop; run them after a complete implementation slice
or when the changed contract crosses that boundary. The new sink tests should
live in a small libdxfrw target so they do not require the cold application
link.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1137

This pass implemented the first part of the rev 1136 execution sequence and
rechecked the result against all current DXF writer call sites. The important
distinction is now explicit: the codec has a byte-staging primitive, but it
does not yet claim full record transactions.

### Completed in this pass

1. Added `dxfRW::allocateDxfHandle()` as the one checked boundary around
   `HandleAllocator::next()`. All production DXF allocation sites now use it,
   including table records, IMAGE/IMAGEDEF reactors, BLOCK_RECORD planning,
   OBJECTS dictionaries and groups, PLOTSETTINGS, and LAYOUT. The existing
   ENTITY and SEQEND paths were migrated to the same helper as well.
2. Changed the public `dxfRW::allocHandle()` helper to return zero on
   exhaustion instead of allowing an allocator exception to escape. The
   structural collision-remap path in `RS_FilterDXFRW` now detects zero,
   reports the failure, destroys the unpublished writer, and refuses to start
   output.
3. Removed allocator rewinds from IMAGE and BLOCK_RECORD failure paths. A
   value consumed during the active write remains consumed until the top-level
   write resets generated state; retrying cannot silently reissue a handle.
4. Generalized the low-level DXF writer sink from `std::ofstream*` to
   `std::ostream*`. This preserves file output and lets the writer operate on
   an in-memory staging stream. The `$HANDSEED` back-patch now uses the same
   generic stream type.
5. Added `DxfWriterRecordScope`, an RAII byte scope supporting commit, abort,
   nested scopes, stream failure detection, and restoration of writer-local
   error state. `writePoint()` and the typed background OBJECTS emitter are
   the first production users.
6. Added deterministic tests for scope commit/abort/nesting and handle
   exhaustion through an ENTITY path and a typed OBJECTS path. The tests use a
   reservation at `UINT32_MAX - 1` during the write, so they do not require a
   large corpus or a long allocation loop.

### Corrected scope status

#### Allocator boundary: closed for direct `next()` use

The only remaining `m_handleAllocator.next()` occurrences in
`libdxfrw.cpp` are inside `allocateDxfHandle()` or explanatory comments.
Allocation failure is converted to a false result and `m_writeError` during
an active write. A pre-write collision-remap failure is handled by the filter
before `dxfRW::write()` can reset the per-write latch. The allocator remains
monotonic on failed records; the next top-level attempt begins from the
documented generated-state reset.

#### Byte scope: proof exists, full transaction does not

`DxfWriterRecordScope` stages the encoded bytes and restores the low-level
writer's stream and error latch on abort. It does not snapshot a caller's
entity handle, `sourceHandleToMintedMap`, ambiguous-source set, block maps,
image-definition ownership, or any other dxfRW state. A commit failure after
the destination stream accepts no bytes can therefore still leave caller
state changed. This is intentional intermediate infrastructure, not closure
of the no-partial-record invariant.

The next implementation must introduce a dxfRW-level record checkpoint around
the scope. It should snapshot only the state that can be mutated by the
wrapped operation, retain monotonic allocator consumption, and restore the
snapshot when `commit()` fails or the emitter returns false. The checkpoint
must distinguish a pre-existing source mapping from a mapping created by the
record, and it must not erase mappings belonging to previously committed
records.

#### Current production coverage of the scope

The first scope users are deliberately small: POINT is a single ordinary
ENTITY and BACKGROUND is a typed OBJECTS record with no child stream. The
following remain direct-to-parent and must not be described as transactional:
LINE and other simple entities, all table entries, raw OBJECT/section replay,
POLYLINE/INSERT with child records, BLOCK/ENDBLK, BLOCK_RECORD, IMAGE/IMAGEDEF
/reactor, GROUP, and the remaining typed OBJECTS records. The generic
`std::ostream` contract is ready for those migrations, but state rollback and
compound ownership rules must be implemented before broad wrapping.

### Refined next slices

1. Add a dxfRW record checkpoint for handle mutations, entity handle fields,
   source maps, and newly visible metadata. Prove it with POINT on a failing
   destination and with a false-returning typed OBJECTS record.
2. Wrap one table record and one raw OBJECT after the checkpoint proof. Then
   extend to all simple ENTITY emitters and typed OBJECTS records, keeping
   callback return values and the outer `DwgDxfOutputTransaction` unchanged.
3. Define compound scopes for POLYLINE/INSERT, BLOCK/ENDBLK, and
   IMAGE/IMAGEDEF/reactor. Child failures must abort the parent byte scope and
   remove every uncommitted ownership edge while preserving consumed handles.
4. Resolve the independent SORTENTSTABLE sort-handle policy and document the
   intentionally lossy GROUP unresolved-member policy before applying strict
   raw replay rules.
5. Freeze class/table manifests before HEADER/CLASSES/TABLES, derive counts and
   HANDSEED from committed records, then implement physical DataStorage
   receipts and AC1027/AC1032 evidence fixtures.

### Remaining transaction gap after rev 1138

`DxfWriterRecordScope` owns encoded bytes and the POINT-specific guard owns
the first caller-state set. The scope still does not automatically cover
table-map insertion, BLOCK_RECORD pending vectors, image-definition pointers,
compound child ownership, raw replay, or typed OBJECTS metadata. In
particular, a false return from a direct table emitter can still leave bytes
in its parent staging stream when the caller has not wrapped it. The next
slice must replace the POINT-specific guard with a reusable dxfRW checkpoint
whose tracked state is explicit and whose rollback is non-allocating.

The checkpoint must also distinguish nested ownership: an inner committed
record becomes part of its outer scope, while an inner aborted record must not
remove mappings or metadata already committed by an earlier sibling. Handle
allocation is the exception to rollback: consumed values remain tombstones
for the active attempt and are reset only at the next top-level write.

### Refined implementation order

1. Extract the POINT state guard into a reusable dxfRW record-state scope and
   add an injected failing output stream test for commit failure. Keep stream
   staging and state rollback separate so either layer can be audited.
2. Apply the reusable scope to one table emitter and one raw OBJECT, including
   insertion/removal of any maps they update. Add tests that inspect both
   destination bytes and state after false returns.
3. Wrap all simple ENTITY and typed OBJECTS emitters, then compound
   POLYLINE/INSERT, BLOCK/ENDBLK, and IMAGE/IMAGEDEF/reactor operations. Use
   parent scopes for child records and close ownership edges only at parent
   commit.
4. Resolve SORTENTSTABLE sort-handle semantics and make class/table
   registration immutable before HEADER/CLASSES/TABLES. Only after those
   contracts are stable should DataStorage physical receipts and AC1032
   independent evidence be added.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1139

This pass compared the recorded transaction gaps with the current writer
call graph after the raw replay change. The roadmap needed correction before
the next implementation slice.

### Findings and corrections

1. Raw OBJECT and raw SECTION replay are no longer direct-to-parent. Both now
   use `DxfWriterRecordScope`; the previous statement that raw replay remained
   unscoped was stale and is corrected here. The scope is byte-atomic, but raw
   object replay still needs a dxfRW state checkpoint if handle remapping or
   source maps are changed during emission.
2. Table emitters already use both the byte scope and the reusable
   `RecordStateScope`. The remaining state risk is not table bytes but the
   signed `int` storage used by `lineTypesMap`, `textStyleMap`, and `blockMap`.
   The allocator and raw carriers are 32-bit unsigned; converting a valid
   handle above `INT_MAX` to `int` is implementation-defined and can later
   turn a valid reference into a negative or truncated lookup result. The
   implementation slice must use an unsigned handle type through lookup and
   filter consumers, or reject the full high-bit range before any cast. The
   preferred fix is the unsigned type because the public handle contract is
   already 32-bit.
3. `writeObjects()` allocates image/group handles and deletes image-definition
   pointers after emission. Per-object scopes can protect bytes, but retryable
   state rollback cannot safely restore those pointers after deletion. The
   object phase needs a parent scope and delayed ownership release; it must not
   pretend that a local byte scope alone provides retry semantics.
4. The simple OBJECTS writers are mostly non-mutating and can be wrapped with
   byte scopes independently. This is a low-risk way to close partial-record
   output before tackling IMAGE/IMAGEDEF, dictionaries, GROUP, and compound
   entities. Each wrapper must check its existing boolean return paths and
   commit only after extdata and stream status succeed.
5. The existing focused suite proves scope nesting and allocator exhaustion,
   but it does not prove a parent-stream write failure. Add a small streambuf
   that fails after a configurable byte count and verify that `commit()` leaves
   the parent bytes unchanged and latches the writer error. Keep this test in
   the narrow DXF object target.

### Revised implementation slice

1. Change the DXF writing-context handle maps and their public consumers to
   `std::uint32_t`; add a high-bit regression that writes a line type, text
   style, block record, and dependent DIMSTYLE reference without signed
   conversion.
2. Add byte scopes to the non-mutating typed OBJECTS family and test one
   malformed extdata case plus one stream-failure case. Do not delete or move
   image-definition ownership in this slice.
3. Add a parent state/byte scope around the OBJECTS phase, then move image
   definition release after successful commit. Preserve monotonic handle
   consumption across aborts and retries.
4. Extend the state checkpoint to compound ENTITY children and ownership maps;
   only then migrate POLYLINE, INSERT, BLOCK, and IMAGE/IMAGEDEF to nested
   record scopes.
5. Freeze class/table manifests, then proceed to physical DataStorage receipts
   and independent AC1027/AC1032 validation.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1140

This pass implemented and verified the first two corrections from rev 1139,
then re-read the affected call graph to avoid overstating the transaction
guarantee.

### Implemented

1. The DXF writing context now stores `lineTypesMap`, `textStyleMap`, and
   `blockMap` values as `std::uint32_t`. Their public lookup functions and
   LibreCAD filter consumers use `DRW::NoHandle` rather than `-1`. A high-bit
   regression writes a line type above `0x80000000` and confirms that its
   dependent DIMSTYLE references the same full-width handle.
2. `writeSun`, `writeScale`, `writeDictionaryVar`, and
   `writeRasterVariables` now stage their complete OBJECTS records and commit
   only after the existing extdata and stream checks succeed. The existing
   BACKGROUND writer and raw replay paths remain staged as well.
3. `writeObjects()` is now a parent byte/state transaction. It keeps all
   typed/raw/named OBJECTS bytes unpublished until the phase succeeds and
   destroys `DRW_ImageDef` carriers only after commit. An aborted phase leaves
   those carriers available for a retry; consumed handles remain monotonic.
4. The low-level scope test now uses a rejecting parent stream. It confirms
   that a failed parent write latches the writer error and publishes no bytes.

### Corrected status

The unsigned lookup fix closes the identified narrowing defect. It does not
make the older `RS_FilterDXFRW::findLineTypeHandleToWrite()` API binary-stable
for callers that explicitly depended on a signed `-1`; the source-level
contract is intentionally changed to the codec's actual 32-bit handle domain.
The four new OBJECTS scopes are record-atomic, but the rest of the heterogeneous
OBJECTS family is covered by the parent phase scope rather than individual
record scopes. This is sufficient for published-file atomicity and avoids
claiming per-object retry semantics where image/dictionary ownership still
needs a dedicated design.

## Deep codebase review 2026-08-30, rev 1141

This pass compares the current implementation, including the rev 1140
changes, with the remaining roadmap claims. The review covered `dxfRW`,
`DxfWriterRecordScope`, `dwgReader18`, `dwgReader21`, `DwgObjectFrame`,
`dwgWriter15`, `dwgWriter18`, `dwgWriter21`, `dwgRW`, and
`RS_FilterDXFRW`. It corrects the implementation order where the previous
plan treated a logical guarantee as a physical one.

### Status corrections

1. The DXF entity boundary mechanism is already implemented through
   `DxfEntityBoundary` and `m_hasPendingEntityBoundary`. The first BLOCK
   entity is no longer known to be unconditionally dropped. The remaining
   work is formal state-machine testing and error propagation, not a wholesale
   parser rewrite.
2. `writeObjects()` has an outer byte transaction and its image-definition
   deletion is delayed until successful commit. This protects destination
   publication, but it does not make every child record independently
   retryable and its state snapshot is expensive rather than a complete
   mutation journal.
3. The DXF class vector is still emitted without writer-side identity
   validation or a frozen late-registration boundary. DWG class manifest
   preparation is stronger, but that does not establish equivalent DXF or
   AC1032 conformance.
4. DataStorage replay receipts currently prove a logical source/carrier
   ledger. They do not yet identify the physical DWG section, page, offset,
   encoded size, decoded size, and checksum that carried each row.
5. `dwgWriter32` inherits the R2018-family writer implementation. Factory
   coverage for AC1032 is present, but independent AC1032 conformance evidence
   is still missing.
6. The R2007+ reader still treats several page and payload CRC/checksum
   mismatches as warnings. This is not equivalent to the roadmap's strict
   malformed-input contract and requires an explicit strict/tolerant policy.

### Findings grouped by implementation area

#### DXF writer session, scope, and ownership

1. `RecordStateScope` in `src/libdxfrw.cpp` copies the complete writing
   context, maps, pending block-record vector, and scalar state. It is used at
   record granularity, so allocation and copy cost can be paid for every
   table record. A future checkpoint must be a mutation journal or checkpoint
   token, not another full snapshot. Log map insert/replace/erase operations,
   restore only mutations after the token, checkpoint vector sizes, and make
   rollback `noexcept` and allocation-free. The journal itself may allocate
   while recording; that limitation must be explicit and tested. Nested
   commits must retain changes within their parent, while an inner abort must
   not erase a previous sibling's committed state.
2. `DxfWriterRecordScope::commit()` appends staged bytes to its parent. A
   generic `ostream` cannot truncate bytes that a parent accepted before a
   later short write. The API must document that a child can report append
   failure and poison its ancestor, while the outer file/phase transaction is
   the publication boundary. Give commit failure a distinct state so the
   destructor cannot accidentally restore a failed scope, and test both a
   rejecting stream and a partial-write stream.
3. Top-level `dxfRW::write()` clears `blockMap`, `textStyleMap`, pending block
   records, and source-handle remap state, but does not clear
   `m_writingContext.lineTypesMap`. Reusing one codec with a different
   linetype order can therefore return a stale DIMSTYLE linetype handle. Add
   the missing reset or make every derived map part of one per-write context,
   then test success-success, failure-success, and failure-failure reuse.
4. `currHandle` and its checkpoint are still signed `int`, while block-record
   handles are now unsigned 32-bit. Assigning a high-bit handle and computing
   `currHandle + 1` or `+ 2` can be implementation-defined or undefined. Use
   `std::uint32_t` throughout and a checked offset helper shared with
   block-record allocation. Add a high-bit BLOCK/ENDBLK test.
5. Structural writes at the start of `dxfRW::write()` and in table/block
   framing often ignore individual boolean returns and check only the sticky
   writer error later. Publication safety is already supplied by the outer
   output transaction, but callbacks can continue after the sink has failed.
   Centralize boundary writes and short-circuit after each structural failure
   so no later callback mutates derived maps or ownership state.
6. Void `DRW_Interface::writeBlocks()` and `writeEntities()` callbacks cannot
   report a per-record failure directly. Section staging alone cannot enforce
   child semantics. Add compound scopes first: POLYLINE with VERTEX/SEQEND,
   INSERT with ATTRIB/SEQEND, and BLOCK with its prior ENDBLK, header, child
   entities, and final auto-close. Require exactly one block close and restore
   `writingBlock`, `currHandle`, block maps, and pending records on failure.
7. The top-level reset needs an explicit `resetDxfWriteSession()` contract.
   Derived maps, error flags, reservation failure, and per-write generation
   state are reset; persistent input configuration such as classes, raw
   sections, root dictionaries, named objects, groups, and remap policy is
   retained. Delayed `DRW_ImageDef` ownership must also define whether a
   failed write can be retried without re-emitting or double-consuming an
   image carrier.
8. In the non-collecting `writeBlockRecord()` path, bytes can be emitted before
   `blockMap` is updated. If metadata insertion fails or duplicate handling
   changes, the stream and lookup state diverge. Update metadata before bytes
   inside a rollback scope, or always stage the record and map mutation
   together; reject late records after collection has closed.
9. Add writer-side DXF class preflight before HEADER/CLASSES output. Validate
   safe text and ranges, case-insensitive `recName` uniqueness, class-name
   identity, duplicate/conflicting definitions, nonnegative instance counts,
   and the policy for counts that do not match emitted objects. Freeze the
   registry after preflight and reject late registration. Keep the existing
   filter-level class deduplication, but do not rely on it for direct
   `dxfRW` callers.

#### DXF parser state and child semantics

10. Complete tests around the existing pending-boundary cursor: consume each
    pending code-0 token exactly once; reject ENDSEC and ENDBLK in the wrong
    context; distinguish an empty code-0 value from “no pending token”; retain
    the first BLOCK entity; preserve the first group on raw custom entities;
    and never append a failed ATTRIB, VERTEX, or SEQEND child.

#### DWG framing and physical integrity

11. Define CRC policy by layer. Header, section-map, and page-map integrity
    failures should be hard parse failures. Payload CRC/checksum failures must
    either be hard failures in the default strict mode or be accepted only by
    an explicit tolerant mode with a visible parse report. Do not leave the
    current warning-only behavior undocumented.
12. `DwgObjectFrame` uses a 256 MiB body limit while container safety and
    writer limits are larger. Either share a version-specific frame limit or
    make the writer refuse output that its own reader cannot consume. Its
    `int32_t` CRC/read offsets also constrain large files even where container
    offsets are unsigned 64-bit. Remove that signed API limit or document and
    test the supported file-size ceiling.
13. Object-frame CRC coverage is currently centralized as if one rule applied
    to every R13+ frame family. Verify the exact coverage and seed for R13,
    R2000, R2004, and R2007+ against versioned fixtures; page integrity and
    object-frame integrity are separate checks and must not be conflated.

#### DataStorage and version evidence

14. Add a post-finalize `DwgPhysicalSectionReport` or a deterministic parser
    of the emitted bytes. Bind each DataStorage source row and generation to
    its actual section id, page id, file offset, stored size, uncompressed
    size, encoding, and checksum. Use the existing raw-section writer rather
    than inventing a new DataStorage format. Only after this binding succeeds
    may AC1027 same-version replay be called physically preserved.
15. Gate AC1027 and AC1032 separately. For each version, exercise minimal and
    feature-rich files and inspect version bytes, header, page/section maps,
    object map, class section, HANDSEED, object-frame CRCs, and DataStorage
    presence bits. Use the in-tree reader plus libreDWG/ODA when installed;
    record unavailable external readers as skipped evidence, never as a pass.
    Include wrong-codec, missing/duplicate-page, truncation, checksum/CRC, and
    invalid DataStorage-bit cases.

### Ready-to-implement sub-plans

#### P0: close concrete correctness gaps

1. Clear `lineTypesMap` in the per-write reset and add reuse tests with
   reordered linetypes and DIMSTYLE references.
2. Convert `currHandle` and checkpoint state to `std::uint32_t`; add checked
   `base + delta` handling and high-bit BLOCK/ENDBLK coverage.
3. Add direct-DXF class preflight, duplicate/conflict tests, registry freeze,
   and late-registration failure behavior.
4. Make all three items visible in the coverage inventory and run only the
   affected warm test targets first.

#### P1: transactional writer core

1. Define the scope failure state and partial-parent-stream contract, then add
   rejecting and partial-write tests.
2. Replace full `RecordStateScope` copies with a journal/checkpoint design;
   prove allocation-free `noexcept` rollback and nested scope behavior.
3. Add `resetDxfWriteSession()` and retry tests for success-success,
   failure-success, and failure-failure, including image-definition policy.
4. Move BLOCK_RECORD metadata mutation into the same state/byte transaction as
   its bytes and reject late collection mutations.

#### P2: compound records and parser proof

1. Add parent scopes and status propagation for POLYLINE, INSERT, and BLOCK
   child records, including failed ATTRIB/VERTEX/SEQEND fixtures.
2. Centralize structural boundary writes and stop callbacks immediately after
   a sink error.
3. Complete pending-boundary/state-machine tests before considering a parser
   cursor rewrite.
4. Add section staging only after compound ownership and callback semantics
   are proven.

#### P3: strict DWG integrity

1. Define strict versus tolerant parse policy and report fields; make strict
   mode the default for malformed-input tests.
2. Align frame/body/offset limits across readers and writers, or make output
   refusal explicit at the reader limit.
3. Add version-specific object-frame and page-integrity golden fixtures for
   AC1012 through AC1032 where the framing rules differ.

#### P4: physical DataStorage and release gates

1. Produce physical section/page receipts after final section layout and bind
   them to logical DataStorage rows.
2. Test same-version AC1027 replay and explicit cross-version rejection when
   no typed converter exists.
3. Run the independent AC1027/AC1032 matrix and retain external-tool
   availability in the report.

### Incremental verification policy

Use the warm `build/dwg-fast` tree and
`scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only` after each source slice.
Run one focused selector at a time because the test targets share the same
static archive. Keep slow corpus, sanitizer, qmake6, and external-reader
checks for the end of each P-level slice; use `--skip-slow` during iteration
and run the explicitly selected slow cases only at the release gate. Do not
describe a roadmap item as complete from compilation alone: record the
focused test result, malformed-input result, and, for DWG, the version/tool
matrix separately.

### Review result

No new tests were run during this plan-only audit. The rev 1140 focused
results remain valid as recorded above; rerun them after the next source edit.
The next implementation action is P0, followed by the journal and compound
scope work. Physical DataStorage receipts and independent AC1032 evidence
remain release-gate work, not implied by the current logical ledger or writer
factory coverage.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1148): boundary closure, TABLES publication, and DWG evidence

This is the newest authoritative reconciliation with the live source tree. It
supersedes rev 1147; earlier sections remain historical evidence and may
contain intentionally stale next-step text. The shared worktree contains
unrelated changes and generated build output, so this revision claims only the
files and behavior listed here.

### Implemented since rev 1147

1. `setEntityBoundary()` now clears both `nextentity` and
   `m_hasPendingEntityBoundary` when called with a nonzero code. Failed record
   reads and end-of-input in `readEntityBoundary()` and
   `consumeEntityFooter()` clear the same state. An empty code-0 value remains
   a staged but invalid boundary and is rejected by classification.
2. Every previously bare entity-parser call to
   `setEntityBoundary(code)` now checks for `DxfEntityBoundary::Error` and
   returns `BAD_READ_ENTITIES`. There are no remaining exact unchecked calls
   in `libdxfrw.cpp`; callers that need `NextEntity`, `EndSection`, or
   `EndBlock` retain explicit result handling.
3. Focused boundary coverage now rejects a non-code-0 record at ENTITIES
   dispatch and verifies that no line callback occurs. Existing malformed
   entity and block selectors still cover empty boundaries, wrong-context
   terminators, child terminators, and ENDBLK footer validation.
4. The six direct ordinary DXF writers identified in the prior inventory now
   use `EntityRecordScope`: LIGHT, CAMERA, GEOPOSITIONMARKER, SECTION, MESH,
   and SHAPE. `writePoint()` already has an explicit local state and byte
   transaction and is not an unguarded path. POLYLINE, INSERT, BLOCKS, and
   OBJECTS retain their compound or section transactions.
5. Several writer-side normalization mutations have been removed. ELLIPSE
   axis correction, HATCH/MPOLYGON loop and edge counts, LWPOLYLINE vertex
   count, and dimension type flags are now derived in local values. The source
   state regression currently proves ELLIPSE and dimension preservation; the
   remaining geometry families still need direct snapshot coverage.

### Codebase findings that change the next slice

1. `writeTables()` still has no local `RecordStateScope` or
   `DxfWriterRecordScope`. It writes the complete TABLES section directly and
   invokes callbacks for VPORT, LTYPE, LAYER, STYLE, VIEW, UCS, APPID,
   DIMSTYLE, and legacy BLOCK_RECORD output. Its fallback table-entry calls
   currently ignore the boolean result of `writeVport()`, `writeLayer()`,
   `writeTextstyle()`, and `writeDimstyle()`; callback phases do not test the
   sticky writer error before continuing.
2. `writeBlocks()` and `writeObjects()` already stage complete sections and
   perform final sticky-error/commit checks. They must not receive redundant
   nested transactions. Their remaining risk is unchecked structural writes
   and the inability of a `void` callback to stop immediately after a failed
   child write.
3. The top-level `DwgDxfOutputTransaction` protects the destination file, but
   it cannot retract bytes accepted by an arbitrary caller-owned stream. A
   local section transaction is therefore a state/section-publication guard,
   not a general promise that a callback can be rolled back after observing
   partial bytes.
4. The parser boundary audit is now at the API-call level, but it is not yet a
   no-partial-callback parser. `processBlock()` still calls `addBlock()` and
   child callbacks before ENDBLK footer validation. The stronger invariant
   requires event staging or a parser-owned intermediate block model; simply
   adding more status checks cannot provide it.
5. `DwgObjectFrame::bodyBitSize()` still names the handle-stream bit count,
   and the DWG integrity API remains counter-based. DataStorage receipts still
   describe logical source coverage rather than final physical section/page
   bytes. Those are separate P3/P4 boundaries and are not closed by this DXF
   work.

### Revised closure map

| Area | Current status | Remaining closure condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DXF ordinary writer admission | six direct paths scoped; local normalization fixes landed | table/raw structural guards, mutation snapshots for all changed families, retry proof |
| DXF TABLES section | not transactionally staged; fallback returns ignored | full section state/byte transaction and callback/fallback sticky checks |
| DXF BLOCKS/OBJECTS sections | compound/section transactions present | structural token audit and callback-failure documentation |
| DXF parser boundary | pending state fail-closed; exact bare calls eliminated | staged BLOCK event stream and binary/text child-atomicity proof |
| DWG frame safety | range/size/cursor/CRC checks present | naming/cap reconciliation and version-specific integrity evidence |
| AC1027 DataStorage | logical admission and replay metadata | occurrence identity and post-layout physical receipts |
| Version matrix | factory and partial paths | independent AC1021/AC1027/AC1032 conformance rows |

### Implementation-ready sub-plan: P1-TABLES

1. At the start of `writeTables()`, reject a null writer, then create one
   `RecordStateScope` and one `DxfWriterRecordScope` covering the complete
   TABLES section. Do not add per-table nested scopes; the section is the
   publication unit and callbacks may add records to it.
2. Immediately after each table callback, stop if `m_writeError` or
   `writer->hasWriteError()` is set. For fallback entries, require the
   boolean writer result. This applies to VPORT, LAYER, STYLE, and DIMSTYLE;
   callback-only phases remain guarded by the sticky state because their
   interface is `void`.
3. Before emitting the next table skeleton and before emitting the final
   `ENDTAB`, check the sticky state. Preserve the existing table order,
   mandatory records, version gates, and `m_pendingBlockRecords` count.
4. Commit the record and state only after the final table section has passed
   the sticky check. Any failed fallback, callback write, or commit must set
   `m_writeError` and return false; no pending table metadata may survive.
5. Use the existing outer output transaction for destination-file rollback.
   Do not promise callback interruption for `void` interface methods; record
   that the section is rejected atomically at the writer boundary.

1. Add a rejecting callback/fallback case for each fallback table entry and
   assert `write()` fails without a committed output file or stale table-map
   state.
2. Add a short-accepting sink case during TABLES and assert the final target
   remains absent or unchanged, depending on whether it existed before the
   attempt.
3. Add failure-success and failure-failure retries using the same `dxfRW`
   object. Assert no duplicate mandatory records, pending BLOCK_RECORDs,
   handles, or table-entry map state.
4. Extend source snapshots to LWPOLYLINE, HATCH, MPOLYGON, and dimension

   success-preservation from failed-write rollback; a source field that is
   never mutated does not need a rollback journal entry.

### P2-B block callback staging decision

1. Before editing callback ownership, inventory `DRW_Interface` callback
   signatures and ownership rules for blocks, entities, custom entities,
   ATTRIB, VERTEX, and SEQEND. The staging model must own independent copies
   until commit and must not replay dangling pointers.
2. Prefer a parser-owned event list with typed value storage and a single
   commit adapter. The list must preserve callback order and the current
   first-child dispatch behavior. If a typed event list cannot represent a
   custom callback safely, introduce an intermediate record object and replay
   from that object rather than weakening validation.
3. Commit only after the BLOCK header, all child records, and ENDBLK footer
   pass. Rejected blocks must produce zero public block/child callbacks and no
   block map insertion. Valid blocks must produce exactly one `addBlock()` and
   one `endBlock()` in the existing order.
4. Add paired ASCII and binary tests for malformed ATTRIB, VERTEX, SEQEND,
   footer owner/handle fields, and first-child retention. Keep headerless
   compatibility fixtures explicitly separate from modern strict fixtures.

### P3/P4/P5 remains unchanged but reordered by dependency

1. Finish P1-TABLES and the writer mutation/retry evidence first; this
   establishes the local transaction contract used by later raw replay and
   physical receipt tests.
2. Finish P2-B staging design and tests before exposing a public DWG
   integrity policy. Parser callback semantics should not be confused with
   DWG report semantics.
3. Implement P3 strict/compatibility diagnostics with a named
   `handleStreamBitSize()` API and audited call sites, then P4 physical
   DataStorage receipts after the writer exposes final page layout through a
   version-neutral receipt.
4. Close P5 only from per-version fixture, malformed, in-tree readback, and
   external-tool rows. Factory construction and self-read alone remain
   insufficient.

### Execution contract after rev 1148

1. Next source edit: implement P1-TABLES as one small patch. Run the warm
   changed compile check immediately, then run `[dxf][writer]`, `[dxf][block]`,
   and `[dxf][entities]` selectors one at a time.
2. Keep inner-loop verification incremental. Use `--skip-slow` and focused
   selectors; defer qmake6, sanitizers, the complete filter suite, slow corpus
   tests, and external readers to the P1/P2 exit gate.
3. After the TABLES patch and tests, append the next roadmap revision with
   exact source paths, selectors, assertion/case counts, and any changed
   closure condition. Do not overwrite historical sections or reuse old
   assertion totals.
4. Do not claim P1 complete until the writer inventory is executable or
   checked against source, all fallback returns are covered, retry behavior is
   tested, and the remaining mutation snapshots pass.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1149): TABLES transaction landed; close writer evidence before parser staging

This is the newest authoritative live-tree update. It supersedes rev 1148;
previous sections remain immutable historical evidence. The revision records
the TABLES implementation slice and changes the next source-sized work to
writer structural-token coverage and complete source-state evidence.

### Implemented in the rev 1149 slice

1. `dxfRW::writeTables()` now rejects a null writer and owns one
   `RecordStateScope` plus one `DxfWriterRecordScope` for the whole TABLES
   section. It commits only after all mandatory table data and callbacks have
   completed without a sticky writer error.
2. The VPORT, LAYER, STYLE, and DIMSTYLE fallback records now require their
   boolean writer result. Every table callback phase checks `m_writeError` and
   `dxfWriter::hasWriteError()` before the next table skeleton is emitted.
   R12's void BLOCK_RECORD callback is checked through the same sticky-error
   boundary.
3. A retry regression uses an invalid LAYER color first, verifies that an
   existing destination remains unchanged, retries with the legal BYLAYER
   replacement, and verifies that the output contains one `RETRY_LAYER`
   record. The fixture deliberately uses 257 as invalid; 256 is the legal
   BYLAYER sentinel and must not be treated as malformed.

- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only --jobs 8` passed on the

The slice has not run qmake6, sanitizers, full filters, slow corpus tests, or

## Current Active Plan (rev 1144): parser proof, integrity policy, and physical receipts

This section supersedes every earlier `Current Active Plan`, `Next
implementation slice`, and `Ready-to-implement sub-plan` section. It is based on a source audit of the
current tree, not on the size of the working-tree diff. No new test process
was started during this plan-only pass; the focused results recorded in rev
1143 remain the latest execution evidence and must be rerun after the next
source edit.

### Verified implementation boundary

#### Implemented and evidence-backed

1. The P0 DXF writer corrections are in the tree: derived linetype state is
   reset per attempt, handle arithmetic uses checked `uint32_t` state, and
   direct DXF CLASS input is validated and frozen before CLASSES emission.
   Focused class, handle, writer, and compile-only checks are recorded in rev
   1142.
2. The writer has a per-attempt reset, an outer filesystem publication
   transaction, and a journal-backed `RecordStateScope`. The journal covers
   the currently known source-handle, ambiguous-handle, block-map,
   text-style, linetype, pending-BLOCK_RECORD, and scalar block mutations.
3. `DxfWriterRecordScope` stages a byte range. POLYLINE, INSERT, and the
   complete BLOCKS section stage their compound bytes until child output and
   automatic boundary records have succeeded. The rejecting-stream,
   short-append, image-retry, and writer selectors passed as recorded in rev
   1143.
4. The DXF parser has a pending code-0 boundary representation. The first
   raw child in a modern BLOCK is covered by a focused test, and an incomplete
   POLYLINE VERTEX is rejected before it reaches the callback.
5. DWG object-frame, page, section-map, DataStorage, class-admission, and raw
   replay code contain substantial checked parsing and logical provenance
   validation. That is useful evidence, but it is not a claim that all
   version-specific physical layouts or all typed features are complete.

#### Partially complete and still unsafe to call complete

1. The DXF byte transaction can detect a parent stream that rejects or only
   partially accepts a staged range, but a generic `std::ostream` cannot
   retract bytes already accepted by the parent. The outer output transaction
   protects the destination file; direct users of the low-level scope still
   need the documented sticky-error contract.
2. The mutation journal is narrower than a general transaction log. Any new
   direct mutation of a map, set, owned pointer, or table-entry field can
   escape rollback unless it is routed through a journal helper. The journal
   vector may allocate while recording, so rollback is allocation-free only
   after the record has been admitted and its journal entries exist.
3. DXF compound callbacks are all-or-nothing for bytes and filter state, but
   `DRW_Interface::writeBlocks()` and `writeEntities()` are `void`. A callback
   can continue issuing calls after one low-level operation fails. The sticky
   writer error prevents section publication, but it cannot undo an external
   callback side effect or stop the callback itself.
4. The parser boundary helper is used by the main entity loops, but many
   entity parsers call `setEntityBoundary(code)` for its state effect and do
   not inspect the returned enum directly. The invariant is currently
   enforced indirectly by `acceptEntityCallbackBoundary()` and later
   classification. It needs a complete audit and direct status tests before a
   cursor rewrite can be ruled out.
5. DXF CLASS preflight prevents unsafe and duplicate definitions and blocks
   late mutation, but instance-count closure across every direct typed, raw,
   generated, and fallback path is not yet a single predictive manifest.
6. DataStorage source-row decisions, object-frame receipts, and logical
   section receipts are present in `RS_FilterDXFRW`. They do not yet prove
   the final physical section/page id, file offset, stored size, encoded size,
   pagination, and checksum produced by `dwgWriter21`/`dwgWriter24`.
7. `dwgWriter32` and the AC1032 factory path exist, while the R2018-family
   implementation is inherited from the modern writer path. Independent
   AC1032 byte-layout and external-reader evidence is still missing.

#### Open release-blocking work

1. Define and expose a DWG integrity policy/report. Current R2004/R2007+
   header, class, page, and payload CRC/checksum mismatches are intentionally
   diagnostic in existing compatibility tests. Do not silently change that
   default; add an explicit strict mode and retain compatibility mode until a
   corpus review justifies a default change.
2. Reconcile the 256 MiB `DwgObjectFrame` body limit with the larger general
   DWG safety/container limits and the writer's admission limits. The current
   signed `int32_t` frame offset/CRC interface also needs an explicit supported
   size ceiling or a checked wider implementation.
3. Verify object-frame CRC coverage and seed independently for R13, R2000,
   R2004, and R2007+; page integrity and object-frame integrity are separate
   contracts.
4. Produce final physical DataStorage receipts after page layout and bind
   each receipt to exactly one logical source row. The current logical ledger
   must not be described as byte-preserving physical replay.
5. Complete AC1027 and AC1032 version/tool gates, including malformed page
   maps, codec mismatches, truncation, CRC/checksum failures, and invalid
   DataStorage presence bits. External tools that are unavailable are
   recorded as skipped, never as passing evidence.
6. Finish the feature inventory for typed DXF/DWG entities, objects, tables,
   raw fallback, and same-version replay. A factory or dispatch case alone is
   not feature-completeness evidence.

### Refined implementation sub-plans

#### P1-R: close the remaining DXF writer transaction boundary

1. Enumerate every mutation in `dxfRW::write()`, all public entity/table
   emitters, BLOCK_RECORD emission, IMAGE handling, raw replay, and the
   deferred OBJECTS paths. Mark each as persistent input, per-attempt state,
   or record-local state. No direct mutation may remain unclassified.
2. Replace the narrow mutation cases with typed journal operations for
   insert, replace, erase, vector append, owned-pointer transfer, and scalar
   assignment. Each operation must record enough previous state to restore
   the exact map/set/vector contents. Nested scopes retain inner commits in
   the parent; an inner abort restores only its own checkpoint.
3. Keep the allocator monotonic after a failed record. Tests must prove that
   consumed handles are not reused, while unpublished maps, metadata, image
   carriers, block ownership, and bytes do not leak into the next attempt.
4. Add an internal `canContinueWrite()` gate after every structural write and
   delegated callback boundary. Preserve the existing void callback ABI; the
   initial contract is sticky failure plus no later low-level publication.
   Consider a status-returning interface only as a separately reviewed API
   change, not as an implicit part of this fix.
5. Exit criteria: mutation-path audit is complete, nested scope tests pass,
   rejecting and short-writing sinks pass, and success-success,
   failure-success, and failure-failure reuse tests pass for BLOCK_RECORD,
   IMAGE, INSERT, POLYLINE, OBJECT, and raw replay.

#### P2-R: finish DXF record-cursor proof without a wholesale rewrite

1. Define an internal status vocabulary with exactly `Ok`, `NextEntity`,
   `EndSec`, `EndBlk`, and `Error`. Make one helper responsible for reading a
   code-0 token, one helper for classifying it, and one helper for consuming
   it. A pending token must be consumed exactly once; an empty code-0 value
   is an error, not an implicit end marker.
2. Audit every `setEntityBoundary(code)` call in `libdxfrw.cpp`. Either use
   and check the returned status immediately or replace the call with the
   status helper. Do not rely on a side effect in `nextentity` without a
   checked state transition.
3. Define the BLOCK callback contract. The header is valid before
   `addBlock()`; a child parse failure must not publish a child entity or a
   block-record map entry. Until the callback API can stage a complete block,
   the implementation must report the block failure, balance exactly one
   `endBlock()` for an opened callback scope, and document that the already
   delivered valid block header is not retractable.
4. Add focused fixtures for an empty boundary, ENDSEC in a BLOCK, ENDBLK in
   top-level ENTITIES, first BLOCK child retention, first raw-group retention,
   malformed ATTRIB, malformed VERTEX, malformed SEQEND, binary chunk
   truncation, and a valid child immediately followed by each legal boundary.
   Assert callback counts, map contents, and the final parser status.
5. Exit criteria: no parser path appends a failed child, no invalid boundary
   is accepted by context, and every pending-token test passes for ASCII and
   binary DXF where the format permits both.

#### P3-R: add explicit DWG integrity policy and align limits

1. Add a public `DwgIntegrityPolicy` with `Compatibility` and `Strict`, plus
   a read-only `DwgIntegrityReport` containing version, layer, section/page
   identity, file offset, expected value, actual value, and fatality. Default
   to `Compatibility` so existing loadable third-party fixtures and current
   warning tests remain valid.
2. Make structural failures unconditional: short headers, invalid section or
   page ids, RS decode failure, impossible offsets/sizes, non-advancing maps,
   decompression failure, and out-of-range object frames must fail before
   callbacks. In compatibility mode, retain only the specifically classified
   checksum/CRC advisories; strict mode upgrades those advisories to errors.
3. Implement the policy at the reader layer rather than duplicating checks in
   `dwgRW`. Preserve the existing counters as compatibility summaries and add
   the detailed report for callers and tests.
4. Define one version-aware maximum object-frame body constant. Use checked
   unsigned arithmetic for file ranges and refuse writer output that the
   in-tree reader cannot consume. Add low-memory malformed declarations and
   boundary tests without allocating a 256 MiB fixture.
5. Add golden frame/page tests for AC1012, AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024,
   AC1027, and AC1032. Verify CRC coverage, seed, page alignment, object-map
   offsets, and policy behavior separately.

#### P4-R: bind DataStorage to final physical layout

1. Keep the current logical replay plan as an admission plan only. Extend
   the modern writer with a finalized physical-section report generated after
   all page ids, offsets, sizes, encoding, encryption, and checksums are
   known.
2. For every replayed DataStorage section, record canonical section rank,
   source section index/version/name, physical section id, page ids, logical
   and stored offsets, encoded and decoded sizes, page limit/alignment,
   codec/encryption flags, checksum/CRC, and a stable byte digest. A section
   split produces multiple page receipts under one source-row identity.
3. Parse the emitted bytes with a test-only decoder and compare the report to
   the actual section and page map. Reject missing, duplicate, reordered,
   overlapping, or unbound receipts before publication.
4. Retain exact opaque replay only for the same encoding family and version
   accepted by the raw carrier policy. Reject cross-version replay unless a
   typed converter exists; do not silently call a re-encoded section byte
   identical.
5. Force page splits, empty sections, duplicate revisions, wide handles, and
   retry-after-failure cases for AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 as
   applicable.

#### P5-R: independent version and feature gates

1. Create a matrix with separate rows for read, typed write, raw replay,
   malformed rejection, and cross-tool readback. Cover AC1012 through AC1032
   where the format rules differ, with explicit legacy and modern DXF rows.
2. For AC1027 and AC1032, inspect version bytes, header, section/page maps,
   object-map offsets, CLASSES, HANDSEED, object-frame CRCs, DataStorage
   presence bits, and physical receipts. Use the in-tree reader first, then
   independently named libreDWG/ODA checks when installed.
3. Drive the matrix from the coverage/parity inventory so a new dispatch case
   cannot be marked complete without a fixture and a failure-path result.
   Record unsupported external tools and unavailable fixtures as skipped.

### Execution order and fast verification

1. Finish P1-R's mutation audit and residual callback gate. This is the only
   work allowed to change the DXF transaction core before parser tests are
   closed.
2. Finish P2-R with focused ASCII/binary boundary fixtures. Do not replace
   the existing parser with a new cursor abstraction unless the audit finds a
   transition that cannot be expressed by the current pending-token model.
3. Implement P3-R's compatibility/strict report and frame-limit alignment.
   Keep default compatibility until the malformed corpus and third-party
   fixture review is complete.
4. Implement P4-R's physical receipt hook and byte-level decoder, then run
   P5-R's version matrix. Only after those gates pass should typed feature
   expansion or broad raw parity be scheduled.

Use the warm `build/dwg-fast` tree and
`scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only` after each source slice.
Run one focused selector at a time because the test targets share a static
archive. Use `--skip-slow` during iteration and explicitly select slow corpus,
sanitizer, qmake6, and external-reader checks at the end of each P-level
slice. Report compile, focused behavior, malformed-input behavior, and
version/tool evidence separately; compilation alone never closes a plan item.

### Current evidence ledger

- Latest focused DXF writer selector: 236 assertions in 23 cases passed.
- Latest record-scope selector: 18 assertions in 1 case passed, including

- Latest image retry selector: 6 assertions in 1 case passed.
- Latest malformed POLYLINE selector: 4 assertions in 2 cases passed under
