### Definition of done for the roadmap

The DWG/DXF roadmap is complete only when every advertised version has a
passing read/write or explicit unsupported result, every preserved opaque
record has a same-version physical receipt, malformed input fails before
publication and callbacks, class/handle/ownership graphs are closed, and the
focused plus release-gate evidence is retained. AC1032 factory construction,
logical DataStorage ledgers, or a successful LibreCAD self-read alone do not
meet this definition.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1145): ordinary DXF records, footer integrity, and physical DWG evidence

This section supersedes rev 1144 and is the current implementation queue. It
is based on a fresh symbol-level audit of the live tree. The audit found no
source regression in the completed work, but it also found that several
remaining guarantees are narrower than the previous plan implied. No source
implementation or test execution was performed in this plan-only pass. The
focused results recorded in rev 1143 remain the latest execution evidence.

### Corrected live-tree boundary

1. `dxfRW::writeEntity()` has 50 non-definition call sites in
   `libdxfrw.cpp`. Only `writePoint()`, `writePolyline()`, and `writeInsert()`
   currently have both a `RecordStateScope` and a `DxfWriterRecordScope`.
   Most ordinary entity writers only return the final writer error. Compound
   staging therefore must not be described as atomicity for all DXF entities.
2. There are 44 direct `setEntityBoundary(code)` calls whose return value is
   not inspected by the caller. The current `DxfEntityBoundary` enum has four
   states: `NextEntity`, `EndSection`, `EndBlock`, and `Error`. A five-state
   vocabulary with `Ok` must not be introduced casually; either the existing
   boundary enum is checked directly or a separate record-status layer is
   added with a documented mapping.
3. The top-level DXF writer still emits required `SECTION`, section-name,
   `ENDSEC`, and `EOF` tokens through unchecked low-level calls in the main
   write path around `dxfRW::write()`. A later sticky-error check is not an
   immediate structural publication barrier.
4. `processBlock()` validates the BLOCK header before `addBlock()` and uses a
   pending code-0 token for the first child, but `consumeEndBlock()` scans
   over the ENDBLK payload without validating the ENDBLK handle, owner, or
   malformed footer fields. Block completion is not fully proven until that
   footer is parsed under the same rules as other records.
5. DWG public diagnostics expose mismatch counters and parse-failure counts,
   but no public integrity policy or detailed report. Current R2004/R2007+
   header, class, page, and payload CRC/checksum mismatches remain advisory;
   existing compatibility tests intentionally accept them.
6. DWG frame receipts and the filter's logical DataStorage ledger exist, but
   no public or test-visible receipt is produced after modern writer page
   layout. The final section id, page ids, physical offset, stored/encoded
   size, alignment, checksum/CRC, and byte digest are not yet reported.
7. The public DWG writer set is AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
   AC1032, while the reader factory also accepts substantially older versions.
   Read coverage and writer coverage must remain separate matrix dimensions.
   AC1032 construction currently follows inherited modern writer logic and
   lacks independent emitted-file evidence.

### Remaining implementation blockers

#### P1-DXFW: ordinary DXF record atomicity and structural writes

Goal: make every public DXF record either fully published with its associated
state or rejected without leaking record-local state. This is a separate
guarantee from the already-scoped POLYLINE, INSERT, and BLOCKS compound paths.

1. Build a live inventory of all 50 non-definition `writeEntity()` call sites,
   the table/object emitters, BLOCK_RECORD creation, IMAGE/IMAGEDEF handling,
   raw replay, and deferred OBJECTS paths. Classify each mutation as
   persistent input, per-attempt state, record-local state, or external
   callback side effect. The inventory must name the owning map/vector/field
   and the rollback owner.
2. Add one shared ordinary-record guard or wrapper around every eligible
   writer. It must stage bytes, checkpoint record-local state, and restore
   source-handle bindings, minted entity handles stored on input objects,
   ambiguity maps, linetype/style maps, block ownership, and generated image
   carriers when the record fails. Do not double-capture a parent compound
   record when a child re-enters `writeEntity()`.
3. Keep handle allocation monotonic after abort. A failed record may consume a
   handle, but a retry must not reuse it; no failed record may remain in a
   published map, emitted byte range, ownership list, or class-instance count.
4. Add `writeRequiredString()` or an equivalent checked structural-token
   helper. Use it for `SECTION`, section names, `ENDSEC`, `EOF`, and any
   required header/backpatch write. Check `canContinueWrite()` immediately
   after each token and delegated callback boundary. Preserve the current
   void callback ABI: sticky failure may prevent later publication, but cannot
   retract arbitrary side effects performed by an external callback.
5. Define the low-level sink contract for rejecting and short-accepting
   streams. A generic `std::ostream` cannot retract bytes already accepted by
   its parent, so all-or-nothing guarantees must be scoped to the staging
   buffer and output-file transaction, not claimed for an arbitrary stream.
6. Exit criteria: all ordinary writers are classified and guarded or have an
   explicit exception documented; nested scope checkpoints pass; structural
   token failures stop the section immediately; failure-success and
   failure-failure retries do not leak state for entity, table, object, image,
   block-record, and raw-replay paths.

#### P2-DXFR: boundary status and ENDBLK footer proof

Goal: prove the existing pending-token model before considering a cursor
rewrite.

1. Retain `DxfEntityBoundary` for code-0 outcomes unless a separate
   `DxfRecordStatus` is required. If a second status type is introduced, map
   exactly `Ok`, `NextEntity`, `EndSec`, `EndBlk`, and `Error` to the existing
   parser states and document which function consumes the pending token.
2. Audit all 44 unchecked `setEntityBoundary(code)` calls. Each must either
   inspect the returned boundary immediately or use one checked helper that
   records the context and rejects illegal transitions. State mutation alone
   is not an accepted proof of correctness.
3. Make `consumeEndBlock()` validate the ENDBLK record itself: required code-5
   handle and code-330 owner where applicable, legal extra groups, record
   termination, and context. A malformed footer must not publish a completed
   block record. Keep exactly one `endBlock()` for every opened callback scope
   even when the footer fails, and document the non-retractable `addBlock()`
   header callback until block-level staging exists.
4. Add focused ASCII and binary fixtures for empty code-0 boundaries, ENDSEC
   inside BLOCKS, ENDBLK in top-level ENTITIES, malformed ENDBLK fields,
   first-child retention, first raw-group retention, malformed ATTRIB,
   VERTEX, and SEQEND, binary-chunk truncation, and every legal boundary after
   a valid child. Assert callback counts, map contents, and final status.
5. Exit criteria: no failed child reaches a callback or ownership map, no
   invalid boundary is accepted by context, pending tokens are consumed once,
   and footer failures are distinguishable from clean block termination.

#### P3-DWGI: explicit integrity policy and aligned limits

Goal: expose compatibility versus strict integrity behavior without changing
the existing default unexpectedly.

1. Add a public `DwgIntegrityPolicy` with `Compatibility` and `Strict`, plus a
   read-only `DwgIntegrityReport`. Each report entry should include version,
   reader layer, section/page or object identity, file offset, expected value,
   actual value, classification, and fatal/advisory severity. Preserve the
   existing counters as compatibility summaries.
2. Make structural failures unconditional in both policies: short headers,
   invalid page or section ids, impossible ranges, non-advancing maps, RS
   decode failure, decompression failure, and out-of-range object frames must
   fail before callbacks, map insertion, or partial child publication. Strict
   mode upgrades only explicitly classified CRC/checksum advisories.
3. Implement the policy at the reader layer, where version-specific checks
   already occur. Ensure `resetReadDiagnostics()` clears the report and all
   legacy counters together, and capture the report before any reader reset.
4. Align `dwgObjectFrame::MaxBodySize`, signed `int32_t` offset/CRC interfaces,
   `dwgsafety.h` buffer caps, and modern writer admission limits. Use checked
   unsigned file-range arithmetic and refuse output that the in-tree reader
   cannot consume. Test limits with small synthetic declarations rather than
   allocating maximum-sized fixtures.
5. Independently verify object-frame CRC coverage and seed for R13, R2000,
   R2004, and R2007+; keep page CRC/checksum and object-frame CRC as separate
   report classes. Add policy tests for clean, advisory mismatch, strict
   mismatch, and unconditional structural failure.
6. Exit criteria: callers can select policy before reading, reports identify
   the failing layer and location, compatibility behavior remains stable, and
   strict behavior is covered for every modern reader family.

#### P4-DWGP: physical DataStorage receipts after final layout

Goal: turn the current logical replay ledger into verifiable physical
evidence, without claiming byte preservation from metadata alone.

1. Keep the `RS_FilterDXFRW` logical ledger as an admission plan. Extend the
   modern writer finalization path after page ids, offsets, sizes, encoding,
   encryption, and checksums are final to produce a physical-section report.
2. Bind each source row to exactly one logical receipt and one or more page
   receipts when splitting occurs. Record source section index/version/name,
   canonical rank, physical section id, page ids, logical/stored offsets,
   encoded/decoded sizes, page limit and alignment, codec/encryption flags,
   checksum/CRC, and a stable digest of the emitted bytes.
3. Add a test-only decoder that compares receipts with the actual section/page
   map. Reject missing, duplicate, reordered, overlapping, or unbound
   receipts before publication. A retry must discard receipts from the failed
   attempt.
4. Permit exact opaque replay only when the raw carrier's version and
   encoding-family policy match. Cross-version replay must fail unless a typed
   converter exists; re-encoded bytes must never be called byte-identical.
5. Force page splitting, empty sections, duplicate revisions, wide handles,
   and retry-after-failure for AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 where
   the writer supports the relevant container family.
6. Exit criteria: every accepted DataStorage row has a physical receipt that
   matches emitted bytes and page maps, and no logical-only receipt is used as
   release evidence for same-version preservation.

#### P5-DWGV: independent version and feature matrix

Goal: distinguish dispatch presence from usable read, typed-write, raw-replay,
malformed-rejection, and cross-tool coverage.

1. Create matrix rows for AC1012 through AC1032 where framing rules differ,
   plus legacy and modern DXF. Each row must separately record reader status,
   typed writer status, raw replay status, malformed-input result, in-tree
   readback, and independent-tool readback.
2. For AC1027 and AC1032 inspect version bytes, header, section/page maps,
   object-map offsets, CLASSES, HANDSEED, object-frame CRCs, DataStorage
   presence bits, and physical receipts. Use the in-tree reader first, then
   named libreDWG or ODA checks only when installed. Missing tools and
   unavailable fixtures are `skipped`, never `passed`.
3. Tie the matrix to the typed/raw feature inventory: entities, objects,
   tables, owners, EED/XDATA, binary DXF chunks, proxy/custom classes, and
   same-version fallback. A factory case or successful self-read cannot close
   a feature row.
4. Add explicit unsupported-writer results for versions readable by the
   factory but outside the public writer set. Keep AC1015, AC1018, AC1021,
   AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 writer claims separate from older reader claims.
5. Exit criteria: every advertised combination has fixture-backed evidence or
   a deliberate unsupported result, and AC1032 has version-specific emitted
   file assertions rather than inherited-code assumptions.

### Ordered execution and evidence policy

1. Implement P1-DXFW's ordinary-record inventory and structural-token guard.
   Do not broaden DXF transaction claims until the 50 call sites are
   classified and the ordinary-record failure tests pass.
2. Complete P2-DXFR using the existing pending-token model. Only introduce a
   new cursor abstraction if a legal transition cannot be represented and the
   failing case is retained as a regression fixture.
3. Implement P3-DWGI with compatibility as the default, then run malformed
   and mismatch fixtures before considering any default-policy change.
4. Implement P4-DWGP after final page layout is observable. Use its receipts
   to constrain P5-DWGV, not the reverse.
5. Run P5-DWGV's version/feature matrix only after the physical receipt and
   integrity gates are in place. Typed feature expansion and broad raw parity
   remain downstream work.

During iteration, use the warm `build/dwg-fast` tree and
`scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only` after each source slice.
Run one focused selector at a time because the test targets share a static
archive. Use `--skip-slow` for iteration and explicitly schedule slow corpus,
sanitizer, qmake6, and external-reader checks at each P-level exit. Record
compile, focused behavior, malformed-input behavior, and version/tool
evidence separately; compilation is never sufficient to close a plan item.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1146): transaction closure, boundary proof, and physical DWG evidence

This section supersedes rev 1145 and is the current implementation queue. It
is a second audit of the live worktree after the first DXF transaction slice
was added. The previous section is retained as historical evidence, but its
counts and "plan-only" status must not be used as current facts.

### Evidence snapshot from the current worktree

1. `dxfRW::writeEntity()` has 52 textual occurrences: one definition and 51
   call sites. There are 44 `EntityRecordScope` placements, but that count is
   not equivalent to 44 atomically covered call sites because some placements
   belong to table-entry writers and some calls are intentionally inside the
   existing compound scopes. `writePolyline()` and `writeInsert()` retain
   their parent `RecordStateScope`/`DxfWriterRecordScope` transactions.
2. The direct ordinary paths still needing an explicit coverage decision are
   `writePoint()`, `writeLight()`, `writeCamera()`,
   `writeGeoPositionMarker()`, `writeSectionObject()`, `writeMesh()`, and
   `writeShape()`. The compound `writePolyline()` and `writeInsert()` paths
   are a different case: adding a nested generic scope would capture the
   parent twice and can break child/parent handle semantics.
3. `EntityRecordScope` rolls back the existing journaled handle/map state and
   newly generated IMAGEDEF carriers, but it does not generically restore
   every source-field mutation. Current examples include `ELLIPSE` axis
   correction, `LWPOLYLINE::vertexnum`, HATCH/MPOLYGON loop counts, and
   dimension subtype bits. These must become local derived values or receive
   explicit journal entries before the guard can be called full record
   atomicity.
4. `writeRequiredString()` is now used by the main `dxfRW::write()` section
   skeleton, including `SECTION`, section names, `ENDSEC`, and `EOF`. The
   helper does not yet cover every required structural token inside
   `writeTables()`, `writeBlocks()`, `writeBlock()`, `writeObjects()`, or raw
   section replay. Those paths still need immediate failure checks at their
   own publication boundaries.
5. The parser still has 44 bare `setEntityBoundary(code);` statements whose
   result is not consumed directly. `acceptEntityCallbackBoundary()` makes
   some transitions safe indirectly, but it does not prove that every caller
   inspected `Error` and applied the correct section/block context.
6. `processBlock()` still calls `addBlock()` before all child records and the
   ENDBLK payload have been validated. `consumeEndBlock()` skips nonzero
   groups and accepts the next code-0 token without validating ENDBLK handle,
   owner, duplicate fields, or footer-specific malformed values. A failed
   footer can therefore close the callback scope, but cannot retract the
   already-issued `addBlock()` callback until block-level staging exists.
7. `DwgObjectFrame::readAt()` currently rejects a frame CRC mismatch
   unconditionally after checking the frame range and body limits. The future
   integrity policy must preserve this behavior until the CRC coverage and
   seed are independently proved for each frame family; it must not turn this
   check into an advisory merely because page/header mismatches are currently
   warning-only.
8. DWG diagnostics remain counter-only at the public `dwgRW` boundary. The
   reader has separate counters for classes, R2004, and R2007+ mismatches, but
   there is no policy selector, location-bearing report, or public way to
   distinguish an advisory mismatch from an unconditional structural error.
9. DataStorage evidence is still logical. The filter's section receipt stores
   `std::set` record indexes and commit receipts are keyed by a 32-bit source
   handle. Sets erase occurrence order and duplicates, and a handle-keyed map
   cannot represent two source rows that intentionally share a handle. These
   structures cannot be used as physical byte-preservation evidence.
10. The modern writer computes its page layout inside the version-specific
    writer implementation. The filter receives object-frame receipts and
    logical section commits, but not final section id, page id, physical file
    offset, encoded size, alignment, checksum/CRC, or emitted-byte digest.
11. The incremental verification path is usable but scoped: the warm CMake
    lane and one focused selector have passed for the current DXF writer slice.
    `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only` is the cheap source
    check; `--fast --suite dxf --test '[dxf][writer]' --abort` is the focused
    behavior check. The qmake6 path is a separate build check, and CTest does
    not register the full or format suites unless its explicit registration
    options are enabled.

### Corrected implementation order

#### P1-DXFW: close DXF writer publication boundaries

Goal: make the atomicity claim precise and complete without duplicating the
compound POLYLINE/INSERT transactions.

1. Maintain a checked inventory with one row per 51 `writeEntity()` call
   site, plus every table entry, BLOCK_RECORD, BLOCK, OBJECTS, raw replay,
   and generated IMAGEDEF path. Each row must state the byte scope, state
   scope, source fields mutated, maps/vectors appended, callback side
   effects, and the failure signal used by the caller.
2. Finish direct ordinary coverage for the seven paths listed above. Use the
   existing `EntityRecordScope` only where the function owns one complete
   record. Preserve the parent scope for POLYLINE and INSERT and explicitly
   mark child re-entry as a non-nesting path.
3. Remove or journal source mutations that occur after the guard starts:
   compute ellipse correction on a local copy, write local vertex/loop
   counts, and derive dimension subtype flags without changing the caller's
   object. If a mutation is part of the documented API result, journal it
   explicitly and test rollback rather than relying on the generic scope.
4. Extend the same immediate token/error discipline to table, block, object,
   raw-section, and backpatch writers. A delegated void callback remains
   non-retractable; the writer must stop subsequent publication and return a
   sticky failure as soon as its own sink rejects a required token.
5. Keep handle allocation monotonic across failure. A failed attempt may
   consume a handle, but it must not leave a source map entry, ownership edge,
   class-instance count, image carrier, or staged record behind. A retry test
   must compare state before the attempt, after failure, and after a successful
   retry.
6. Add rejecting and short-accepting sink tests for ordinary entities,
   table entries, raw objects, generated image definitions, and the section
   skeleton. Scope the guarantee to staged bytes and the output-file
   transaction; do not claim rollback for bytes already accepted by an
   arbitrary parent `std::ostream`.
7. P1 closes only when the inventory is checked in as testable evidence, all
   seven direct paths have a decision, every required structural token has an
   immediate guard, and failure-success/failure-failure retry tests pass.

#### P2-DXFR: prove pending-token transitions and ENDBLK

Goal: preserve the existing pending-token architecture and add a narrow status
helper only if it reduces unchecked transitions.

1. Keep `DxfEntityBoundary` as the code-0 result type. If a helper is added,
   map its result explicitly to `NextEntity`, `EndSection`, `EndBlock`, and
   `Error`; do not add an `Ok` value that conflates "record parsed" with
   "next boundary staged".
2. Replace or annotate all 44 bare boundary statements with one checked
   operation that validates the caller context. The operation must state
   whether it consumes the pending token, leaves it for the next dispatcher,
   or transitions into the BLOCK child loop.
3. Parse ENDBLK fields instead of scanning them away. For a present code 5,
   require a valid nonzero 32-bit handle, reject duplicate code 5, and let
   `registerSelfHandle()` detect drawing-wide collisions. For a present code
   330, require a valid nonzero handle and, when BLOCK has a resolved parent,
   require equality with that parent. Require these fields for known modern
   source versions using the same existing version gates as BLOCK headers;
   preserve minimal legacy/unknown-version fixtures that omit them. Accept
   legal extra groups and terminate only at the next code-0 boundary.
4. Decide the callback contract explicitly. The first implementation may
   close exactly one `endBlock()` for every opened `addBlock()` scope even on
   footer failure, but it must report that the completed block was rejected.
   A stronger "no callback on malformed footer" invariant requires staging
   the entire block callback stream and is a separate sub-plan, not an
   accidental promise of `consumeEndBlock()`.
5. Add ASCII and binary tests for malformed footer handle/owner values,
   duplicate footer fields, owner mismatch, missing modern fields, minimal
   legacy fields, ENDSEC/ENDBLK in the wrong context, first child retention,
   malformed ATTRIB/VERTEX/SEQEND, and binary chunk truncation. Check return
   status, callback counts, block map contents, and pending-token state.
6. P2 closes only when every boundary transition is checked, malformed
   ENDBLK cannot publish a completed block record, and the intentional
   non-retractable header callback behavior is documented and tested.

#### P3-DWGI: add a version-aware integrity policy

Goal: expose strict checking without changing the current compatibility
default until the specification and compatibility corpus support the change.

1. Add public `DwgIntegrityPolicy { Compatibility, Strict }` and a
   read-only `DwgIntegrityReport` at the `dwgRW` API boundary. Report entries
   need version, layer, section/page or object identity, file offset, expected
   value, actual value, classification, and fatal/advisory severity. Keep
   legacy counters as derived summaries for compatibility.
2. Make short input, invalid ids, impossible ranges, non-advancing maps,
   failed RS/decompression, and out-of-range frames fatal in both policies.
   Keep only explicitly classified checksum/CRC mismatches policy-dependent.
   `DwgObjectFrame::readAt()` remains fatal until its family-specific coverage
   is independently verified.
3. Define report lifetime and reset semantics before coding: selection must
   happen before `read()`/`readBuffer()`, a failed read retains its report
   until the next read begins, and `resetReadDiagnostics()` clears counters
   and report together. Copy diagnostics before destroying the reader.
4. Reconcile `MaxBodySize`, signed frame offset/CRC APIs, `dwgsafety.h` caps,
   R2004 page caps, R2007 map caps, and writer admission limits. Use checked
   unsigned range arithmetic and small synthetic declarations rather than
   allocating at the maximum.
5. Add independent CRC/coverage tests for R13/R2000, R2004, and R2007+ object
   frames, plus clean, compatibility-mismatch, strict-mismatch, and fatal
   structural cases. Do not use a counter increment alone as proof that the
   correct byte range was checked.

#### P4-DWGP: produce physical DataStorage receipts

Goal: connect the logical replay plan to final writer layout without claiming
byte identity from metadata.

1. Keep the filter plan as admission input. Add an internal writer finalization
   result emitted only after page ids, offsets, sizes, encoding/encryption,
   padding, checksums, and CRCs are final. Expose a read-only/test-facing
   copy through `dwgRW` rather than coupling the filter to a version-specific
   layout struct.
2. Key evidence by `DwgDataStorageSourceRowKey` plus an occurrence id, not
   only by source handle. Preserve duplicate revisions and source order in a
   vector; use sets only for membership checks. Each row binds to exactly one
   logical object/section receipt and zero or more physical page receipts.
3. Record source section/version/name, canonical rank, physical section id,
   page ids, logical and stored offsets, decoded/encoded sizes, page limit,
   alignment, codec/encryption flags, checksum/CRC, and a stable digest of
   emitted bytes. Validate the report against the actual section/page map
   before output commit.
4. Reject missing, duplicated, reordered, overlapping, or unbound rows.
   Clear all physical receipts on failed attempts and never report a logical
   commit as a physical commit. Force page splitting, empty sections, wide
   handles, duplicate source rows, and retry-after-failure cases.
5. Permit exact opaque replay only for matching version and encoding family.
   A re-encoded payload may be semantically equivalent, but it is not byte
   identical; cross-version replay fails unless a typed converter is present.
6. P4 closes only when AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032 supported
   paths have at least one receipt checked against emitted bytes, with absent
   external tooling recorded as `skipped` rather than `passed`.

#### P5-DWGV: maintain independent version/feature evidence

Goal: distinguish factory dispatch from usable reader, typed writer, raw
replay, malformed rejection, and independent-tool compatibility.

1. Maintain separate rows for AC1012, AC1014, AC1015, AC1018, AC1021,
   AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032, plus legacy/modern DXF. Each row records
   reader result, typed-write result, raw replay result, malformed-input
   result, in-tree readback, and external-tool readback.
2. For AC1027 and AC1032 assert version bytes, header and section/page maps,
   OBJECTS framing, object-map offsets, CLASSES, HANDSEED, frame CRCs,
   DataStorage presence bits, and physical receipts. AC1032 cannot be closed
   by constructing `dwgWriter32` or inheriting AC1027 code alone.
3. Join the matrix to the feature inventory for entities, tables, objects,
   owners, EED/XDATA, binary DXF chunks, custom classes, proxy graphics,
   ACIS/SAB, and same-version fallback. A static dispatch row remains
   `fixture-needed` until a fixture or deliberate unsupported result exists.
4. Keep the public writer set and reader factory set separate. Versions
   accepted by the reader but not emitted by the writer must have explicit
   unsupported results, not empty success cells.

### Execution contract for the next slices

1. The next source slice is P2 ENDBLK validation, preceded by a focused test
   fixture. Do not begin the public integrity API until the parser's footer
   status and callback contract are settled.
2. After each small source edit, run the warm changed compile check. Run one
   focused Catch2 selector at a time because the micro targets share a static

   inner loop. Full filters, sanitizers, slow corpus tests, and external

3. Update this roadmap after each implementation commit with exact source
   scope, selector, assertion count, build lane, and remaining risks. Never

   a logical receipt alone.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1147): pending-state hygiene, callback atomicity, and physical DWG proof

This section supersedes rev 1146. It is the latest reconciliation of the
roadmap with the live source tree, the focused tests already present in the
worktree, and the incremental verification workflow. It corrects stale claims
about ENDBLK and `writePoint()`, and turns the remaining work into source-sized
slices with explicit closure criteria.

### Current evidence and corrected status

1. The core ENDBLK footer validation is implemented in `processBlock()`:
   duplicate or non-hex code 5, zero handles, duplicate or invalid code 330,
   owner mismatch, missing required modern fields, and an unexpected nested
   ENDBLK are rejected. The modern owner requirement is conditional on an
   explicit source version and a resolved BLOCK_RECORD parent; headerless
   minimal fixtures remain tolerant by design.
2. The focused malformed-block tests are present and have passed with 26
   assertions in 8 cases. The broader focused block selector has passed with
   67 assertions in 16 cases. These results close the ENDBLK field-validation
   slice, but they do not close parser boundary hygiene or callback atomicity.
3. `writePoint()` is already protected by an explicit `RecordStateScope` and
   `DxfWriterRecordScope`, with an explicit commit. It must not be counted as
   an unguarded ordinary writer. `writePolyline()` and `writeInsert()` retain
   parent transactions because they emit child records; adding a generic nested
   scope would risk breaking their ownership and handle semantics.
4. The top-level DXF output uses a temporary-file transaction and the main
   section skeleton uses `writeRequiredString()`. This protects the final file
   from a failed write, but it does not prove that every internal required
   token in `writeTables()`, `writeBlocks()`, `writeBlock()`, `writeObjects()`,
   and raw replay is checked at its own publication boundary.
5. `setEntityBoundary()` still returns `Error` for a nonzero code without
   clearing a previously pending token. There are still 44 bare
   `setEntityBoundary(code);` statements. The pending-token state can therefore
   outlive an error unless every caller happens to reject it before accepting
   the stale token.
6. `processBlock()` now delays the block-record map insertion until the footer
   is valid and balances one `endBlock()` for every issued `addBlock()`. It
   still issues `addBlock()` and child callbacks before ENDBLK validation. A
   malformed footer cannot retract those callbacks; no-partial-callback
   behavior requires block event staging and is not a property of the current
   function.
7. `DwgObjectFrame::readAt()` checks encoded size, handle-stream bit count,
   body range, allocation limits, and CRC, and restores the source cursor on
   failure. Its public `bodyBitSize()` name currently denotes the stored
   handle-stream bit count, while callers pass it to parser APIs with a
   body-size parameter. The name and contract need an audited correction before
   further frame work. Its 256 MiB frame cap also needs reconciliation with
   the broader `dwgSafety` buffer cap.
8. DWG integrity diagnostics are still public counters without a policy or a
   location-bearing report. R2004 and R2007+ page/header mismatches remain
   mostly advisory, while impossible ranges, RS/decompression failures, and
   frame CRC failure have structural-failure behavior. This distinction must
   be made explicit rather than inferred from counters.
9. DataStorage preservation evidence remains logical: section receipts use
   sets, commit receipts are keyed by one 32-bit source handle, and final R2007
   page layout is private to the writer. Duplicate source rows, source order,
   physical page identity, encoded bytes, and final checksums are not yet
   represented by the filter-to-writer contract.
10. The writer factory accepts AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and
    AC1032, but factory dispatch is not conformance. AC1027 and AC1032 share
    inherited writer paths, and AC1021 still needs an explicit public
    read/write evidence row. No version is complete until typed output, raw
    replay, malformed rejection, in-tree readback, and external-tool evidence
    are recorded separately.

### Closure map

| Area | Closed by the current worktree | Still open | Next evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DXF write transaction | top-level file rollback, most ordinary record scopes, `writePoint()` local transaction | six direct ordinary paths, mutation rollback, internal token guards, retry behavior | rejecting sink and source-state tests |
| DXF parser boundary | code-0 classification, first-child dispatch, ENDBLK validation, balanced callback scope | stale pending-token clearing, 44-call audit, staged block callbacks, child failure atomicity | ASCII/binary malformed corpus |
| DWG frame safety | checked ranges, size limits, cursor rollback, frame CRC rejection | API naming, cap policy, family-specific CRC evidence | synthetic frame matrix and sanitizer run |
| DWG diagnostics | compatibility counters | strict/compatibility policy and location-bearing report | clean/advisory/fatal report assertions |
| AC1027 DataStorage | typed/logical admission and replay metadata | occurrence identity and physical final-layout receipts | emitted-byte/page receipt validation |
| Version support | factory and partial writer paths | independent AC1027/AC1032 conformance | per-version fixture/tool matrix |

### Implementation-ready sub-plans

#### P1-DXFW: finish DXF write publication boundaries

**Scope and invariants**

1. Keep one inventory row for each `writeEntity()` call site, each table
   entry, each BLOCK_RECORD, each BLOCK/ENDBLK compound writer, each OBJECTS
   record, each raw replay path, and each generated IMAGEDEF. Record whether
   the row is protected by a local record transaction, a compound parent
   transaction, or the whole section transaction. Do not add redundant nested
   scopes to POLYLINE, INSERT, or OBJECTS paths merely to increase a count.
2. Decide the six remaining direct ordinary paths individually:
   `writeLight()`, `writeCamera()`, `writeGeoPositionMarker()`,
   `writeSectionObject()`, `writeMesh()`, and `writeShape()`. A path closes
   only when its complete record bytes and all associated state are covered by
   one clear transaction or is deliberately rejected before publication.
3. Remove writer-side source mutations where possible. In particular, use
   local derived values for ELLIPSE axis correction, LWPOLYLINE vertex count,
   HATCH/MPOLYGON loop count, and dimension subtype flags. If a mutation is
   part of the supported API contract, add it to the mutation journal and
   prove rollback on failure and preservation on success.
4. Define a small checked structural-write layer for required tokens. Apply it
   by phase: table skeleton and table termination, BLOCKS/ENDBLK framing,
   OBJECTS framing, raw section framing, and backpatch operations. Existing
   typed field writes may continue to use the writer's sticky error, but each
   phase must test the error before publishing its next record or callback.
5. Preserve the actual guarantee: a failed top-level write leaves the target
   file unchanged through `DwgDxfOutputTransaction`; a local record scope
   discards staged bytes and journaled state. No helper may claim to retract
   bytes already accepted by an arbitrary caller-owned `std::ostream`.
6. Verify monotonic handle allocation and rollback of maps, ownership edges,
   class counts, image carriers, pending block records, and section vectors.
   A failed attempt may consume a handle, but a retry must not see stale
   source bindings or duplicate generated objects.

**P1 test slices**

- Rejecting sink: one ordinary entity, one compound child failure, one table
  entry, one raw object, one generated IMAGEDEF, and one section skeleton.
- Short-accepting sink: verify sticky failure and that the temporary output is
  discarded rather than silently truncated.
- Mutation snapshot: compare the source entity before and after failed writes
  for ELLIPSE, LWPOLYLINE, HATCH, MPOLYGON, and dimensions.
- Retry matrix: fail then retry the same writer object and fail twice without
  duplicate handles, class rows, map entries, or ownership edges.
- P1 closes only when the inventory is checked in as executable evidence and
  all six direct paths have a documented, tested decision.

#### P2-DXFR: make parser boundaries transactional

**A. Pending-token state hygiene**

1. Make `setEntityBoundary(code)` transactional: for nonzero input or a failed
   `reader->getString()`, clear `nextentity` and
   `m_hasPendingEntityBoundary` before returning `Error`. A failed boundary
   probe must never leave a token that a later dispatcher can accept.
2. Replace the 44 bare calls with a single checked operation or a local result
   variable whose contract is explicit: `NextEntity`, `EndSection`,
   `EndBlock`, or `Error`. Document whether the pending token remains staged
   for the next dispatcher or is consumed by the current parser.
3. Audit `processBlocks()`, `processEntities()`, every entity parser, table
   parser, object parser, and BLOCK child parser independently. The audit must
   cover EOF/read failure, wrong-context ENDSEC/ENDBLK, and a boundary arriving
   immediately after a malformed child.

**B. Block callback atomicity**

1. Preserve the current compatibility behavior while designing a
   `DxfBlockReadTransaction` that records `addBlock`, child entity, and
   `endBlock` events with ownership-safe payloads. The event sink must preserve
   callback order, pointer lifetime, custom entity callbacks, and block map
   updates without invoking the public interface during speculative parsing.
2. Commit the event stream only after the BLOCK header, every child including
   ATTRIB/VERTEX/SEQEND, and ENDBLK footer have passed validation. On failure,
   discard every event and every staged block-record/map insertion. If the
   existing interface ownership rules make deep event capture unsafe, first
   introduce a parser-owned intermediate record model and replay adapter.
3. Keep exactly one public `endBlock()` for each committed `addBlock()`. For a
   rejected block, the target invariant is zero block callbacks and zero child
   callbacks, not merely a balanced callback pair.
4. Do not weaken the modern footer gates while adding staging. Required handle
   and owner fields remain conditional on known source version and resolved
   parent identity; minimal unknown-version fixtures keep their explicit
   compatibility allowance.

**P2 test slices**

- Pending-token regression: nonzero boundary code followed by a valid entity
  must fail without dispatching the old token.
- ASCII and binary: truncated code/value pair, ENDSEC in BLOCK, ENDBLK in
  ENTITIES, duplicate footer fields, invalid footer handles, owner mismatch,
  missing modern fields, and headerless compatibility fixtures.
- Child atomicity: malformed ATTRIB, VERTEX, or SEQEND must produce no block or
  child callbacks and no map entry; valid children must retain the first
  entity's handle, layer, owner, and order.
- P2 closes only after the boundary audit is complete and the staged callback
  contract is tested in both text and binary readers.

#### P3-DWGI: expose strict DWG integrity without hiding compatibility

1. Add public `DwgIntegrityPolicy { Compatibility, Strict }` and a read-only
   `DwgIntegrityReport`. Each entry must carry version, layer (file header,
   section map, page, object frame, or payload), section/page/object identity,
   file offset and range, expected and actual values where applicable,
   classification, and fatal/advisory severity. Existing counters become
   derived summaries, not a second source of truth.
2. Make short input, invalid ids, impossible ranges, non-advancing handle-map
   entries, failed RS/decompression, and out-of-range frames fatal in both
   policies. Only explicitly classified checksum/CRC mismatches may vary by
   policy. Keep object-frame CRC fatal until coverage and seed are proven for
   every frame family.
3. Specify lifetime before implementation: policy is selected before
   `read()`/`readBuffer()`, a failed read retains its report until the next read
   begins, and `resetReadDiagnostics()` clears counters and report together.
   Reports must be copyable after the reader is destroyed.
4. Reconcile the 256 MiB `DwgObjectFrame` cap with `dwgSafety::MaxBufferSize`,
   R2004 page limits, R2007 map limits, signed offset/CRC APIs, and writer
   admission limits. Introduce `handleStreamBitSize()` and
   `objectDataBitSize()` with audited call sites; keep a deprecated alias only
   if source compatibility requires it, and document the bit partition.
5. Add synthetic and fixture-backed tests for clean files, compatibility-only
   mismatches, strict mismatches, and fatal structural failures across R13,
   R2000, R2004, and R2007+. Assert the checked byte range, not just a counter.

#### P4-DWGP: connect AC1027 preservation to final physical layout

1. Keep the filter's logical admission plan as input. Add a version-neutral
   writer finalization result produced only after the version-specific writer
   has fixed section order, page ids, offsets, encoded sizes, padding,
   checksums, and CRCs. Expose a read-only/test-facing copy through `dwgRW`;
   do not expose private R2007 layout structs to the filter.
2. Replace set-only receipt evidence with an ordered vector. Use
   `DwgDataStorageSourceRowKey` plus an occurrence id as the primary identity;
   retain maps only for lookup. Two source rows with the same handle must
   remain two distinct rows with stable source order.
3. For every physical row record source section/version/name, canonical rank,
   physical section id, page ids, logical and stored offsets, decoded and
   encoded sizes, page limit, alignment/padding, codec/encryption flags,
   checksum/CRC, and a digest of the emitted bytes. Validate these receipts
   against the final page map before output commit.
4. Reject missing, duplicated, reordered, overlapping, or unbound rows. Clear
   physical receipts on every failed attempt. A logical commit alone must
   never be reported as a physical commit.
5. Cover page splitting, empty canonical sections, duplicate source rows,
   wide handles, retry-after-failure, AC1027 `AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b`, and the
   per-object DataStorage presence bit. Same-version opaque replay may be
   exact only when the encoding family matches; cross-version replay requires
   a typed converter.
6. Produce physical receipt evidence separately for AC1018, AC1021, AC1024,
   AC1027, and AC1032. An unavailable external reader is recorded as
   `skipped`, never as `passed`.

#### P5-DWGV: close the version and feature matrix honestly

1. Maintain separate rows for AC1012, AC1014, AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024,
   AC1027, and AC1032, plus legacy and modern DXF. Each row records reader,
   typed writer, raw replay, malformed rejection, in-tree readback, and
   external-tool readback independently.
2. For AC1027 and AC1032 verify version bytes, header/section/page maps,
   `AcDbObjects` framing, object-map offsets, CLASSES, HANDSEED, frame CRCs,
   DataStorage presence bits, and physical receipts. AC1032 is not closed by
   constructing `dwgWriter32` or inheriting AC1027 code; every differing
   branch needs evidence or an explicit unsupported result.
3. Join the matrix to the feature inventory: entities, tables, objects,
   ownership, EED/XDATA, binary DXF chunks, custom classes, proxy graphics,
   ACIS/SAB, DataStorage, and same-version fallback. A factory case without a
   fixture or deliberate rejection remains `fixture-needed`.
4. Keep accepted-reader versions and emitted-writer versions as separate
   capability sets. Unsupported writer versions must fail explicitly before
   output creation.

### Revised execution and verification contract

1. Next source slice: P2-A pending-token clearing and a focused regression
   test. ENDBLK field parsing is complete; do not reopen it except when the
   boundary audit exposes a specific regression.
2. Parallel independent slice: P1 inventory correction, beginning with the
   six direct ordinary writers and source mutation snapshots. Do not wrap all
   OBJECTS writers in redundant nested transactions; prove the existing
   section transaction and add local guards only where a function has an
   independent publication boundary.
3. Use the warm CMake tree after each small source edit with
   `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only`. Run one focused
   Catch2 selector at a time because the micro targets share a static archive.
   Use `--skip-slow` for iteration. qmake6, sanitizer, full filter tests, slow
   corpus tests, and external readers are P-level exit gates, not inner-loop
   commands.
4. Record compile, focused behavior, malformed-input behavior, sanitizer,
   qmake6, and external-tool evidence as separate rows. A self-read, factory
   dispatch result, counter increment, logical receipt, or compilation result
   cannot close a version or feature claim.
5. After each implementation commit, update this roadmap with the exact
   source scope, test selector, assertion/case counts, build lane, and risks.
   This rev 1147 update is documentation-only; it claims no new source or
   test changes beyond the already-present ENDBLK implementation and its
   recorded focused results.

## Deep codebase implementation progress 2026-08-30, rev 1143

### P1 and compound-record progress

1. `DxfWriterRecordScope` now stages a byte range rather than assuming a
   single record. POLYLINE, INSERT, and the complete BLOCKS section use a
   nested byte scope and a `RecordStateScope`, so parent bytes are published
   only after all VERTEX, ATTRIB, SEQEND, and BLOCK/ENDBLK work succeeds.
2. The state journal is now used for source-handle bindings, ambiguous source
   handles, block-map insertions, text-style updates, pending BLOCK_RECORDs,
   linetype-map growth, and scalar block state. Rollback restores the owning
   objects and maps without copying the full writing context.
3. `resetDxfWriteSession()` clears all callback-derived maps, allocator output,
   block state, and generated IMAGEDEF carriers. Persistent raw/class/dictionary
   inputs survive a failed attempt; retry output therefore does not accumulate
   image definitions or stale linetype handles.
4. Non-collecting BLOCK_RECORD emission stages metadata and bytes together.
   The pre-collection phase remains transactional, and late registration after
   collection is rejected.

### Verification

- `[dxf][writer]`: 236 assertions in 23 test cases passed after compound
  scopes were added.
- `[dxf][writer][scope]`: 18 assertions in 1 test case passed, including a
  rejecting sink and a short-accepting sink.
- `[dxf][objects][image][writer][reuse]`: 6 assertions in 1 test case passed
  for failure-success retry without duplicate IMAGEDEF records.
- `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only` passed on the warm
  CMake tree after the compound changes.

### Remaining review boundary

The compound writer now has an all-or-nothing in-memory publication boundary,
but callback code can still continue issuing calls after an individual writer
method reports failure. The sticky writer error prevents section commit; a
future callback-status API is needed if early callback termination itself is a
public invariant. Pending-boundary parser tests, version-specific DWG CRC
policy, and physical DataStorage receipts remain incomplete. No strict DWG
release gate is implied by the DXF writer results above.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1152): residual writer barriers, source state, and DWG publication

This final section supersedes rev 1151. It is a codebase review update; no
additional source implementation is attributed to this revision. The latest
writer and parser changes remain in the live tree, but the audit below narrows
the next implementation slices to specific unclosed transitions and lifetime
contracts.

### Verified completed boundary work

1. `dxfRW::setEntityBoundary()` now clears stale pending state for a non-code-0
   probe, and all exact bare calls in the entity parser have been replaced by
   checked status handling. The remaining boundary helpers are used only where
   their context is explicitly classified.
2. `writeTables()` has a section-level byte/state transaction and checks its
   sticky state before and after each delegated table callback. The six
   previously direct ordinary entity writers now use `EntityRecordScope`.
3. `writeBlocks()` and `writeObjects()` check the fixed preamble before entering
   their void callbacks. `writeRawDxfSection()` already checks its complete
   framing chain before committing.
4. Geometry normalization no longer mutates the source object for ELLIPSE,
   LWPOLYLINE, HATCH, MPOLYGON, or dimension type derivation. The source-state
   selector covers 27 assertions in one case.

### Newly confirmed gaps

1. TABLES still has eight `ENDTAB` transitions with no immediate failure gate
   before the next `TABLE` preamble. A failed terminator can therefore cause
   the next table's fixed bytes to be attempted before the section aborts.
   The fix should gate each logical table transition, not mechanically wrap
   every scalar field write.
2. `writeBlocks()` has a pre-callback guard but no post-callback guard before
   its automatic ENDBLK close. A void callback that leaves `writingBlock` set
   after a low-level failure can enter the auto-close path and issue more bytes
   after the failure. The post-callback guard must precede state inspection and
   auto-close.
3. `dwgRW::write()` computes `ok` from finalization, then calls
   `output.commit()` even when `ok` is already false. If finalization fails
   without setting the file stream's fail bit, an incomplete temporary file can
   still be published. The failure branch must abort and preserve the existing
   destination; commit is legal only after every finalization step succeeds.
4. `dxfRW::writeImage()` returns `DRW_ImageDef*` while its
   `EntityRecordScope` commits or rolls back in the destructor. A short parent
   append can roll back and delete the generated definition after the return
   expression has been evaluated, leaving the caller with a dangling pointer.
   The API needs an explicit stable-lifetime contract or a status/handle result
   that cannot expose an object before record commit.
5. `writeLineType()` calls the mutating `DRW_LType::update()` before entering
   its record/state scope. A later failure can leave `path`, `segments`, `size`,
   and `length` changed on caller-owned input. `writeVport()` similarly assigns
   `*ACTIVE`; its rollback is failure-only, so a successful write still changes
   the source name. Both are source-state decisions, not merely byte-scope
   decisions, and need explicit tests and local normalization.
6. Several OBJECTS emitters use `DxfWriterRecordScope` without a corresponding
   state scope. Their handle reservations are intentionally monotonic, but the
   inventory must prove that no supplied-handle, dictionary, carrier, or
   caller-owned field mutation escapes a failed record. Byte atomicity alone is
   not sufficient for these paths.
7. The public `writeBlock()` path is protected by the outer BLOCKS transaction,
   but it has no independent record boundary and manually changes
   `writingBlock`/`currHandle`. The callback contract must state that block
   sequencing is section-owned, or the implementation must add a dedicated
   block-state transaction without breaking the one-open-block invariant.
8. Modern DWG finalizers build physical page vectors locally and flush them
   directly. Existing frame receipts and logical DataStorage receipts do not
   expose the final section/page ids, offsets, stored sizes, alignment,
   checksums, CRCs, or a digest of the emitted bytes. AC1032 still inherits the
   AC1027 container path and has no independent physical-reader evidence.

### Refined implementation sub-plans

#### P1: finish writer publication barriers and ownership

1. Add a small structural transition guard and place it after every TABLES
   `ENDTAB`, immediately after `iface->writeBlocks()`, and at the existing
   OBJECTS/ENTITIES/raw-section boundaries. Keep scalar field writes grouped
   inside their current record or section transaction; do not turn the writer
   into a boolean-returning rewrite of every legacy call.
2. Change `dwgRW::write()` to take the explicit abort path whenever any
   preamble, callback, class/handle phase, header backpatch, finalizer, or
   stream check fails. Add a test with an existing destination and a forced
   finalizer failure proving the destination is byte-for-byte unchanged.
3. Resolve `writeImage()` lifetime before adding more image tests. Preferred
   shape: commit the image record and carrier state before returning a pointer,
   or replace the pointer result with a stable session-owned handle/status and
   make callers query the committed definition. Test success, validation
   failure, short append, retry, and no duplicate reactor/carrier state.
4. Move line-type normalization to a local value or extend the source-state
   snapshot to include every field changed by `update()`. Replace successful
   VPORT input mutation with a local emitted name unless the public API
   explicitly promises that `*ACTIVE` is written back to the caller.
5. Complete the emitter inventory for OBJECTS, PLOTSETTINGS, LAYOUT,
   BLOCK_RECORD, IMAGE, raw replay, and block sequencing. Classify every
   mutation as persistent input, monotonic allocator state, per-attempt state,
   or record-local state, and test failure-success retry for each category.
6. Exit P1 only when the eight table transitions, BLOCKS post-callback guard,
   DWG output abort path, image lifetime, and source-state cases have focused
   regression coverage. A sticky error plus outer rollback remains the public
   callback contract; it does not promise to undo arbitrary callback side
   effects.

#### P2: close parser publication semantics

1. Keep the current checked pending-token model. The next audit is limited to
   `processBlock()`, `processAttrib()`, VERTEX/SEQEND handling, and raw child
   capture; do not introduce a new cursor abstraction unless one of these
   paths cannot express its status without side effects.
2. Stage a parser-owned block event or intermediate block model containing the
   validated header, owned child copies, custom/raw payloads, and footer result.
   Publish `addBlock`, child callbacks, the block map entry, and exactly one
   `endBlock()` only after the complete block is valid. Until staging exists,
   document the weaker already-published-header behavior rather than calling
   it atomic.
3. Reject unknown or duplicate ENDBLK footer fields according to the selected
   compatibility policy. Validate handle presence, owner equality, boundary
   classification, and the next-token handoff in both ASCII and binary input.
4. Add paired tests for malformed ATTRIB, VERTEX, SEQEND, ENDBLK, first-child
   retention, owner mismatch, duplicate handles, and a valid child immediately
   followed by each legal boundary. Assert callbacks, block-map state, and
   pending-token state separately.

#### P3: make DWG integrity and failure policy explicit

1. Add the compatibility/strict integrity policy and location-bearing report
   already specified in the previous active plan. Structural range, id, RS,
   decompression, map-progress, and frame failures remain fatal in both modes;
   only classified CRC/checksum mismatches may remain advisory by default.
2. Add an output transaction test for each modern finalizer family and ensure
   `writer.reset()` cannot turn an unsuccessful finalize into a successful
   publication. Keep failure reports available until the next read starts.
3. Reconcile frame caps, signed offsets, page capacities, and writer admission
   limits before exposing a strict mode as a release guarantee.

#### P4: bind DataStorage to physical receipts

1. Have AC1018/AC1021+ finalizers publish a version-neutral receipt only after
   all page ids, physical order, offsets, sizes, padding, encoding, encryption,
   checksums, and CRCs are final.
2. Key duplicate source revisions by source-row identity plus occurrence in an
   ordered vector. Maps remain lookup aids and cannot define replay order.
3. Decode the emitted test bytes and compare every receipt to the actual page

4. Prove AC1027 and AC1032 independently. Same-version opaque replay is
   preservation; it is not cross-version conversion.

#### P5: maintain honest version/feature evidence

   AC1027, AC1032, and legacy/modern DXF, separating reader, typed writer, raw

3. Record qmake6, sanitizer, full-filter, slow-corpus, and external-reader

2. Use one warm `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only --jobs 8`

## Current Active Plan (rev 1153): writer transaction closure and BLOCK parser admission

This section supersedes rev 1152. Rev 1153 records the completed writer slice
and narrows the next implementation boundary. It does not claim that the
remaining parser publication problem is solved.

### Completed in rev 1153

1. `writeTables()` now emits each `ENDTAB` through one checked helper. A
   failed terminator write cannot be followed by the next table's bytes inside
   the staged TABLES section.
2. `writeBlocks()` checks the callback immediately after
   `iface->writeBlocks()` and before it can synthesize an automatic `ENDBLK`.
3. `dwgRW::write()` commits the output transaction only when all finalization
   phases and the destination stream are good. A failed finalizer aborts the
   temporary output instead of publishing it.
4. `EntityRecordScope` supports an explicit commit. `writeImage()` uses it
   before returning its session-owned `DRW_ImageDef*`; generated definitions
   and reactor inserts are rollback-tracked, and ownership transfer cannot
   leak on vector allocation failure.
5. LTYPE normalization now runs on a copy, and VPORT's synthesized
   `*ACTIVE` name is local to the emitted record. Successful or failed writes
   no longer rewrite those caller-owned fields.
6. Added focused source-state coverage for LTYPE/VPORT; the existing DWG
   finalization-rejection test proves the destination remains absent.

### Evidence

1. `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --changed --compile-only --jobs 8`: passed after
   rev 1153 source changes.
2. `[dxf][writer][source-state]`: 34 assertions, 2 cases, passed.
3. `[dwg-write] dwgRW removes an unfinalized output after callback rejection`:
   3 assertions, 1 case, passed.
4. `git diff --check` passed for the rev 1153 source/test slice.

### Newly active parser boundary

The next slice is P2a, deliberately smaller than full BLOCK event staging:

1. Make `consumeEndBlock()` reject nonzero footer fields it does not model,
   rather than silently accepting arbitrary data between the last child and
   the next record. Preserve only documented ENDBLK codes, including
   version-gated owner and handle fields.
2. Audit `processBlock()` and `processAttrib()` so a failed child parse cannot
   be reported as a successful child or leave a pending entity token to be
   consumed by the next block. The invariant is no public child callback for a
   failed child and no stale boundary state after return.
3. Add malformed ENDBLK and child-failure tests that assert callback counts,
   `endBlock()` balance, block-map admission, and pending-token state.
4. Keep the existing published-header behavior explicit in the test contract:
   a valid BLOCK header may already have reached `addBlock()` before a later
   child/footer failure. Full atomic block publication remains P2b and is not
   smuggled into this narrow parser patch.

### P2a exit criteria

P2a is complete only when malformed footer/child cases fail closed, valid
legacy and modern BLOCKs retain their current callbacks, and the focused DXF
parser suite passes. Then P2b can introduce a staged block event model with a
separate callback-publication test matrix.

### Next execution contract

1. Inspect the reader's exact token handoff and code classification before
   editing; do not guess from the public `DRW_Interface` callbacks.
2. Patch only P2a parser validation and tests in the next source slice.
3. Use the warm DXF target and one focused malformed/block selector; defer
   full filters, qmake6, sanitizers, slow corpus, and external readers to the
   release gates.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1154): atomic BLOCK publication and DWG integrity gates

This section supersedes rev 1153. The P2a parser boundary is implemented and
the next work must not quietly broaden it into a callback-publication rewrite.

### Completed in rev 1154

1. `consumeEndBlock()` now admits only the documented ENDBLK identity, layer,
   subclass, application-group, and XDATA codes. It rejects unknown fields,
   duplicate layer/marker/identity fields, malformed handles, owner mismatch,
   and unbalanced `102` groups before the block record is published.
2. The footer is decoded through a temporary `DRW_Block` with `isEnd` set,
   so the existing entity/XDATA validation rules are reused without exposing
   a synthetic public callback or mutating the parsed BLOCK header.
3. `processBlock()` retains the existing published-header compatibility
   contract: a valid header is reported once, every failure closes the block
   scope once, and the staged `blockRecordMap` entry is committed only after
   the child sequence and ENDBLK footer succeed.
4. Regression coverage proves malformed LINE, ATTRIB, and VERTEX children do
   not call their public child callbacks. It also covers unknown and
   unbalanced ENDBLK data while retaining valid legacy, modern, and balanced
   application-group fixtures.

### Evidence

1. `scripts/dwg-fast-check.sh --test '[dxf][block]' --suite dxf --jobs 8`:
   96 assertions, 18 cases passed.
2. The rev 1154 source/test slice compiled incrementally through the same
   target, and `git diff --check` is clean for the touched source/test files.
3. Existing block tests continue to prove first-child token retention,
   case-insensitive dispatch, owner validation, duplicate self-handle
   rejection, and balanced `endBlock()` callbacks.

### Codebase findings that constrain the next slice

1. `processBlock()` still calls `iface->addBlock()` before parsing children.
   `endBlock()` is a scope-balancing callback, not a commit notification, so
   changing its timing would break current consumers. Full atomic publication
   needs an explicit event buffer and a compatibility decision for callback
   order; it cannot be achieved by moving one call below `processEntities()`.
2. Entity processors such as `processAttrib()` and `processVertex()` already
   validate a completed child before appending it, and parent processors call
   their public callback only after the owned sequence reaches `SEQEND`.
   The remaining risk is direct callback emission during a block, not partial
   child admission inside those processors.
3. `m_hasPendingEntityBoundary` and `nextentity` are private parser state.
   Failure-path tests can prove no subsequent block is consumed from the same
   read, but they cannot inspect the token directly without adding a debug
   API. Do not expose parser internals solely for a test; use callback/map
   receipts and a second independent read instead.
4. ENDBLK XDATA is validated and consumed but is not represented by a public
   end-block object. If lossless footer replay is required later, add a
   parser-owned footer carrier rather than attaching it to the preceding
   BLOCK, because the two records have different handles and ownership.

### Remaining implementation plan

#### P2b: stage BLOCK events without changing the public order accidentally

1. Define a private `DxfBlockEvent` discriminated union covering every
   callback that `processEntities(true)` can emit, including typed entities,
   raw entities, compound-parent snapshots, and child-owned ATTRIB/VERTEX
   data. Store values, not pointers into parser-local objects.
2. Add a temporary block event sink selected only while parsing one BLOCK.
   Entity processors append validated events to that sink; top-level ENTITIES
   and OBJECTS continue to use the existing interface directly. Preserve the
   current event order: `addBlock`, child events in source order, exactly one
   `endBlock`.
3. Keep the block header callback compatibility decision explicit. The first
   implementation may retain the current early `addBlock` publication while
   making child/map publication atomic, or it may add an opt-in staged mode;
   do not silently change LibreCAD's block scope semantics.
4. Commit the staged map record only after the full event stream reaches a
   legal ENDBLK boundary. If a parser allocation fails, clear the event sink,
   clear pending boundary state, and close any already-published scope.
5. Add event-order, callback-count, map-admission, malformed-child, malformed
   footer, and valid-boundary tests for ASCII and binary DXF. Include a block
   with a raw child, an INSERT with multiple ATTRIBs, and a POLYLINE with
   multiple VERTEX records.

#### P3: expose the DWG integrity policy and physical receipts

1. Inventory the current page/frame checks by reader version and classify
   each as fatal structural validation or advisory checksum validation. The
   default compatibility mode may relax only classified checksum mismatches;
   page ids, ranges, RS decode, decompression, object-map progress, and frame
   bounds remain fatal.
2. Add a location-bearing error record containing version, section/page id,
   file offset, logical object handle, and check kind. Preserve it until the
   next read/write attempt so callers can diagnose a rejected file without
   relying on debug logging.
3. Make every modern finalizer publish a physical receipt only after page
   order, offsets, sizes, padding, encoding, encryption, checksums, and CRCs
   are final. Verify receipts against the bytes that will be committed.
4. Add malformed-corpus and writer tests for missing page ids, sparse pages,
   overflow, RS failure, checksum/CRC mismatch, non-advancing HANDLES entries,
   and unsuccessful finalization with an existing destination. Run these in
   the focused lane before enabling slower external-reader gates.

#### P4: version and feature evidence

1. Keep separate read, typed-write, raw-replay, malformed-rejection,
   in-tree-readback, and external-reader rows for AC1012/14/15/18/21/24/27/32
   and legacy/modern DXF.
2. Close an AC1027 row only after DataStorage source rows, object frames,
   opaque section receipts, and same-version replay agree. Close AC1032 only
   after an independent R2018 header/container/object-layout fixture, even
   where the implementation inherits AC1027 code.
3. Record qmake6, sanitizer, full-filter, slow-corpus, and external-reader
   results as `passed`, `failed`, or `skipped` with tool/fixture reasons.

### Next execution contract

1. Before P2b edits, map every `processEntities(true)` callback path and its

2. Implement one event-family slice at a time, with a warm compile and one
