## Historical Active Plan (rev 1198): retain the bounded opaque-table refusal
graph and retain AC1027/AC1032 DataStorage evidence

### Review delta verified for revision 1198

The deferred compound ledger now covers committed INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND and
POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND sequences. `consumeSeqEnd()` transfers a typed receipt
to its consumer, whether the terminator is decoded on demand or was first seen
by the unordered entity sweep. Cached terminators carry no public receipt until
the validated owner consumes them. `readPlineVertex()` returns a private bundle
of staged VERTEX and terminator records; only after `addPolyline()` succeeds
does `readDwgEntity()` emit the parent followed by the bundle in wire order.
The existing child quarantine path discards that bundle on every failed frame,
bad owner, missing/cyclic/duplicate vertex, or invalid terminator.

This completes the ordinary compound-child portion of P7c.3a.i. It does not
complete all entity-frame coverage: `readDwgBlocks()` parses BLOCK and ENDBLK
directly and currently exposes their scope callbacks without ledger records.
Those delimiters cannot be added as a cosmetic callback mirror, because the
current block walk can discover a child failure after `addBlock()`. A separate
scope transaction must define whether and when a BLOCK/ENDBLK receipt is
admissible; until then, a coverage report must explicitly call block-delimiter
coverage partial.

Focused incremental verification rebuilt only `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests`.
The R2010 three-VERTEX polyline passed 24 assertions and proves parent, three
vertices, and terminator receipt order; its R13/R2000 counterpart passed 20.
The updated INSERT checks remain green: AC1032 passed 56 assertions and
R13/R2000 passed 34. The known local `LC_VERSION` warning remains unrelated.

### Review delta verified for revision 1197

Deferred INSERT/ATTRIB receipt publication now follows the existing compound
geometry transaction instead of the individual parse callbacks. A pending
INSERT keeps a staged parent receipt; its validated ATTRIB children keep staged
receipts in the same owner queue. After `consumeSeqEnd()` and the existing
owner/duplicate/completeness checks succeed, `addInsert()` is called and then
one parent receipt followed by the ATTRIB receipts is emitted. Every existing
quarantine, owner, duplicate, or terminator failure clears the matching receipt
queues too, so no rejected compound child can create graph evidence.

R13-R2000 requires a distinct ordering rule: its INSERT body carries only the
first and last ATTRIB handles. The existing boundary validator establishes
membership; the receipt queue therefore uses the validated parsed ATTRIB chain
order for those versions. R2004+ continues to publish the declared handle
order. This distinction is structural DWG behavior, not a compatibility
fallback. SEQEND itself is still deliberately unreported, as are POLYLINE
VERTEX/SEQEND children; the latter remains the next scoped reader ledger work.

Focused incremental verification rebuilt only `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests`.
The AC1032 INSERT/ATTRIB fixture passed 53 assertions and proves exactly one
typed INSERT receipt, one typed ATTRIB receipt, and no SEQEND receipt. The
R13/R2000 three-ATTRIB fixture passed 32 assertions and proves one INSERT plus
the three children appear once in parsed chain order. `git diff --check` is
clean. The persistent local `LC_VERSION` redefinition warning is unrelated to
this receipt path.

### Review delta verified for revision 1196

The reader now emits entity receipts for immediately committed entity frames.
`readDwgEntity()` keeps a single source-handle-bound capture while its existing
`entryParse()` completes the typed common header/handle stream. Raw entity
paths update that same capture, so an ordinary LINE reports `Typed` and a
VIEWPORT reports `TypedAndRaw`; a fixed or generic raw shell reports `Raw`.
The receipt is emitted only after the dispatch arm finishes successfully, so
failed body parses still have no receipt. The capture ignores nested SEQEND
parsing by matching the original source handle.

Compound frames remain intentionally unreported rather than prematurely
published: ATTRIB, SEQEND, and an INSERT retained in `m_pendingInserts` receive
no receipt yet. A POLYLINE parent receives a receipt after its vertex/SEQEND
transaction succeeds, but its consumed VERTEX/SEQEND children do not yet have
their own records. This is partial entity coverage, not a document inventory.

Verification used the existing focused fixtures: the six-version LINE EED
round trip now proves a typed receipt (276 assertions); R2010 VIEWPORT proves
typed-plus-raw (8 assertions); and the R2013 raw-carrier/common-link VIEWPORT
fixture proves the modern receipt (9 assertions).

### Review delta verified for revision 1195

The metadata-side half of the receipt contract now treats a handle as source
identity rather than an overwrite key. `LC_DwgAdvancedMetadata` merges only
receipts whose version, resolved identity, custom-class identity, object/entity
kind, and full validity-tagged common-link tuple agree. It unions distinct
typed/raw carrier views to `TypedAndRaw`; an incompatible reuse of the same
source handle remains retained, marks frame coverage incomplete, and records
the conflicting handle for a later refusal diagnostic. Clearing metadata also
clears this coverage state.

The narrow accumulator test proves typed-plus-raw merging and an incompatible
same-handle type conflict (6 assertions). This still does not make the graph
inventory available: the reader currently emits only OBJECTS receipts. The
entity implementation must stage compound children until the public INSERT or
POLYLINE sequence commits, and must discard all staged receipts on the same
failure paths that already quarantine their entities.

### Review delta verified for revision 1194

P7c.3a now has a reader-issued receipt for every successfully dispatched
OBJECTS frame. `DRW_DwgFramePublication` is emitted once, only after the
complete object parser succeeds. It carries the source handle, encoded and
resolved type, custom-class identity, and the same validity-tagged common
owner/reactor/xdictionary snapshot used by raw carriers. Its carrier is set by
the dispatch itself: `Typed`, `Raw`, or `TypedAndRaw`. A fixed opaque shell,
generic custom fallback, and each intentional legacy opaque fallback report
`Raw`; a typed parser plus its raw preservation carrier reports
`TypedAndRaw`. A failed parser emits no receipt.

`RS_FilterDXFRW` stores these receipts in `LC_DwgAdvancedMetadata`, alongside
rather than derived from raw objects. The callback is source-compatible for
other consumers. The receipt currently covers OBJECTS only: `readDwgEntity()`
still needs its own final publication point because BLOCK ownership and
ATTRIB/VERTEX/SEQEND child handling can defer or combine public callbacks.
The source inventory must not use object-only coverage as a document-wide
graph claim.

Verification used the incremental `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` target.
The DICTIONARY round-trip now proves its `TypedAndRaw` receipt and common
links across the supported writer versions (208 assertions). The raw custom
object replay proves a `Raw` custom-class receipt (108 assertions). The
physical R2010 TABLESTYLE/NOD refusal remains green (29 assertions).

### Review delta verified for revision 1193

P7c.3a now has its first complete reader-to-metadata slice. Modern OBJECTS
records use the existing independent `DRW_TableEntry` probe for both the
common header and `parseDwgCommonHandleData()`. `DRW_UnsupportedObject`,
`RawObjectRecord`, metadata restoration, and opaque-table fingerprints retain
the resulting explicit validity bit, owner, ordered reactors, reactor count,
xdictionary flag, and xdictionary handle. A malformed modern common tail fails
before the raw callback. Legacy OBJECTS records still retain
`commonHandleDataValidated=false`; their zero-valued fields are intentionally
not graph evidence.

The same representation now reaches every modern entity raw carrier. Fixed
opaque shells and generic custom shells copy their successful
`RawEntityShell` common tail. Typed entity paths that retain a raw frame copy
the completed `DRW_Entity` common-tail state after `entryParse()` succeeds.
The raw carrier is not published on a failed typed parse. This includes
VIEWPORT, proxy, modeler, OLE, SHAPE, the supported surface classes, CAMERA,
LIGHT, SECTIONOBJECT, and the generic custom fallback. The legacy custom
fallback deliberately remains unvalidated because its inline layout does not
provide an independently bounded tail.

This is raw-carrier coverage, not the required document-wide graph ledger.
Typed-only frames still discard their common link state after their ordinary
callback. A metadata-side scan cannot repair that omission: it cannot
distinguish a typed-only frame from a raw-only frame or detect incompatible
duplicate frame publications. The next implementation step must therefore add
one reader-issued `DwgFramePublication` event, staged after a complete parse
and before the reader returns success. It must identify the source handle,
encoded and resolved type, custom-class identity, object/entity kind, and the
validity-tagged common links. The event producer, rather than a consumer
heuristic, must state whether the same frame published a typed view, raw view,
or both. `LC_DwgAdvancedMetadata` will merge only identical repeated views and
will mark incompatible duplicate source identities as partial coverage.

refusal passed 29; the raw custom OBJECT lane passed 84; the legacy fixed

### Review delta verified for revision 1192

The next general-reference increment is an input-inventory prerequisite, not
an admission expansion. The current reader validates an OBJECTS common header
on an independent cursor, but that probe stops before
`parseDwgCommonHandleData()`. `DRW_UnsupportedObject` and its metadata copy
therefore retain an owner only where an individual dispatch arm explicitly
copies one. The R2010 `TABLESTYLE` arm does so; generic custom raw objects,
`TABLECONTENT`, and `CELLSTYLEMAP` do not inherit the already parsed common
owner. The carrier also retains neither reactors nor its extension-dictionary
link. A zero owner in that carrier consequently does not establish that the
source object was ownerless.

The existing `RawObjectShell` does validate the common handle tail for modern
unknown custom objects before publishing them, but it discards the decoded
links. Typed metadata records such as `DictionaryRecord` retain owner,
reactor, and xdictionary values, while paired typed/raw representations of
one handle have no normalized carrier or collision protocol. The current
opaque-table fingerprint also cannot detect a mutation to raw common links
that it does not store. These are evidence gaps, not permission to assume
that the links are absent.

The writer has a second hard boundary: its named-object producer always emits
its generated `ACAD_GROUP` entry first and then appends individually
registered entries. It has no sealed source-root-vector API and cannot prove
an arbitrary input root order or a source `ACAD_GROUP` relocation. P7c.3 must
therefore first capture and report the full graph, then add a typed-only root
layout contract if the inventory produces an actually remappable graph. It
must not broaden the existing two-entry TABLESTYLE route, raw replay policy,
or generic dictionary replay.

### Review delta verified for revision 1189

P7c.0c and P7c.0d are now implemented, not remaining design work. The

with only that copy's owner changed to target `0x0c`. The source metadata is

The physical-success search is now bounded by evidence rather than optimism.
`dwgread -O JSON` found no graph matching the exact P7c.0c predicate in 196

cannot exist, but it demonstrates that the two-entry root is not a useful
stand-in for ordinary external R24 drawings, whose NOD has standard sibling
branches. Do not manufacture a fixture by hand to turn this writer-mechanics
proof into a support claim.

The active remaining work is therefore: retain the refusal boundary, make the

### Review delta verified for revision 1188

The source-handle assumption in the first P7c graph predicate is too strong.
`DRW::DwgNamedObjectsDictionaryHandle` (`0x0c`) and
`DRW::DwgAcadGroupDictionaryHandle` (`0x0d`) are identities of LibreCAD's
*output* skeleton; they are not universal input-DWG identities. The live
writer audit finds five places that currently conflate those domains:

1. `inspectDwgOpaqueTableRawObject()` looks up the source root by `0x0c` and
   requires the child owner to be `0x0c`.
2. `validateDwgOpaqueTableReferenceReceipts()` repeats those source checks
   even though its root receipt is necessarily the output NOD at `0x0c`.
3. `writeDwgClasses()` rejects a graph whose source root is not `0x0c` before
   registering the target named entry.
4. `writeObjects()` incorrectly requires the metadata root to equal the target
   root, and writes the selected child with its source owner instead of the
   emitted NOD owner.
5. The consumed-index mechanism correctly prevents the selected source root
   and child from reaching generic dictionary replay, but it has no test that
   proves this remains true when the source root is dynamic.

The correction is deliberately bounded. It does **not** make source NOD
handles generally remappable and it does not replay an arbitrary NOD. For the
one-child TABLESTYLE route, the root source handle may be any unique nonzero
dictionary handle. The selected child must be its only named non-group child,
and is the sole source dictionary emitted as an output object. The writer's
already-proven NOD producer remains the only physical root producer and
always emits target `0x0c -> ACAD_GROUP -> 0x0d`.

The LibreDWG R2010 fixture gives a precise negative oracle for this boundary.
Its decoded root is `0x0b`, not `0x0c`; LibreDWG reports fifteen root entries,
including `ACAD_TABLESTYLE -> 0x43`, and that child has `Standard -> 0x47`.
It is therefore neither an absent-root case nor a minimal source graph. Its
extra root entries and source `ACAD_GROUP` target require a multi-child NOD
transaction or handle relocation, neither of which has a raw-body proof. It
must continue to refuse atomically after the source-root correction.

    definition-only, reactor-only, and paired external handles are rejected
    until a remapped IMAGEDEF/reactor graph has a fixture-backed contract.

### Invariants now enforced

1. A DataStorage row is replayable only when exactly one selected carrier owns
   the source handle, the owner has a matching numeric/lexical identity, the
   opaque section is copied, and the object-frame receipt carries the selected
   operation and admission token. A failed parse, remap, duplicate owner, or
   missing selected carrier rejects the output before publication.
2. Class ordinals are not a universal object property. A frame must have a
   nonzero class ordinal only when the selected raw or typed capability
   requires a CLASSES entry. Fixed types such as LAYOUT legitimately commit
   frame and writer class ordinal zero.
3. Planning is target-version based; it must not ask a newly constructed
   `dwgRW` whether it can write a binding before `dwgRW::write()` sets that
   writer's version. Preflight performs the live capability check after that
   transition.
4. Exact raw DataStorage preservation means the section payload and each
   parser-visible record payload/marker remain equal. It does not mean the
   enclosing DWG byte stream is identical, nor that unrelated source objects
   are serializable.
5. A structurally invalid DataStorage section is a file-level read failure.
   It cannot leave a staged partial index that later exposes an entity with a
   dangling DataStorage-presence bit.

### Remaining implementation queue

#### P7c: R24 TABLESTYLE and related opaque table objects

##### Completed P7c.0b--P7c.0d: bounded source-root mechanics

The source-root translation, late-mutation, and physical-refusal work is
complete. The code and tests establish these limited facts only:

1. The source root is dynamically discovered and used solely as immutable
   source provenance. The target NOD remains `0x0c`; the output has no frame
   at a dynamic source-root handle.
2. The selected child and raw TABLESTYLE handles are preserved, the emitted
   child copy is reparented to `0x0c`, and raw bytes are never patched. The
   source root and child are both excluded from generic dictionary replay.
3. The frozen plan/receipts reject every tested graph or raw mutation before
   staged publication. The external R2010 graph is retained as a real refusal
   oracle: it proves decoded provenance and an untouched pre-existing target,
   not accepted preservation.
4. A synthetic raw TABLESTYLE remains planning/refusal evidence only. It is
   intentionally not written successfully or reread as a payload oracle.

##### P7c.1: qualify physical success evidence

1. Complete: the legally redistributable LibreDWG R2010 fixture proves the
   safe result for an external TABLESTYLE hierarchy: import succeeds and
   same-version export refuses atomically. It deliberately remains a refusal
   fixture, not a graph-complete success source.
2. Complete: immutable preflight tuples and per-attempt runtime receipts now
   make refusal actionable without changing admission policy. Focused tests
   cover the original unverified-body, source-group, owner/cardinality,

   Target NOD/child/raw receipt diagnostics remain covered at the low-level

3. A graph-complete R2010, R2013, or R2018 fixture may be added only when a
   legally redistributable, independently generated source meets all of these

   one canonical child; one typed-parser-validated TABLESTYLE raw frame; no

4. Do not block P7c or fabricate a success fixture if that source never
   appears. The two completed scans found none, which is expected for normal

5. A fixture with a fixed LTYPE or STYLE relationship is accepted only when

1. This is a maintenance rule, not a feature queue. Any edit to opaque-table

2. Continue to refuse nonfixed text styles/linetypes, style/content links,
   values, blocks, fields, attributes, and geometry. Their target handle must

3. Keep `CELLSTYLEMAP`, `TABLECONTENT`, and `ACAD_TABLE` on distinct admission

Do not patch arbitrary opaque bytes to make external handles fit LibreCAD's

remaining terminator and polyline work was completed in rev 1198.

###### P7c.3b: build a read-only, coverage-aware source inventory

1. Add a pure inventory builder over the reader ledger and advanced metadata.

   entry, owner, reactor, xdictionary, and class/body relation. Escape names
   in diagnostic output exactly as `dwg-admission-report` already does.
2. Discover a candidate root by tracing each opaque-table raw object's
   verified owner through exactly one dictionary chain to exactly one
   ownerless dictionary. This is source provenance only: do not look up the
   imported root by output handle `0x0c`, and do not call every ownerless
   dictionary a NOD. Missing, cyclic, duplicate, or ambiguous chain members
   make that root `refuse`.
3. Inventory every source root entry in wire order, including its name,
   target handle, target node carrier, and child common owner. Build reverse
   indexes for all verified owner/reactor/xdictionary links so inbound edges
   from elsewhere in the drawing are visible. Dictionary entries form typed
   outbound edges. Typed class-specific body extractors may add outbound
   edges only from a versioned, specification-backed field ledger.
4. A raw body contributes its verified common links, but its body links are
   `OpaqueUnknown` until an exhaustive, version-specific decoder ledger
   proves otherwise. `typedPayloadValidated` proves a parser accepted its

   coverage, a partial typed extractor, or an opaque body that might observe a
   relocated handle is an inventory refusal, never an empty edge set.
5. Extend the hidden report with deterministic `graph-root`, `graph-node`,
   and `graph-edge` lines plus a root-level `candidate=refuse` reason list.

4. Keep the classification data immutable in a planner-owned record with

### Implementation order and boundaries

1. Completed: immutable preflight tuples, per-attempt runtime receipts, the
   read-only test query, and the R2010 refusal rerun are in place. They do not
   alter raw bytes, class-registration timing, generic dictionary replay, or

   owner/reactor/xdictionary absence from today’s incomplete carrier. Implement

### Incremental verification

1. Build only `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` for P7c and rerun its exact
   Catch2 selectors with `--no-build` after the executable is current. Run the
   AC1027/AC1032 DataStorage selectors only when shared admission code changes.
   Reserve broad DWG suites, sanitizers, and full CMake/qmake builds for a
   changed shared boundary.
2. For manifest changes, run `validate_fixture_manifest.py`,
   `hash_fixtures.py --check`, `test_fixture_manifest.py`, and the gap-report
   check. The optional `libredwg:open` receipt may be `skipped` when the tool
   is absent; it must never be silently recorded as a successful external
   validation.
3. Before a P7 family is marked complete, verify both output-absence checks
   and reader callbacks. A false return alone is insufficient if a staged
   target remains on disk or a malformed child was already published. A
   successful result must also prove the relevant handle/class/object graph on
   reread, not merely that the low-level writer returned true.
4. A source-graph test is not complete until it checks both structural views:
   the writer's emitted NOD/child/raw receipts and a fresh reader's decoded
   NOD entry, child owner/entry, raw parent/class tuple, and relationship
   handle. The two views catch a bookkeeping-only receipt and an unreachable
   raw object respectively.

### Exit criteria for rev 1192

1. P6b remains green with exact section/record evidence, typed fixed-owner
   receipt coverage, same-version acceptance, and atomic cross-version and
   handle-collision rejection.
2. P6d proves the two physical parser/replay failures without partial public
   state. P6c independently proves the same bounded owner/payload/replay
   contract for AC1032.
3. The frozen P7 plan is the sole policy source for CLASSES, BLOCKS, ENTITIES,
   and OBJECTS. No P7 family recomputes raw/typed/refusal safety after the plan
   is frozen, and a refused save preserves both absent and pre-existing
   destinations.
4. P7c has a collision-resistant raw/summary identity proof, a reader-issued
   known-payload provenance marker, a physical target NOD and selected
   child-dictionary receipt, immutable root/child/raw graph fingerprints, and
   one immutable policy per modern raw OBJECT frame. Post-CLASSES source
   mutation and the real external R2010 hierarchy fail atomically before
   publication. The implemented source-root translation remains limited to
   the two-entry TABLESTYLE spine: the source root may differ from output
   `0x0c`, while the source group remains `0x0d` and child/raw identities are
   byte-stable. Preflight and later runtime failures are reported from their
   separate immutable plan and per-attempt receipt domains, and the explicit
   local report exposes that evidence without touching the source path. No
   source is called supported until a provenance-pinned
   physical R24 fixture proves fresh-reader reachability and payload identity;
   synthetic tests cannot satisfy this criterion. All other R24 table
   relations and nonzero WIPEOUT partner handles remain refused unless their
   complete typed or raw relationship is proven before CLASSES.
5. P7c.3 cannot start a writer transaction until raw common links have an
   explicit validity bit, the reader ledger covers every participating frame,
   the graph report distinguishes `TypedAndRaw` from duplicates, and every
   root edge has one of the three documented classifications. The current NOD
   writer's append-only entry API is not a general-order proof.
6. No documentation or release claim states that whole-file modeler export is
   complete solely from the AC1027 and AC1032 DataStorage tests.

### Non-goals for rev 1192

1. No typed ACIS/SAB conversion, cross-version opaque DataStorage conversion,
   full-file byte identity, or mandatory external oracle.
2. No guessed R24 TABLESTYLE encoder, synthetic IMAGEDEF for a WIPEOUT, raw
   byte patching, broad external-resource rewrite, or hard-coded anonymous
   block-name policy.
3. No semantic-name substitution for opaque relationship handles, no claim
   that local fixed-handle receipt tests accept arbitrary external DWGs, and
   no copied sibling-repository fixture without independently documented
   redistribution rights.
4. No raw-body handle scanner, heuristic source-NOD remap, unordered NOD
   append workaround, or conversion of a missing graph ledger into an empty
   relation set. Those approaches would hide exactly the relationships P7c.3
   is intended to prove.

## Historical Plan (rev 1206): complete reader evidence before graph use

### Review result and completed baseline

The source-location baseline is now in the reader. `readDwgHandles()` retains
the HANDLE-map decode order in `stagedEntries`, carries it in `objHandle`, and
seeds an ordered source-frame vector only after the map's CRC and complete
stream have validated. `DRW_DwgFramePublication` now receives the map ordinal,
object offset, and physical-versus-decoded address space at its one public
publication boundary. `LC_DwgAdvancedMetadata` compares that location when it
coalesces same-frame views. This removes the previous false dependence on
`unordered_map` iteration.

The narrow control-flow repair is also complete: a false
`walkBlockRecordEntities()` result, or a new owned-entity failure during that
walk, now makes `blockScopeFailure` true. The block's source rows are then
quarantined. The focused incremental checks pass after this change:

1. `RS_FilterDXFRW rejects a serialized INSERT child-owner mismatch atomically`
   passes with 64 assertions. It proves malformed INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND source
   rows have no publication, and the final report is `FinalizedPartial`.
2. `dwgRW user blocks retain POLYLINE and INSERT compound children` passes
   with 162 assertions.
3. `LC_DwgAdvancedMetadata merges matching DWG frame publications` passes
   with 7 assertions. It proves that matching receipts alone never imply
   complete coverage; only a `FinalizedComplete` report does.

P0.1's basic implementation is now present. The public entry carries a live
disposition, stable reason, and publication count; all ordinary publication
paths use a single receipt helper; and `dwgRW::processDwg()` finalizes one
HANDLE-map report after the later reader phases. The metadata compatibility
boolean starts false and becomes true only for an internally consistent
`FinalizedComplete` report. This is a useful checkpoint, not evidence that
the complete P0 contract or normal-file completeness has been reached.

P0.2 is also complete. `DwgSourceFrameId` now carries the existing HANDLE-map
tuple through typed entity, object, compound-child, and raw-paired receipt
construction. Receipt delivery validates all four fields against the ledger
before any public callback or `Published` transition. The HANDLE-map parser
also stages physical offsets across every group and rejects aliases with the
specific `ObjectMapDuplicateOffset` diagnostic before it commits either map
or ledger. The R15, R18, and R21 adapters each make one base-parser call per
attempt with their correct physical or decoded address space.

The focused P0.2 checks pass in `librecad_fast_tests`:

1. duplicate offsets within one HANDLE-map group: 4 assertions;
2. duplicate offsets across groups: 4 assertions;
3. forged source identity leaves the source row `Pending`: 7 assertions;
4. a valid two-group map retains source-map ordinals 0 and 1: 8 assertions.

Those are foundations, not a completed source-ledger contract. The next work
remains strictly reader-side. It does not widen DWG writing or relax the R24
opaque-table refusal.

The first P0.3 and P0.4 checkpoints are now implemented as well. Quarantine
is idempotent for already failed/quarantined rows, rejects unknown and
published rows without adding a quarantine marker, and its block-ownership
cleanup removes a map entry only after the ledger accepted the terminal
state. Entity-to-object deferral now accepts its exact `Deferred` transition
before it enqueues the object-pass map entry, and block-owned map entries
quarantine through their captured source identity. The unused `SkippedLegacy` public disposition was removed: versions
without a HANDLE map remain `NotAvailable` rather than manufacturing a
source-frame state. Receipt callbacks, direct entity/object callback
recovery, process exits, and coverage-report delivery now leave mapped frames
internally partial instead of leaving coverage in progress. This does not make
every callback boundary exact yet: the direct entity/object recovery catch
also contains unexpected decoder/allocation exceptions, while TABLES/header
delivery is contained at batch rather than individual-callback granularity.
P0.4 remains in progress until source attribution is explicit.

The focused incremental evidence for these checkpoints is:

1. failed-row quarantine is idempotent: 8 assertions;
2. published and missing-row quarantine is rejected without a side marker:
   10 assertions;
3. a throwing mapped LINE callback leaves its row `Failed` with
   `CallbackException`: 9 assertions;
4. a throwing receipt callback leaves the row unpublished and failed:
   6 assertions;
5. a throwing coverage-report callback leaves internal status
   `FinalizedPartial`: 5 assertions.
6. mapped fixed-object deferral records the exact source row as `Deferred`:
   8 assertions.
7. a malformed table record restores its object-map entry while retaining the
   source row as `TableDeferred`: 122 assertions in the table rollback
   fixture.
8. a forged identity cannot quarantine a pending source row or add a side
   marker: 7 assertions.
9. a throwing table callback returns `BAD_READ_TABLES` and emits one
   `FinalizedPartial` report without a staged table receipt: 6 assertions.
10. a typed LAYER receipt follows its accepted table callback and retains its
   exact source location: 9 assertions.
11. a deferred raw control reaches its raw callback and one source-bound
   `Raw` receipt: 12 assertions; the legacy source-less path still passes
   its existing 5-assertion test.
12. a throwing deferred-raw callback leaves its mapped frame failed with
   `CallbackException` and no receipt: 6 assertions.

The existing malformed R2000 INSERT owner regression (64 assertions) and the
compound user-block regression (162 assertions) remain green after these
state-machine changes.

### Findings from this review

1. **Receipt delivery now has exact source identity; map transfers do not.**
   `DwgSourceFrameId` gates publication and the checked transition overload,
   but the compatibility overload used by deferred cleanup still reconstructs
   an id from a bare handle. Quarantine now validates before it changes a map
   or side marker, but P0.3 must remove the remaining convenience path from
   parser map transfers so every consumer carries its original map entry
   instead of re-looking it up after an erase or move.
2. **HANDLE-map seeding is now bijective.**
   Duplicate handles and duplicate physical offsets are rejected across the
   full staged map; zero remains valid when the active object-stream range
   admits it. The remaining work is to preserve that captured identity across
   every later map transfer.
3. **Terminal cleanup is now idempotent, but transfer ownership is mixed.**
   `quarantineDwgFrame()` now preserves an already failed/quarantined row and
   fails closed for an unknown or published row. Its block cleanup uses the
   result before erasing a source map entry. Other direct `ObjectMap` and
   `objObjectMap` erases still need the same captured-source discipline.
4. **Finalization survives delivery failure, but not every boundary is exact.**
   Header, table, block, entity, object, and raw-section phase boundaries now
   preserve their phase-specific error on an exception. Table/header delivery
   is still batch-level rather than an individual callback boundary.
   `publishDwgFramePublication()` calls the interface before changing the
   ledger, now uses `CallbackException`, and `processDwg()` owns a
   non-throwing best-effort finalizer. Direct entity/object recovery also
   records `CallbackException` when a mapped frame unwinds. That preserves an
   honest partial result, but it cannot promise rollback of an event the
   consumer already received or distinguish every non-callback exception.
5. **BLOCK callback publication is still speculative.**
   `readDwgBlocks()` calls `intfa.addBlock(bk)` before the named block's
   entities are walked, and `readDwgEntity()` contains more than fifty direct
   interface calls, including typed and raw carrier pairs. Receipt suppression
   is now correct for a failed walk, but a malformed child can still have
   opened a consumer block and delivered earlier children. The existing
   global pending INSERT/orphan ATTRIB structures also let one incomplete
   scope affect a later delimiter-receipt decision.
6. **Callback exceptions need a separate, honest contract.**
   Staging can guarantee that malformed bytes produce no public callbacks.
   It cannot make arbitrary pre-existing `DRW_Interface` callbacks atomic if
   a consumer throws halfway through replay: prior callbacks have already
   reached external state and there is no generic undo API. The plan must not
   claim otherwise. Such a failure is reported as partial external delivery;
   it is not repaired by rolling back `RS_FilterDXFRW`.
7. **TABLES and raw-control paths keep source frames invisible.**
   `readDwgTables()` keeps erased source handles for rollback, but its
   successful controls and typed records never issue frame receipts.
   `stagedRawControls` later reaches `publishDeferredRawObjects()` through
   `addUnsupportedObject()` without any frame receipt at all. Thus every
   ordinary DWG with tables remains necessarily partial under the current
   all-published predicate.
8. **CLASSES has a separate ordered source lane.**
   `dwgReader15`, `dwgReader18`, and `dwgReader21` stage class vectors in
   stream order and only then call `publishDwgClasses()`, but retain no public
   evidence. Classes are not HANDLE-map frames, so they must not be faked as
   them. The class reader needs its own records, byte/bit ranges, and final
   status, linked from custom frame receipts by class number.
9. **The graph and writer remain deliberately blocked.**
   No `DwgSourceGraphInventory` exists yet. The current admission report only
   describes writer-side policy. It cannot infer source order, complete
   roots, or opaque-body edges from raw metadata, and must not enable raw
   TABLESTYLE/CELLSTYLEMAP/TABLECONTENT replay.

### P0: finish the remaining source-frame state machine

#### P0.3: centralize source-frame consumption and completion

1. Replace ad-hoc `ObjectMap.erase`, `objObjectMap.erase`, and
   `remainingMap` transfers in DWG reader paths with narrowly named helpers:
   `takePendingSourceFrame`, `deferSourceFrame`, `publishSourceFrame`,
   `failSourceFrame`, and `quarantineSourceFrame`. Each accepts the captured
   `DwgSourceFrameId`, verifies the permitted transition, and only then
   changes its map or side set. It returns false without mutation on an
   invalid state. An already `Failed` or `Quarantined` row can be cleaned up
   idempotently; a `Published` row cannot be relabelled or quarantined.
2. Audit the exact consumers in `readDwgTables`, `readDwgBlocks`,
   `walkBlockRecordEntities`, `readPlineVertex`, `consumeSeqEnd`,
   `readDwgEntities`, `deferObject`, and `readDwgObjects`. Include all early
   fixed-object/custom-class deferrals, `remainingMap` paths, invalid SEQEND
   cleanup, and end-of-pass pending/orphan cleanup. No frame may bypass this
   list because it did not become a normal entity.
3. Split receipt construction from receipt delivery. A construction helper
   only enriches a validated payload with its immutable source identity.
   The delivery helper performs the single public callback and then makes the
   `Published` transition. If no source row exists, delivery fails closed and
   creates no source-less receipt.
4. Keep the existing process-end finalization for normal returns, but route
   every map-transfer failure through the same source-row reason before it
   returns. P0.4 owns the non-throwing exit guard for callback exceptions.
   Raw-section/DataStorage callbacks remain section evidence and do not enter
   the HANDLE-map completion count.
5. Completed: the unused `SkippedLegacy` disposition was removed. Preserve
   the existing `NotAvailable` status for formats without a HANDLE map; do
   not replace it with a synthetic per-frame lifecycle.

#### P0.4: make consumer delivery failure explicit

1. Add `CallbackException` to the coverage reason vocabulary. It describes a
   consumer-delivery failure, never malformed source bytes. Keep it distinct
   from `ParseFailure`, `PhaseAborted`, and an invalid internal transition.
2. Completed checkpoint: a non-throwing process-scope finalizer now runs
   immediately after a valid
   HANDLE map. It sets internal status and resolves pending/deferred rows on
   every normal return and stack unwind. Its report callback is best effort:
   failure to deliver that callback cannot leave the reader internally
   `InProgress` or turn the source result into complete.
3. Completed checkpoint: the header, table, block, entity, object, and
   raw-section process boundaries preserve their phase-specific error and
   stop later phases on a thrown callback. Continue with individual source
   attribution: on a thrown callback, mark the current source frame `Failed`
   with `CallbackException` when known. Prior callbacks are deliberately not
   undone. For a named block, call `endBlock` only as the current best-effort
   balancing callback after a successful `addBlock`.
4. Keep receipt publication ordered as it is: only an interface call that
   returned normally may transition the source row to `Published`. The
   finalizer exposes any interrupted row as partial rather than guessing
   whether the consumer acted before it threw.

### P1: make malformed BLOCK input callback-atomic

#### P1.1: introduce a narrow, complete entity callback surface

1. Do not derive a journal from the full `DRW_Interface`: it would duplicate
   unrelated header/table methods and make omission likely. Introduce a narrow
   `DwgEntitySink` used only by `readDwgEntity` and compound helpers. Generate
   its complete method list from one local X-macro declaration covering every
   direct dispatch now visible in `readDwgEntity`: typed values, pointer
   forms, raw-object carriers, and the paired typed/raw arms.
2. Add `DwgDirectEntitySink`, an adapter that forwards that list to the real
   `DRW_Interface`. Convert every current direct `intfa.add...` in the entity
   switch, the INSERT commit lambda, and POLYLINE completion to that sink.
   The X-macro also supplies test-visible event names and a compile-time count
   so a new dispatch cannot silently bypass journal staging.
3. Add `DwgBlockCallbackJournal` as the other sink implementation. It stores
   value callbacks by owned copy and pointer callbacks in owned storage; no
   closure may retain a parser-stack pointer. Bound its event and byte growth
   by existing DWG safety limits and fail the block safely on allocation or
   limit failure.

#### P1.2: parse each BLOCK_RECORD as one reader transaction

1. Add `DwgBlockScopeTransaction` to own a parsed BLOCK/ENDBLK pair, declared
   ordered children, journal events, child source identities, and a local
   INSERT/ATTRIB/SEQEND or POLYLINE/VERTEX/SEQEND registry. An unresolved
   compound child belongs to the owning BLOCK_RECORD at the moment it is
   deferred; it cannot be decided from global queues belonging to a later
   block.
2. Parse the whole owned group through the journal before any consumer
   callback. The parser may consume its own source-map entries, but a failed
   group quarantines the delimiters, every declared owned handle, and every
   locally consumed compound child immediately. Do not leave recovery to the
   unordered entity sweep.
3. For named blocks, successful replay order is `addBlock`, child journal
   events in BLOCK_RECORD order, `endBlock`, then the BLOCK/child/ENDBLK frame
   receipts in source-map order. For model/paper space, stage the full group
   first, then preserve the existing `addBlock`, `endBlock`, post-scope entity
   routing on successful replay. Receipt timing remains after all consumer
   entity events in both cases.
4. Delete the global `m_pendingInserts.empty()` and `m_orphanAttribs.empty()`
   receipt guard once every owned compound is local to the transaction. Keep
   a separate orphan policy for genuinely ownerless frames in the later sweep;
   its result is a source-row reason, not a veto on another block's receipt.
5. Structural malformed-input atomicity is the P1 acceptance condition: a
   malformed child produces no `addBlock`, child, `endBlock`, raw-carrier, or
   frame-receipt callback for that block. A throwing consumer is instead the
   P0.4 partial-external-delivery case; no P1 test may claim that already
   delivered callbacks were undone.

### P2: complete TABLES, raw, and CLASSES evidence

#### P2.1: stage TABLES receipts with the existing table transaction

1. Completed checkpoint: typed table records now stage a source-bound
   `entity=false` receipt alongside `erasedObjectHandles`. The receipt carries
   its HANDLE-map id, record name, common-object links, and `Typed` carrier;
   all table source rows first become `TableDeferred` before their map entry
   is removed. Wire type codes remain a follow-up because the generic table
   parser does not retain them through the table map.
2. Completed checkpoint: after all existing table callbacks return normally,
   `libdwgr.cpp` publishes the staged typed receipts in HANDLE-map ordinal
   order. A table callback exception bypasses the entire batch; the process
   finalizer reports partial coverage. The R2000 LAYER fixture proves receipt
   timing and a throwing layer fixture proves receipt suppression.
3. Completed checkpoint: a failed table parse clears staged receipts and
   restores the object map unchanged. The process-level finalizer reports the
   rows unresolved; it must not report them published merely because a local
   table map briefly contained a record.
4. Completed checkpoint: `publishDeferredRawObjects()` now requires the raw
   callback to return normally before it publishes one source-bound `Raw`
   receipt. A mapped callback failure marks the source `CallbackException`;
   a legacy source-less delivery remains valid but deliberately emits no
   fabricated receipt. The R2000-style raw-control test and the pre-HANDLE-map
   legacy test cover both paths; a mapped throwing callback has its own
   receipt-suppression regression.

#### P2.2: add an independent class-stream ledger

1. Define `DRW_DwgClassCoverageEntry`, separate from HANDLE-map frames, with
   class-stream ordinal; class number; record, class, and application names;
   entity/proxy flags; instance count; version; and parsed data/string stream
   bit ranges. Its section location is explicitly decoded-buffer-relative.
2. Capture the ranges around each `DRW_Class::parseDwg()` in reader15,
   reader18, and reader21. Reuse each reader's existing staged vector order;
   do not derive class ordering from `classesmap`.
3. Give the class lane the same explicit lifecycle vocabulary as frame
   coverage, but keep it logically independent: finalization records whether
   the CLASSES phase itself reached a valid, published stream even if a later
   HANDLE-map phase fails. A duplicate number, invalid footer, parser-bound
   failure, or class callback exception finalizes that lane partial rather
   than silently omitting evidence. Custom frame receipts reference a
   validated class number and class-stream ordinal where one exists.

#### P2.3: distinguish absent links from validated links

1. Replace the ambiguous `m_commonHandleDataValidated` boolean in new evidence
   with `CommonLinkEvidence::{NotApplicable, Validated, AbsentInLegacy,
   Invalid}`. Preserve the old boolean only as a compatibility projection.
2. Audit fixed/custom raw objects, raw entities, `remainingMap`, deferred
   objects, and DataStorage-bearing shells. Each source frame ends with one
   disposition; each *published* frame has exactly one receipt carrier only
   after frame bounds, class resolution, and applicable common-handle parsing
   have passed. Do not infer an empty relationship list from an unavailable
   legacy tail or opaque body.

### P3: build a report-only source graph after P0--P2 are complete

1. Implement `DwgSourceGraphInventory` as a pure reader-metadata consumer.
   It accepts only `FinalizedComplete` source evidence plus a final class
   report. `NotAvailable`, `InProgress`, `FinalizedPartial`, a conflicting
   receipt, or a raw body with unknown links rejects construction.
2. Use HANDLE-map ordinal for frame ordering, CLASSES stream ordinal for
   classes, dictionary vector order for dictionary entries, and decoded
   reactor order for reactor edges. `(offset, handle)` is only a diagnostic
   tie breaker; no graph edge may come from unordered container iteration.
3. Emit only verified typed edges: dictionary membership, common owner,
   reactor, xdictionary, and per-version typed-body ledgers that list all
   handles. A raw body contributes `OpaqueUnknownBody`, never an inferred
   empty edge set.
4. Extend `dwg-admission-report` with deterministic `frame-status`,
   `class-status`, `graph-node`, `graph-edge`, and `graph-root` lines. This is
   diagnostic-only and cannot affect current admission or output behavior.

### P4: retain the existing writer boundary

1. Only after P0--P3 may the writer classify an edge as
   `identity-preserved`, `typed-remappable`, or `opaque-unpatchable`. Partial
   evidence, unknown raw links, changed common links, class mismatch, or an
   unmodeled inbound edge remains `opaque-unpatchable` and atomically refuses
   its root.
2. Keep R24 TABLESTYLE, CELLSTYLEMAP, TABLECONTENT, and ACAD_TABLE raw replay
   refused. The first permitted expansion remains a complete typed,
   versioned encoder verified by fresh-reader physical receipts, never a raw
   named-object-dictionary rewrite.
3. AC1027/AC1032 DataStorage stays a same-version structural contract. It
   neither completes general source coverage nor permits raw cross-version
   replay or typed ACIS/SAB conversion.

### Proof, order, and fast execution

1. Continue P0.3 through every map-transfer site. The initial focused checks
   prove failed-row idempotence, rejected published/missing rows, and the
   absence of a quarantine-set side effect. Add one test for each remaining
   `ObjectMap`/`objObjectMap` transfer that a rejected source changes neither
   its parser map nor its side set. Exercise one normal finalization and every
   aborted process phase, each with exactly one `FinalizedPartial` report.
2. Continue P0.4 before the block journal. The focused receipt, direct LINE,
   and coverage-report throwing callbacks now prove internally partial
   coverage. Add throwing test interfaces for
   a table callback, an entity callback, and the coverage-report callback.
   Assert failure and internally partial coverage, then assert only the
   callbacks before the throw were externally observable. No test asserts
   rollback.
3. Then implement P1. Extend the existing malformed R2000 owner fixture to
   assert no model-space block or child callbacks after journal staging. Add a
   named-block case, an R2004+ `entMap` case, a successful exact event-order
   case. The separate P0.4 tests own the throwing-callback boundary.
4. Implement P2 in two commits: table/raw receipts first, then the three
   CLASSES readers and custom-class linkage. Test table rollback, table
   callback failure before the staged receipt batch, a late raw control,
   duplicate classes, invalid class footer/bounds, and an ordinary DWG whose
   complete report is possible only after table receipts exist.
5. Build P3 as a standalone metadata test target before wiring the command.
   Test source ordering, ambiguous roots, owner cycles, opaque bodies, and
   inbound reactor/xdictionary edges. Every unsafe case must refuse graph
   construction without invoking writer code.
6. During P0--P2, use only the incremental
   `librecad_dwg_write_fast_tests` target and exact Catch2 selectors. The
   three selectors listed in the completed baseline are the first regression
   gate. Run broader DWG suites or ASan/UBSan only when a shared buffer/frame
   helper changes; run DataStorage selectors only for DataStorage paths.

### Non-goals

1. No speculative second parse, callback undo in `RS_FilterDXFRW`, raw-byte
   handle patching, source-order inference from unordered containers, or
   pretending a missing report is complete.
2. No new DWG writer version, broad opaque R24 table acceptance, typed
   ACIS/SAB conversion, cross-version DataStorage replay, or whole-file
   preservation claim.
3. No DXF behavior change in this slice. The new default interface reports
   remain DWG-only evidence and do not promote DXF raw/typed coverage.

## Current Active Plan (rev 1215): make deferred compound frames recoverable

### Completed work removed from the active queue

The HANDLE-map ledger, exact receipt identity validation, duplicate-offset
rejection, deferred table-record receipts, deferred raw-control receipts, and
best-effort HANDLE-map finalization are implemented. The focused malformed
compound regressions, table receipt/callback regressions, and raw-control
regressions pass on the incremental DWG target. They remain historical proof;
they are not repeated as active implementation work.

This revision deliberately does not call the remaining work "complete DWG
coverage". Standard table control frames still have no receipt, CLASSES has
no independent public coverage report, and several parser-map transfers still
reconstruct a source identity from only a handle. Until those gaps are closed,
`FinalizedComplete` must remain a conservative result rather than a normal
file expectation.

R1.0 is complete in the current worktree. The new side-effect-free deferred
compound validator runs before EOF abandonment; five focused state-contract
tests passed 54 assertions, and the adjacent INSERT/SEQEND/source-lease
regressions passed 43 assertions. An empty unparsed ATTRIB list may omit its
receipt vector in the current representation; every non-empty or unmatched
covered companion is now a structural failure before cleanup mutates state.

### Rev 1215 codebase audit

The previous revision correctly identified the reader boundary, but the
current implementation makes the ownership problem more concrete:

1. `readDwgObjects()` is the only normal sweep using `DwgFrameMapLease` from
   detach through terminal discard. `readDwgEntities()` and both
   `walkBlockRecordEntities()` branches still call `takeDwgSourceFrame()` and
   erase before `readDwgEntity()` has accepted a parse, deferred an object, or
   staged a compound record. Their later `markDwgFrameOutcome(Failed)` call
   updates evidence but cannot recover the erased node. `deferObject()` also
   still uses the older value-lease transfer, so its allocation/collision
   failure follows an already-erased entity source.
2. Deferred INSERT state is split between `m_pendingInserts`,
   `m_pendingInsertFramePublications`, and
   `m_pendingAttribFramePublications`. Orphans have a parallel pair of maps;
   parked SEQENDs are divided among a valid-handle set, owner map, receipt map,
   and consumed-handle set. The ATTRIB append path now reserves and avoids
   initial `operator[]`, but INSERT orphan adoption still assigns through
   `m_pendingAttribFramePublications[e.handle]`. That can overwrite a stale
   companion receipt after the ATTRIB objects have already moved. The model has
   no single owner that can either restore every node or abandon every exact
   receipt.
3. `consumeSeqEnd(..., borrowedLease)` is not a recoverable borrow when a
   SEQEND was seen by the unordered sweep: it synthesizes a value lease from a
   stored receipt after the node was removed from both maps. POLYLINE likewise
   pre-borrows all children but takes them one at a time; a later take or
   SEQEND commit failure leaves earlier vertices unavailable for restore. The
   same window exists for a complete INSERT after it consumes its SEQEND but
   before the parent/ATTRIB receipt sequence is accepted.
4. `Deferred` presently means both "resident in `objObjectMap`" and
   "compound record awaiting a future parent". A detached compound node has
   no truthful ledger state: marking it `Deferred` loses residency meaning;
   leaving it `Pending` says it remains map-owned. Add a distinct transient
   `Staged` disposition and `CompoundStaged` reason. Finalization maps
   `Pending`, `Deferred`, and `Staged` to `Unresolved`; receipt publication
   accepts a staged source exactly once. Exact rollback may restore
   `Staged -> Pending` only while its original node is reinserted with zero
   publications; no generic handle-only reverse transition is permitted.
5. Generic borrow/discard, SEQEND, POLYLINE, and block cleanup now reject dual
   residency. The remaining audit must cover every direct paired
   `ObjectMap.find()` / `objObjectMap.find()` lookup and every detached-node
   destructor path. A `DwgFrameMapLease` must be explicitly restored,
   transferred, or terminally discarded; silently destroying a nonempty node
   is a reader-invariant failure. `remainingMap` remains diagnostics-only,
   never a third parser owner.
6. A malformed input rejection before the first callback and a consumer
   callback failure have different contracts. The former restores detached
   nodes until the phase chooses one exact-source quarantine/failed outcome;
   it emits neither business callback nor receipt. The latter cannot retract
   observed callbacks: terminalize the delivered prefix, quarantine/fail the
   undispatched suffix, and report partial delivery. R1 preserves this current
   callback policy; R4 alone makes BLOCK callback admission atomic.
7. `stageCurrentEntityFrame()` now rejects a covered publication unless its
   exact detached `DwgFrameMapLease` is present. This closes the temporary
   receipt-only staging loophole, but it also confirms that the normal parser
   cannot use the aggregate maps until its map-owning sweeps pass a live lease
   into the entity dispatch. `readDwgEntity()` is not yet a parse-only helper:
   it mixes bounded parsing, deferred-object routing, compound bookkeeping,
   business callbacks, and receipt publication. R1.3 must introduce a narrow
   mapped ownership context around this existing function before extracting
   compound-specific operations; a wrapper that simply calls it after
   `takeDwgSourceFrame()` would preserve the very lost-node bug being fixed.
8. The first R1.3 slice is implemented: `readMappedDwgEntity()` owns one
   detached `ObjectMap` node while the current callbackful dispatcher runs,
   transfers fixed/custom OBJECTS through `deferDetachedDwgSourceFrame`, and
   discards a simple frame only after a published receipt or terminal failure.
   Both unordered and BLOCK_RECORD sweeps use it for non-compound records.
   The preflight deliberately leaves INSERT/MINSERT, ATTRIB, SEQEND,
   POLYLINE, and VERTEX on the legacy value-lease route. That is temporary
   containment, not completed compound migration. The source-less publication
   boundary now emits no fabricated receipt when no HANDLE-map coverage is
   available.

The existing R1 wording below is retained as historical rationale. The
following subplan supersedes its implementation detail and is the only active
R1 work.

### R1 implementation subplan (rev 1215)

#### R1.1: introduce recoverable map leases

The primitive is complete and `readDwgObjects()` now uses it. Four focused
lease tests passed 64 assertions; the covered object-sweep publication,
object-failure, and lease selectors passed 71 assertions. The value-only lease
remains only at compound/entity/block call sites until R1.2 can retain a
detached parent or child safely.

1. `DwgFrameMapLease` is private and move-only: exact `objHandle` and source
   tuple, origin-map kind, coverage flag, and an optional C++17
   `unordered_map::node_type`. The existing `DwgSourceFrameLease` remains the
   borrowed view. No lease helper becomes public API.
2. `detachDwgSourceFrame`, `restoreDwgSourceFrame`,
   `deferDetachedDwgSourceFrame`, and `discardDetachedDwgSourceFrame` validate
   the map key, embedded handle, exact ledger tuple, allowed disposition, zero
   publication count, and mutual exclusion before mutation. Detaching does not
   update the ledger.
3. Restore retains its node on an unexpected source-key collision; detached
   deferral reserves its target before transfer and restores its node after a
   target collision or failed ledger transition. Deterministic collision tests
   replace a global allocation-failure hook. Multi-node paths must reserve
   before their first detach.
4. A terminal ledger update occurs only on defer, exact-source quarantine,
   failed parse, or successful receipt publication. A preflight rejection has
   no transition; the later explicit abandonment owns that transition.

#### R1.2: introduce truthful staged residency and one compound aggregate

The first mutation-hardening pass is complete: ATTRIB routing no longer uses
`operator[]` to create its initial pending or orphan receipt queue, reserves
both child vectors before appending, and removes a partially created orphan
companion on failure. The source-less validator retains legacy stale-SEQEND
cleanup while covered HANDLE-map state remains strict. The focused
deferred/INSERT/ATTRIB regressions passed 103 assertions in 10 cases. The
first staging primitive is also complete: `Staged` coverage now has exact
lease transition, rollback, finalization, and aggregate-custody tests; the
focused lease/deferred family passed 175 assertions in 13 cases. The aggregate
validator now rejects receiptless covered frames and coexistence with any
legacy parallel queue; EOF abandonment terminalizes every owned staged node
before clearing the aggregate. The parser queues still use the transitional
parallel maps, so aggregate ownership is not complete and the remaining steps
below stay active.

1. **Complete:** `Staged` is now present in `DRW_DwgFrameDisposition` with
   `CompoundStaged` evidence. `Pending -> Staged`, terminal
   `Staged -> Published|Quarantined|Failed`, and exact-node
   `Staged -> Pending` rollback are implemented and tested. A covered receipt
   now requires that exact detached node; a source-less parse cannot fabricate
   a receipt. Publication and finalization recognize `Staged`; `Deferred`
   still requires an `objObjectMap` resident source. The remaining aggregate
   call sites must use this state rather than marking a parked child
   `Deferred`.
2. **Foundation complete:** private move-only storage in `dwgReader` now has
   no public production container access, validates one node/receipt owner,
   and abandons owned nodes deterministically. It contains:
   - `DwgStagedFrame` owns an optional `DwgFrameMapLease` and, for a covered
     frame, its exact `DRW_DwgFramePublication`. A source-less direct parse has
     neither map node nor coverage receipt.
   - `StagedAttribState` owns `shared_ptr<DRW_Attrib>` and its
     `DwgStagedFrame` together.
   - `PendingInsertState` owns the parsed `DRW_Insert`, its parent staged
     frame, and its ordered `StagedAttribState` vector.
   - `OrphanAttribState` owns only the owner-handle key and ordered attributes.
   - `StagedSeqEndState` owns its parsed owner handle and staged frame, keyed
     by SEQEND handle until exactly one parent adopts it.
   The new maps are `m_pendingInsertStates`, `m_orphanAttribStates`, and
   `m_stagedSeqEnds`. Replace, then delete, all five receipt/entity parallel
   maps and the valid-SEQEND owner/receipt sets. Keep terminal invalid and
   consumed markers only where a later block/entity walk must distinguish a
   known completed or quarantined child from a missing one.
3. Add small private primitives with one responsibility each:
   `stageDetachedCompoundFrame`, `restoreStagedCompoundFrame`,
   `abandonStagedCompoundFrame`, `adoptOrphanAttributes`,
   `stageSeqEnd`, and `tryCommitPendingInsert`. Each reserves every destination
   map/vector before the first detach, validates source identity and cardinality
   before moving, then either owns all child nodes in one aggregate or restores
   every moved node through the exact `Staged -> Pending` rollback. A known
   malformed group instead terminally abandons its detached nodes without
   reinsertion. A failed insertion leaves the source lease local and restores
   it; an aggregate is never visible without its object and receipt together.
   Remove `consumeSeqEnd(..., borrowedLease)` rather than teaching a value
   lease to impersonate a detached node.
4. Stage the parent INSERT/MINSERT, ATTRIB, and SEQEND before changing their
   terminal ledger disposition. A SEQEND or ATTRIB reached first by the
   unordered sweep transfers its actual detached node into the appropriate
   aggregate. Parent arrival adopts orphan attributes by moving their complete
   states, then adopts only the declared SEQEND whose handle and parsed owner
   agree. Preserve R2004+ declared ATTRIB order and the validated R13--R2000
   chain order; reject duplicate handles, a missing/extra child, stale owner,
   receipt mismatch, or a source tuple mismatch before `addInsert()`.
5. Make compound commit explicit. Before the first callback, verify the parent,
   every ATTRIB, and optional SEQEND state and prebuild the ordered receipt list.
   Invoke `addInsert()`, then publish receipts in parent/ATTRIB/SEQEND order.
   After each successfully published receipt, mark that exact staged node
   published and discard it. An allocation/transfer failure before semantic
   rejection restores every staged node and its `Pending` row; a known malformed
   sequence terminally abandons every detached node once through exact-source
   quarantine or failure. On an interface exception, retain the already-
   published prefix, terminalize the remaining detached nodes without a second
   callback, and return a partial result. Only a successful terminal commit
   updates legacy next-link state and the completed-child marker.
6. Replace `validateDeferredCompoundState()` with a side-effect-free aggregate
   validator: every covered staged frame has exact ledger tuple, zero
   publication count, `Staged` disposition, and one aggregate owner; every
   source-less item has no fabricated receipt. It validates declared child sets
   and exact ordering without changing maps or markers. EOF abandonment walks
   a deterministic order of pending parents, their attributes, staged SEQENDs,
   and orphan groups; it restores only pre-commit nodes when the caller still
   owns recovery, otherwise quarantines exact covered sources or marks
   source-less children once. It must leave no detached lease to die silently.
7. Keep production state private. Replace direct test setup through
   `m_pendingInserts` and related maps with narrow `DwgEntityReaderProbe`
   builders/snapshots that construct a valid or deliberately malformed whole
   aggregate. Tests may inspect immutable snapshots, ledger rows, and map
   membership, but cannot manufacture a receipt-free half-state by default.

#### R1.3: give mapped entity parsing an explicit terminal result

1. **Partial:** a private mapped-frame ownership context now surrounds the existing
   callbackful `readDwgEntity` compatibility entry point. It receives a
   detached `DwgFrameMapLease`, transfers deferred OBJECTS exactly, and
   terminally discards non-compound simple frames. It does not yet transfer a
   compound node to the aggregate, so it uses a conservative type preflight to
   leave every compound record on the old route. Extend it with explicit
   `StagedCompound`, `RejectedBeforeCallback`, and `PartialCallbackFailure`
   results only when those routes can own all affected children. Do not
   describe the current
   dispatch as parse-only: ordinary cases still invoke business callbacks and
   receipts in `readDwgEntity`. Extract a pure typed/raw payload only after
   the context has removed every value-lease transfer from deferred-object and
   compound paths.
2. **Partial:** `readDwgEntities()` detaches and routes every non-compound
   `ObjectMap` node through the context. A deferred object moves by
   `deferDetachedDwgSourceFrame`; a simple published or rejected entity is
   discarded only after its terminal receipt/outcome. Preserve the current
   soft typed-body-failure policy and final EOF aggregate cleanup while adding
   compound staging.
3. **Partial:** both `walkBlockRecordEntities()` branches now do the same for
   non-compound records, preserving their
   existing legacy-link traversal, modern `entMap` order, recovery warnings,

   not reported as a missing frame by a later block walk. R1 does not move
   `addBlock()`/`endBlock()` timing; it only makes each child frame recoverable
   until the current callback policy reaches a terminal result.
4. Change `deferObject()` before the wrapper reaches any fixed/custom OBJECTS
   route: when a mapped context is active it must transfer that exact detached
   lease through `deferDetachedDwgSourceFrame`, not reconstitute a
   `DwgSourceFrameLease` after its source map was erased. Keep the source-less
   compatibility route only for direct callers and assert it never has an
   active mapped owner.
5. Tighten `DwgFrameMapLease`: `discardDetachedDwgSourceFrame` validates a real
   origin as well as identity; every caller must leave it empty by an explicit
   restore, defer, park, or discard. Put a debug-only no-throw scope guard in
   each mapped-frame owner so control-flow exit with a nonempty lease records
   an invariant failure before normal destruction; keep the lease destructor
   passive and never turn an allocation failure into process termination.

#### R1.4: convert sequence children after their owner can park leases

1. Replace `readPlineVertex()`'s `objHandle` child list and sequential `take`
   loop with a vector of real borrowed-then-detached leases plus typed vertex
   payloads. Parse all VERTEX and SEQEND frames while borrowed; reserve all
   vector/map capacity; detach every source; and restore every detached node if
   any later detach or pre-callback check fails. Do not insert a vertex,
   consume a handle, or update `nextEntLink` until that local transaction is
   accepted. Preserve R13--R2000 chain restoration and R2004+ `hadlesList`

2. Replace the legacy SEQEND cache/consume route with the R1.2 staged SEQEND
   primitive for both POLYLINE and INSERT. A staged terminator is a real node
   until receipt publication; a source-less direct parse remains a no-receipt
   compatibility path. There is no second parse and no reconstructed source

3. Delete the old value-lease use from normal entity, block, SEQEND, and
   POLYLINE paths once their mapped wrappers are live. Keep it only for
   read-only borrow compatibility until its remaining TABLES-specific callers
   are converted or removed. Re-audit all paired-map lookups, including block
   quarantine and raw-object deferral, for an explicit dual-residency failure.

#### R1.5: prove the transactional boundary on the fast target

1. Extend lease tests with a forced aggregate-map insertion failure, source and
   target collision, wrong origin, forged tuple, nonempty-destructor invariant,
   duplicate residency, staged-row publication rejection, and exact
   restore/ledger preservation. Assert both parser maps and the aggregate
   snapshot after every pre-callback failure.
2. Add covered and source-less compound cases for ATTRIB-before-INSERT,
   SEQEND-before-parent, two ATTRIBs, stale owner, duplicate child, orphan
   receipt-only, failed orphan adoption, delayed SEQEND, and callback throws at
   `addInsert` and at each receipt position. Malformed inputs must emit no
   business callback or receipt; callback tests assert only the externally
   observed prefix and a final partial report.
3. Add POLYLINE cases that fail after the first child detached, at the final

4. After each compile-affecting wave, build only
